9A60.02.title: Allergic conjunctivitis
9A60.02.definition: Allergic conjunctivitis is an IgE-mediated response due to the exposure of seasonal or perennial allergens in sensitized patients. The allergen-induced inflammatory response of the conjunctiva results in the release of histamine and other mediators. Symptoms consist of redness (mainly due to vasodilation of the peripheral small blood vessels), oedema (swelling) of the conjunctiva, itching, and increased lacrimation (production of tears).
synonyms: Allergic conjunctivitis due to drugs or medicaments

9A60.2.title: Cicatrizing conjunctivitis
synonyms: Chronic cicatrizing conjunctivitis, ocular cicatricial pemphigoid

9A60.01.title: Acute atopic conjunctivitis
9A60.01.definition: This is the allergic inflammation of the conjunctiva (mucous membrane that covers the posterior surface of the eyelids and the anterior pericorneal surface of the eyeball) of the immediate type, due to airborne allergens such as pollens, dusts, spores, and animal hair.

9A60.5.title: Vernal keratoconjunctivitis
9A60.5.definition: Vernal keratoconjunctivitis is a persistent and severe form of ocular allergy that affects children and young adults, usually in warm climates. Vernal keratoconjunctivitis typically appears in boys between the ages of 4–12 years. The typical symptoms are intense itching, tearing, and photophobia. Disease exacerbation can be triggered either by allergen re-exposure or by nonspecific stimuli such as sunlight, wind, and dust. The tarsal form is characterised by irregularly sized hypertrophic papillae, leading to a cobblestone appearance of the upper tarsal plate. The limbal form is characterised by transient, multiple limbal, or conjunctival gelatinous yellow-grey infiltrates superposed with white points or deposits, known as Horner–Trantas dots and papillae at the limbus.

9A61.3.title: Conjunctival scars
9A61.3.definition: These are cicatrices of the mucous membrane that lines the inner surface of the eyelid and the exposed surface of the eyeball that occur due to various reasons such as trauma, infection or allergy.

9A61.5.title: Conjunctival or subconjunctival haemorrhage
9A61.5.definition: A conjunctival haemorrhage is a small haematoma clearly delimited on the conjunctiva itself resulting from a direct blow on the eye. Subconjunctival haemorrhage extends from the orbit, forward and deep to the conjunctiva with no posterior limit.

9A61.4Y.title: Other specified conjunctival vascular disorders
synonyms: Conjunctival vascular disorders, other local vascular disorders

9A61.6.title: Conjunctival or subconjunctival degenerations or deposits
9A61.6.definition: These are the conjunctival/subconjunctival accumulation of some materials and gradual deterioration with impairment or loss of function, caused by injury, disease, or aging.
synonyms: Conjunctival or subconjunctival degenerations or deposits

9A62.title: Mucous membrane pemphigoid with ocular involvement
9A62.definition: Mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) involving the conjunctivae is also known as ocular pemphigoid. This may be confined to the conjunctivae or may be associated with involvement of other sites as well. Its importance lies in its potential to cause loss of vision and it may thus warrant more aggressive therapy than would be considered for MMP of other sites.
synonyms: Mucous membrane pemphigoid with ocular involvement

9A73.definition: This is an exposure condition in which the eye's cornea, the front part of the eye, becomes inflamed. The condition is often marked by moderate to intense pain and usually involves impaired eyesight. May cause feelings of scratching each time individual blinks eye.

9A77.1.title: Adherent leukoma
9A77.1.definition: This is a white tumour of the cornea enclosing a prolapsed adherent iris.

9A76.title: Corneal ulcer
9A76.definition: Loss of epithelial tissue from the surface of the cornea due to progressive erosion and necrosis of the tissue. It is often caused by bacterial, fungal, or viral infection.

9A78.20.title: Bullous keratopathy
9A78.20.definition:
This is the maximum stage of corneal oedema.

It is a pathological condition in which small vesicles, or bullae, are formed in the cornea due to endothelial dysfunction. In a healthy cornea, endothelial cells keep the tissue from excess fluid absorption, pumping it back into the aqueous humour. When affected by some reason, such as Fuchs' dystrophy or a trauma during cataract removal, endothelial cells suffer mortality or damage. The corneal endothelial cells normally do not undergo mitotic cell division, and cell loss results in permanent loss of function.

9A78.21.title: Secondary corneal oedema
synonyms: Corneal oedema due to contact lens
Corneal oedema secondary to contact lens

9A78.50.title: Keratoconus
9A78.50.definition: Keratoconus is a noninflammatory, often bilateral, corneal dystrophy characterised by progressive cone-shaped bulging and thinning of the cornea.

9A78.3.title: Changes in corneal membranes
synonyms: Folds or rupture in Bowman's membrane

9A78.6.title: Anaesthesia of cornea
9A78.6.definition: This is the condition of having sensation (including the feeling of pain) blocked or temporarily taken away, of the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

9A78.7.title: Hypoesthesia of cornea
9A78.7.definition: This refers to a reduced sense of touch or sensation, or a partial loss of sensitivity to sensory stimuli, of the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

9A90.1.definition: This refers to the change of tissue to a lower or less functionally active form, of the thin, circular structure in the eye, responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil and thus the amount of light reaching the retina. 9A93.definition: This refers to adhesions and disruptions of the thin, circular structure in the eye, responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil and thus the amount of light reaching the retina. The colour of the iris is often referred to as "eye colour." It is also of the circumferential tissue inside the eye composed of the ciliary muscle and ciliary processes. 9A94.1.title: Floppy iris syndrome

9B10.21.title: Diabetic cataract
9B10.21.definition: This refers to an unspecified group of metabolic diseases in which a person has high blood sugar, either because the pancreas does not produce enough insulin, or because cells do not respond to the insulin that is produced. This diagnosis is with diabetic cataract.

9B10.02.title: Mature age-related cataract
9B10.02.definition: This is a mature age-related clouding of the lens inside the eye which leads to a decrease in vision. It is the most common cause of blindness and is conventionally treated with surgery. Visual loss occurs because opacification of the lens obstructs light from passing and being focused on to the retina at the back of the eye.

9B10.1Y.title: Other specified infantile or juvenile cataract
synonyms: Other specified infantile or juvenile cataract
Infantile or juvenile cortical, lamellar, or zonular cataract
Anterior subcapsular polar infantile or juvenile cataract
Posterior subcapsular polar infantile or juvenile cataract

9B10.20.title: Traumatic cataract
9B10.20.definition: Partial or complete opacity on or in the lens or capsule of one or both eyes, impairing vision or causing blindness. The many kinds of cataract are classified by their morphology (size, shape, location) or etiology (cause and time of occurrence) resulting from or following injury.
synonyms: Cataract associated with radiation or other physical influences

9B10.22.title: After-cataract
9B10.22.definition: This is a clouding of the lens of the eye, which impedes the passage of light resulting from disease, degeneration, or from surgery.

9B10.2Y.title: Other specified cataracts
synonyms: Cataract associated with other general disorders
Cataract due to ocular inflammatory disorders
Cataract secondary to ocular inflammatory disorders
Cataract due to ocular degenerative disorders

synonyms: Other specified disorders of the eyeball - anterior segment

9B51.title: Scleritis
9B51.definition: Inflammation of the white, opaque, fibrous, outer tunic of the eyeball. Can be associated with uveitis.

9B62.title: Chorioretinal scars
synonyms: Macula scars of posterior pole, post traumatic
Macula scars of posterior pole, postinflammatory

9B50.title: Episcleritis
9B50.definition: Episcleritis is a benign, self-limiting inflammatory disease affecting part of the eye called the episclera. The episclera is a thin layer of tissue that lies between the conjunctiva and the connective tissue layer that forms the white of the eye (sclera). Episcleritis is a common condition, and is characterised by the abrupt onset of mild eye pain and redness.

9B65.0.title: Noninfectious posterior choroiditis
synonyms: Posterior uveitis due to Vogt Koyanagi Harada syndrome
Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
Acute idiopathic enlarged blind spot syndrome

9B66.0.title: Noninfectious intermediate choroiditis
9B66.0.definition: This is a non-infectious form of uveitis localised to the vitreous and peripheral retina. Primary sites of inflammation include the vitreous of which other such entities as pars planitis, posterior cyclitis, and hyalitis are encompassed. Intermediate uveitis may either be an isolated eye disease or associated with the development of a systemic disease such as multiple sclerosis or sarcoidosis.

9B66.1.title: Infectious intermediate choroiditis
9B66.1.definition: This is a infectious form of uveitis localised to the vitreous and peripheral retina. Primary sites of inflammation include the vitreous of which other such entities as pars planitis, posterior cyclitis, and hyalitis are encompassed. Intermediate uveitis may either be an isolated eye disease or associated with the development of a systemic disease such as multiple sclerosis or sarcoidosis.
synonyms: Infectious intermediate uveitis in Lyme disease

9B6Y.title: Other specified disorders of the choroid
synonyms: Other specified disorders of the choroid

9B71.2.title: Radiation retinopathy
9B71.2.definition: Radiation retinopathy is damage to retina due to exposure to ionizing radiation. Radiation retinopathy has a delayed onset, typically after months or years of radiation, and is slowly progressive. In general, radiation retinopathy is seen around 18 months after treatment with external-beam radiation and with brachytherapy.

9B71.01.title: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy
9B71.01.definition:
This is proliferative retinopathy (damage to the retina) caused by complications of diabetes, which can eventually lead to blindness. It is an ocular manifestation of diabetes, a systemic disease, which affects up to 80 percent of all patients who have had diabetes for 10 years or more.


Always assign an additional code for the type of diabetes mellitus.
synonyms: Diabetes mellitus, independent of type with proliferative retinopathy
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with vitreous haemorrhage
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with tractional retinal detachment, macula not involved
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with tractional retinal detachment, macula involved
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with combined rhegmatogenous and tractional retinal detachment

9B71.00.title: Nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy
synonyms: Diabetes mellitus, independent of type with preproliferative retinopathy
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with preproliferative retinopathy

9B71.3.title: Retinopathy of prematurity
9B71.3.definition: Retinopathy of prematurity is a vasoproliferative disorder that affects extremely premature infants potentially leading to severe visual impairment or blindness. Exposure of newborn premature infants to hyperoxia down regulates retinal vascular endothelial growth factor. Blood vessels constrict and can become obliterated, resulting in delays of normal retinal vascular development. Low birth weight, young gestational age, and severity of illness (e.g. respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, sepsis) are associated factors. It primarily occurs in extremely low birth weight infants because of the cessation of normal retinal vascular maturation.

9B71.1.title: Hypertensive retinopathy
synonyms: Hypertensive Retinopathy, Stage 1, mild arteriolar narrowing, broadening of arteriolar light reflex

Hypertensive Retinopathy, Stage 4, Signs of stage 3 retinopathy plus swelling of the optic disk

9B72.00.title: Cytomegaloviral retinitis
9B72.00.definition: This is an inflammation of the eye's retina that can lead to blindness. This is a DNA virus in the family Herpesviridae known for producing large cells with nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions. Such inclusions are called an "owl's eye" effect.

9B71.5.title: Autoimmune retinopathy
9B71.5.definition:
Autoimmune retinopathies are immune-mediated inflammatory disorders of the retina that differ from paraneoplastic retinopathies in the lack of association with cancer. Patients present with progressive visual loss and dysfunction of rods (impaired dark adaption and peripheral vision problems) and cones (visual acuity, colour dysfunction, photosensitivity and glare) may occur. The symptoms are often worse than the clinical signs on fundoscopy. Multiple anti-retinal autoantibodies (e.g. anti-recoverin antibodies) are described although their significance is uncertain. Autoimmune retinopathy is a diagnosis of exclusion and other causes of retinopathy need to be ruled out, while the potential role of immunotherapy remains uncertain. 
Associated neural autoantibodies include:
anti-recoverin autoantibodies; alpha-enolase autoantibodies; anti-transducin autoantibodies.

9B73.11.title: Juvenile retinoschisis
9B73.11.definition: X-linked retinoschisis is a genetic ocular disease that is characterised by reduced visual acuity in males due to juvenile macular degeneration.

9B73.3.title: Serous retinal detachment
9B73.3.definition: This occurs due to inflammation, injury or vascular abnormalities that results in fluid accumulating underneath the retina without the presence of a hole, tear, or break.

9B73.2.definition: A retinal cyst is a closed sac, having a distinct membrane and division compared to the nearby tissue in retina that can either be congenital or acquired.

9B75.2.title: Central serous chorioretinopathy
9B75.2.definition: This is an eye disease which causes visual impairment, often temporary, usually in one eye. When the disorder is active it is characterised by leakage of fluid under the retina that has a propensity to accumulate under the central macula.

9B75.0Y.title: Other specified age-related macular degeneration

9B78.0.title: Retinal vasculopathy and cerebral leukodystrophy
9B78.0.definition: Retinal vasculopathy and cerebral leukodystrophy is an inherited group of small vessel diseases comprised of cerebroretinal vasculopathy, hereditary vascular retinopathy and hereditary endotheliopathy with retinopathy, nephropathy and stroke (HERNS); all exhibiting progressive visual impairment as well as variable cerebral dysfunction.

9B77.title: Eales disease
9B77.definition: Eales disease is a retinal vasculopathy that presents as an inflammatory stage with retinal periphlebitis affecting especially peripheral retina, then an ischemic stage with sclerosis of retinal veins, and finally a proliferative stage characterised by neovascularization, haemorrhage and retinal detachment.

9B78.61.title: Haemorrhagic detachment of retinal pigment epithelium
9B78.61.definition: This refers to the haemorrhagic detachment of the pigmented cell layer just outside the neurosensory retina that nourishes retinal visual cells, and is firmly attached to the underlying choroid and overlying retinal visual cells.
synonyms: Haemorrhagic detachment of retinal pigment epithelium

9B8Z.title: Disorders of the vitreous body, unspecified

9C20.2.title: Purulent endophthalmitis
9C20.2.definition: Suppurative inflammation of the tissues of the internal structures of the eye; often caused by fungi, necrosis of intraocular tumours, or retained intraocular foreign bodies. Other aetiology can be any infectious uveitis.

9B78.60.title: Serous detachment of retinal pigment epithelium
9B78.60.definition: This refers to the serous detachment of the pigmented cell layer just outside the neurosensory retina that nourishes retinal visual cells, and is firmly attached to the underlying choroid and overlying retinal visual cells.
synonyms: Serous detachment of retinal pigment epithelium

9B78.9.title: Retinal atrophy
9B78.9.definition: This is a group of genetic diseases and is characterised by the bilateral degeneration of the retina, causing progressive vision loss culminating in blindness.

9C40.40.definition: This refers to anterior ischemic damage to the optic nerve due to any cause. Damage and death of these nerve cells, or neurons, leads to characteristic features of optic neuropathy.

9C61.11.title: Primary angle-closure
9C61.11.definition: Primary angle closure is a condition defined by the presence of iridotrabecular contact with elevated intraocular pressure or peripheral anterior synechiae but no signs of optic nerve damage.

9C61.0Y.title: Other specified primary open-angle glaucoma
synonyms: Primary capsular glaucoma with pseudoexfoliation of lens

9C61.01.title: Ocular hypertension
9C61.01.definition: Ocular hypertension is a condition of elevated intraocular pressure in the absence of optic nerve, nerve fibre layer or visual field abnormalities.

9C61.13.title: Primary angle closure without pupillary block
9C61.13.definition: Primary angle closure without pupillary block is a condition described as anatomical variation in the iris root in which narrowing of the anterior chamber angle occurs independent of pupillary block causing angle closure.
synonyms: Primary angle closure without pupillary block

9C61.17.title: Condition after acute angle-closure glaucoma attack
9C61.17.definition: Condition after acute angle closure glaucoma attack refers to a condition after a previous episode of acute angle-closure attack, usually with secondary alterations of the iris (sphincter lesions) and lens (“Glaukomflecken”, cataract).
synonyms: Condition after acute angle-closure glaucoma attack

9C61.1Y.title: Other specified primary angle closure and angle closure glaucoma
synonyms: Other specified primary angle closure and angle closure glaucoma

9C61.12.title: Primary angle closure glaucoma
9C61.12.definition: Primary angle closure glaucoma is a condition described as angle closure or/and peripheral anterior synechiae with elevated intraocular pressure and evidence of optic nerve damage.

9C61.10.title: Primary angle closure suspect or anatomical narrow angle
9C61.10.definition: Primary angle closure glaucoma suspect is a condition of narrow anterior chamber angle, suspicious for future closure, with no signs of trabecular meshwork or optic nerve damage.
synonyms: Primary angle closure suspect or anatomical narrow angle

9C61.00.title: Normal tension glaucoma
9C61.00.definition: Normal tension glaucoma is a condition considered to be within the continuum of primary open-angle glaucoma; the term is used when intraocular pressure is within the statistically normal range (10-21 mmHg).

9C61.15.title: Intermittent angle-closure
9C61.15.definition: Intermittent Angle Closure is a milder clinical manifestation of acute angle closure that resolves spontaneously.

9C61.1Z.title: Primary angle closure and angle closure glaucoma, unspecified
synonyms: Primary angle closure and angle closure glaucoma, unspecified
Primary angle closure and angle closure glaucoma

9C61.14.title: Acute angle closure with pupillary block
9C61.14.definition: Acute Angle Closure (AAC) with pupillary block is a condition described as circumferential iris apposition to the trabecular meshwork with rapid and excessive increase in intraocular pressure that does not resolve spontaneously.
synonyms: Acute angle closure with pupillary block

9C60.title: Glaucoma suspect
synonyms: narrow angle anterior chamber glaucoma suspect
Open angle with borderline intraocular pressure glaucoma suspect

9C61.20.title: Pseudoexfoliative open-angle glaucoma
9C61.20.definition: Pseudoexfoliative Open-Angle glaucoma is a condition where fibrillar pseudoexfoliative material is produced by various ocular tissues and is deposited on the trabecular meshwork, lens, and other structures of the anterior segment leading to intraocular pressure elevation and subsequent optic nerve damage.
synonyms: residual stage capsular glaucoma with pseudoexfoliation of lens

9C61.23.title: Glaucoma associated with intraocular haemorrhage
9C61.23.definition: Ghost cell glaucoma is a condition where bleeding into the vitreous body or anterior chamber can lead to intraocular pressure elevation when stiffer red blood cells that have lost their haemoglobin obstruct the trabecular meshwork.

9C61.2C.title: Secondary glaucoma due to extra-ocular mass
synonyms: Secondary glaucoma due to extra-ocular mass

9C61.16.title: Chronic angle-closure
9C61.16.definition: Chronic angle closure is a condition when intraocular pressure elevation is due to variable portions of anterior chamber angle being permanently closed by peripheral anterior synechiae.

9C61.25.title: Glaucomato-cyclitic crisis
9C61.25.definition: A glaucomato-cyclitic crisis presents with mild keratic precipitates and aqueous flare, acute intraocular pressure elevation and optic nerve damage when repeated attacks occur.

9C61.30.title: Secondary angle closure glaucoma with pupillary block
9C61.30.definition: Secondary angle closure glaucoma with pupillary block is a condition where an anteriorly subluxated lens occludes the pupil causing acute secondary angle closure and intraocular pressure elevation.
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma with pupillary block

9C61.21.title: Pigmentary open-angle glaucoma
9C61.21.definition: Pigmentary open-angle glaucoma is a condition where pigment is liberated due to rubbing of the zonules against the posterior iris sheath that leads to obstruction of the trabecular meshwork causing intraocular pressure elevation and subsequent optic nerve damage.

9C61.24.title: Glaucoma due to eye inflammation
synonyms: Uveal effusion with ocular hypertension due to Inflammation

9C61.33.title: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to endothelial overgrowth
9C61.33.definition: Secondary angle-closure glaucoma due to endothelial overgrowth is a condition where corneal endothelial cells overgrow the trabecular meshwork and iris, closing the angle by tissue contraction leading to intraocular pressure elevation and subsequent optic nerve damage.
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to endothelial overgrowth

9C61.2B.title: Glaucoma caused by increased episcleral venous pressure
synonyms: Glaucoma caused by increased episcleral venous pressure

9C61.31.title: Secondary angle closure glaucoma without pupillary block
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma without pupillary block

9C61.35.title: Ciliary block glaucoma
9C61.35.definition: Ciliary block glaucoma is a condition where aqueous misdirection into the vitreous cavity displaces the lens-iris diaphragm anteriorly thus causing angle closure with subsequent intraocular pressure elevation and optic nerve damage.

9C61.26.title: Secondary open-angle glaucoma due to parasitic eye disease
synonyms: Secondary open-angle glaucoma due to parasitic eye disease

9C61.34.title: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to epithelial ingrowth
9C61.34.definition: Epithelial ingrowth is a condition after open globe trauma or surgery where conjunctival or corneal epithelial cells get access to the anterior chamber and overgrow the trabecular meshwork with subsequent intraocular pressure elevation and optic nerve damage.
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to epithelial ingrowth

9C61.32.title: Neovascular secondary angle closure glaucoma
9C61.32.definition: Neovascular secondary angle-closure glaucoma is a frequent condition where neovascular membranes occlude and close the chamber angle by fibrovascular contraction leading to intraocular pressure elevation and subsequent optic nerve damage. Neovascularization can be due to retinal venous occlusion, diabetic retinopathy, ocular ischemia, long-standing retinal detachment and other ischemic conditions of the eye.
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma by neovascular membrane due to diabetic retinopathy
Secondary angle closure glaucoma by neovascular membrane, without pupillary block, due to diabetic retinopathy
Glaucoma due to retinopathy of prematurity

Decompensation in far distance – type divergens excess

9C61.41.title: Primary infantile glaucoma
9C61.41.definition: Primary infantile glaucoma is a condition after 2 years of age where malformation of the trabecular meshwork causes elevated intraocular pressure without enlargement of the eyeball but damage to the optic nerve similar to congenital glaucoma.

9C81.0Y.title: Other specified third nerve palsy
synonyms: Oculomotor nerve palsy with cyclic spasm
Oculomotor nerve palsy associated with other neurologic signs

9C80.2.title: Vertical or torsional strabismus
9C80.2.definition: An abnormal binocular alignment which may be constant or intermittent, that is not horizontal, but vertical or torsional (rotational) around the pupillary axis.

9C61.3Y.title: Other specified secondary angle closure glaucoma
synonyms: Other specified secondary angle closure glaucoma
Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to uveitis

9C80.5.title: Mechanical strabismus
9C80.5.definition: An abnormal binocular alignment caused by abnormalities of ocular movement in one or both eyes caused by damage to the extraocular muscles and/or other orbital structures. Mechanical strabismus is characterised by limitation of movements in one or more directions and variable strabismus.
synonyms: Mechanical strabismus from orbital pulley disorder
Mechanical strabismus from local anaesthetic myotoxicity
Mechanical strabismus due to thyroid eye disease
Traumatic limitation of duction of eye muscle

9C80.1.title: Exotropia
9C80.1.definition: Exotropia is an abnormal binocular alignment in which one of the eyes has an outward deviation. Fixation can be alternatiing or monocular. Exotropia is present in all distances.

9C61.36.title: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to other anterior displacement of the lens-iris diaphragm
9C61.36.definition: Iris and ciliary body cysts, intraocular tumours, posterior scleritis, uveal effusion, or Silicon Oil or gas in the vitreous cavity can cause IOP elevation by angle closure.
synonyms: Secondary angle closure glaucoma due to other anterior displacement of the lens-iris diaphragm
Silicon oil or gas in the vitreous cavity causing IOP elevation

9C61.40.title: Primary congenital glaucoma
9C61.40.definition: Primary Congenital Glaucoma is a condition during early infancy where delayed development and malformation of the trabecular meshwork blocks the outflow routes leading to elevated intraocular pressure that causes enlargement of the eyeball (Buphthalmus), corneal oedema, Descemet tears, myopia, and damage to the optic nerve, often resulting in severe visual impairment or blindness

9C81.2.title: Sixth nerve palsy
synonyms: disease or disorder of abducent nerve
Abducens nerve palsy associated with other neurologic signs

9C80.0.title: Esotropia
9C80.0.definition: Esotropia is an abnormal binocular alignment in which one of the eyes has an inward deviation. Fixation can be alternating or monocular. Esotropia is present in all distances. Squint angles can vary with distances.

9C81.00.title: External bilateral paralysis of oculomotor nerve
synonyms: External bilateral paralysis of oculomotor nerve

9C81.1.title: Fourth nerve palsy
synonyms: Chronic trochlear nerve palsy, spread of comitance

9C80.4.title: Heterophoria
9C80.4.definition: A temporary deviation of the eyes from normal binocular alignment when there is disruption of the visual input from one eye. The alignment is normal when there is binocular visual input.

9C82.0.title: Progressive external ophthalmoplegia
9C82.0.definition: Chronic ophthalmoplegia is characterised by progressive weakness of ocular muscles and levator muscle of the upper eyelid. The condition is mainly manifested in adults. It may be totally and permanently isolated, however in a minority of cases it is associated with skeletal myopathy, which causes abnormal fatigability and even permanent muscle weakness. In this case the affection is still termed isolated progressive external ophthalmoplegia. A large proportion of chronic ophthalmoplegias presents with multisystemic pattern of signs: neurological signs (hearing loss, retinopathy, cerebellar disorders, peripheral neuropathy, etc.), endocrine (diabetes, hypogonadism, hypoparathyroidism, etc.), kidney (kidney failure, tubulopathy, etc.), and heart disorders (conduction disorders, myocardiopathy, etc.).
synonyms: Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, autosomal dominant, type 1
PEOA1 - [Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, autosomal dominant, type 1]
Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, autosomal dominant, type 2
Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, autosomal dominant, type 3

9C81.Y.title: Palsy of other specified ocular motor nerve
synonyms: Palsy of other specified ocular motor nerve

9C82.1.title: Muscular dystrophy affecting extraocular muscle
9C82.1.definition: Non-specific term that is used to describe a range of primary myopathies that affect the extraocular muscles.

9C83.02.title: Monocular elevator palsy
9C83.02.definition: Monocular elevator palsy is an incomplete or absent movement of one eye in upgaze. May be due to pathology in the orbit, as well as infranuclear, internuclear, or supranuclear in origin.

9C82.4.title: Oculomotor apraxia

synonyms: Other specified disorders of extraocular muscles

paralysis of extrinsic muscle of eye
paralysis of rectus muscle of eye

9C83.00.title: Horizontal gaze palsy
9C83.00.definition: A palsy of horizontal gaze is an incomplete or absent movement of the two eyes in a horizontal direction of gaze. May be in one or both directions
synonyms: Congenital horizontal gaze palsies associated with other neurological signs
Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis
HGPPS - [Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis]
Lesions of the paramedian pontine reticular formation
Acquired horizontal gaze palsies associated with other neurological signs

9C81.Z.title: Palsy of unspecified ocular motor nerve

9C83.11.title: Upward gaze deviation
synonyms: Paroxysmal tonic upgaze of childhood with ataxia

9C83.0Y.title: Other specified palsy of conjugate gaze
synonyms: Other specified palsy of conjugate gaze

9C83.1Y.title: Other specified spasm of conjugate gaze
synonyms: Other specified spasm of conjugate gaze

9C83.65.title: Ocular tilt reaction
9C83.65.definition: skew deviation associated with ocular torsion (cyclodeviation) and a head tilt (ear to shoulder)

9C83.63.title: Synergistic divergence
9C83.63.definition:
Anomalous innervation of muscle normally supplied by the oculomotor nerve.
In congenital unilateral adduction palsy, when adduction is attempted, the affected eye abducts rather than adducts.

9C83.01.title: Vertical gaze palsy
9C83.01.definition: A palsy of vertical gaze is an incomplete or absent movement of the two eyes in the vertical direction of gaze.
synonyms: Paralysis of combined upgaze and downgaze

9C83.5.title: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia
9C83.5.definition: This is a disorder of conjugate lateral gaze in which the affected eye shows impairment of adduction.

9C83.10.title: Horizontal conjugate gaze deviation
synonyms: Sustained horizontal conjugate gaze deviation, ipsilateral type
Sustained horizontal conjugate gaze deviation, contralateral type
Sustained tonic horizontal conjugate gaze deviation

9C83.13.title: Oculogyric crisis
9C83.13.definition: Episodic spells of tonic upward and sometimes lateral deviation of the eyes, rarely downward.

9C83.Y.title: Other specified disorders of binocular movement
synonyms: Other specified disorders of binocular movement

9C83.6Y.title: Other specified anomalies of divergence or deviation of eye movement
synonyms: Other specified anomalies of divergence or deviation of eye movement

9C83.6Z.title: Anomalies of divergence or deviation of eye movement, unspecified
synonyms: Anomalies of divergence or deviation of eye movement, unspecified
Anomalies of divergence or deviation of eye movement

9C83.64.title: Skew deviation
9C83.64.definition: a vertical misalignment of the visual axes caused by a disturbance of prenuclear inputs

9C84.5Y.title: Other specified nystagmus occurring in visual system disorders
synonyms: Other specified nystagmus occurring in visual system disorders
Vertical jerk nystagmus with convergent-divergent horizontal component

9C84.5Z.title: Nystagmus occurring in visual system disorders, unspecified
synonyms: Nystagmus occurring in visual system disorders, unspecified
Nystagmus occurring in visual system disorders

9C85.0Y.title: Other specified anomalies of saccadic eye movements
synonyms: Other specified anomalies of saccadic eye movements

9C8Z.title: Strabismus or ocular motility disorders, unspecified
synonyms: Strabismus or ocular motility disorders, unspecified

9C85.0Z.title: Anomalies of saccadic eye movements, unspecified
synonyms: Anomalies of saccadic eye movements, unspecified

9C85.Y.title: Other specified irregular eye movements
synonyms: Spontaneous eye movement in unconscious patients

9D00.0.title: Myopia
9D00.0.definition: A refractive error in which rays of light entering the eye parallel to the optic axis are brought to a focus in front of the retina when ocular accommodation is relaxed. This usually results from the eyeball being too long from front to back, but can be caused by an overly curved cornea, a lens with increased optical power, or both. It is also called nearsightedness.

9D00.1.title: Hypermetropia
9D00.1.definition: A refractive error in which rays of light entering the eye parallel to the optic axis are brought to a focus behind the retina, as a result of the eyeball being too short from front to back. It is also called farsightedness because the near point is more distant than it is in emmetropia with an equal amplitude of accommodation.

9C8Y.title: Other specified strabismus or ocular motility disorders
synonyms: Other specified strabismus or ocular motility disorders
Ocular muscle contracture, not elsewhere specified

9D00.3.title: Presbyopia
9D00.3.definition: The normal decreasing elasticity of the crystalline lens that leads to loss of accommodation.

9D00.2.title: Astigmatism
9D00.2.definition: Unequal curvature of the refractive surfaces of the eye. Thus a point source of light cannot be brought to a point focus on the retina but is spread over a more or less diffuse area. This results from the radius of curvature in one plane being longer or shorter than the radius at right angles to it.

9D42.70.title: Bi-nasal defects heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Bi-nasal defects heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D42.22.title: Nasal step
9D42.22.definition: A nasal step is a discontinuity of the nasal field limit at the horizontal meridian. It is typical for glaucoma.

9D20.title: Bullous aphakic keratopathy following cataract surgery
synonyms: Bullous aphakic keratopathy following cataract surgery

9D42.60.title: Right hemi-field homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Right hemi-field homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D42.7Z.title: Heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia, unspecified
synonyms: Heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia, unspecified

9D23.title: Conjunctival blebitis after glaucoma surgery
synonyms: inflammation or infection of postprocedural bleb
Inflammation or infection of postprocedural bleb, stage 1
Inflammation or infection of postprocedural bleb, stage 2
Inflammation or infection of postprocedural bleb, stage 3

9D24.title: Complications with glaucoma drainage devices
synonyms: Dislodged plate or tube after glaucoma surgery
Ectopic plate or tubes after glaucoma surgery

9D42.6Z.title: Homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia, unspecified
synonyms: Homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia, unspecified

9D42.24.title: Isolated peripheral scotoma
9D42.24.definition: Isolated scotomas may be the result of scarring from infections or surgery.

9D42.5.title: Para-central scotoma
9D42.5.definition: A para-central scotoma is a scotoma adjacent to the fovea. Both may minimally affect letter chart acuity, but may interfere significantly with reading and other activities.

9D42.4.title: Central scotoma
9D42.4.definition: A central scotoma is a defect that covers the fovea. It therefore causes visual acuity loss and may necessitate eccentric fixation.

9D42.61.title: Left hemi-field homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Left hemi-field homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D42.3.title: Hemianopic or quadrantic loss
9D42.3.definition: Defects that cover a hemi-field or a quadrant in one eye may be the result of optic nerve involvement.

9D42.23.title: Ring scotoma
9D42.23.definition: A ring scotoma is a scotoma that surrounds the central field. Initially, it may consist of several smaller scotomas that gradually coalesce.

9D0Z.title: Disorders of refraction or accommodation, unspecified
synonyms: Disorders of refraction or accommodation, unspecified

9D21.title: Cataract lens fragments in eye following cataract surgery
synonyms: Cataract lens fragments in eye following cataract surgery

9D42.21.title: Arcuate scotoma
9D42.21.definition: A Bjerrum or arcuate scotoma follows the pattern of the retinal nerve fibres. It is typical for glaucomatous defects and can also be caused by juxta-papillary lesions.

9D41.title: Impairment of visual field
9D41.definition: Ranges of visual field impairment refer to the extent of peripheral vision outside fixation. The extent should be measured for each eye separately.

9D25.title: Glaucoma due to ocular surgery or laser
synonyms: Glaucoma due to ocular surgery or laser

9D42.Z.title: Patterns of visual field impairment, unspecified
synonyms: Patterns of visual field impairment, unspecified

9D22.title: Chorioretinal scars after surgery for detachment
synonyms: Chorioretinal scars after surgery for detachment

9D0Y.title: Other specified disorders of refraction or accommodation
synonyms: Other specified disorders of refraction or accommodation

9D42.6Y.title: Other specified homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Other specified homonymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D42.Y.title: Other specified patterns of visual field impairment
synonyms: Other specified patterns of visual field impairment

9D42.71.title: Bi-temporal defects heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Bi-temporal defects heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D46.title: Impairment of binocular functions
synonyms: Impairment of stereopsis, degree not specified
Impairment of fusion, degree not specified
Certain specified disorders of binocular vision

9D43.title: Impairment of contrast vision
9D43.definition:
Contrast sensitivity refers to the ability to distinguish small differences in brightness between adjacent surfaces.

Peak Contrast sensitivity refers to the smallest differences that are discernible for large stimuli.

For smaller objects, such as those involved in many Activities of Daily Living, contrast sensitivity interacts with visual acuity and visual field. Better contrast makes smaller details visible. The visual field is larger for stronger stimuli.

9D53.title: Entoptic phenomena
9D53.definition: Entoptic phenomena are visual phenomena caused by changes within the eye.
synonyms: Visual distortions of shape and size

9D42.7Y.title: Other specified heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia
synonyms: Other specified heteronymous hemianopia or quadrant anopia

9D7Y.title: Other specified impairment of visual functions
synonyms: Other specified impairment of visual functions

9D44.title: Impairment of colour vision
9D44.definition: Colour vision refers to the ability to distinguish colour differences. True colour “blindness” is extremely rare. Most colour vision deficiencies are minor, and congenital, with X-linked recessive inheritance (more prevalent among men). Some drugs and optic neuritis may also cause colour vision deficiencies.

9D93.title: Complex vision-related dysfunctions
9D93.definition: Complex Vision-Related Dysfunctions involve interactions with other sensory and motor systems. They reflect the combined effects at all stages of processing.
synonyms: Moderate limitation in orientation or mobility
Profound limitation in orientation or mobility

9D54.title: Visual illusions
9D54.definition: Visual illusions refer to percepts based on an erroneous interpretation of visual input.

9D90.1.title: Mild vision impairment
synonyms: visual impairment category 1, in both eyes
visual impairment category 9 in both eyes

9D51.title: Transient visual loss
synonyms: Transient vision loss, type not specified

9D90.7.title: Near vision impairment
9D90.7.definition: Near vision refers to the ability to perform tasks that require detailed vision at a close distance. It should be measured with both eyes open at the subject’s preferred viewing distance and with the subject’s habitual near vision correction (if any). Near vision impairment is characterised by a presenting near visual acuity worse than N6.

9D90.3.title: Severe vision impairment
synonyms: blindness, one eye, low vision other eye
visual impairment category 3 in one eye, with categories 1 or 2 in the other eye
inclusions: visual impairment category 3 in one eye, with categories 1 or 2 in the other eye

9D52.title: Hemifield losses
synonyms: Hemifield loss in migraine or epilepsy
Hemifield loss caused by vertebrobasilar artery

9D95.title: Impairment of best corrected visual acuity
synonyms: Impairment of best corrected visual acuity

AA00.title: Abscess of external ear
AA00.definition: A fluctuant collection of purulent exudate and necrotic tissue located in the external auditory canal or in the soft tissues of the pinna, most commonly due to Staphylococcus aureus.

9D90.6.title: Blindness
9D90.6.definition: The numerical definition used for WHO statistics refers to profound, near-total or total loss. The functional definition refers to individuals who have little or no residual vision and who have to rely predominantly on vision substitution skills, i.e. on using senses other than vision (Braille or talking books for reading, a long cane or guide dog for mobility, or touch for manipulation).
synonyms: visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in both eyes
visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in one eye and categories 1, 2, 3 or 9 in the other eye
visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in one eye [normal vision in other eye]
inclusions: visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in both eyes
visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in one eye and categories 1, 2, 3 or 9 in the other eye
visual impairment categories 4, 5, 6 in one eye [normal vision in other eye]

9D56.title: Visual release hallucinations
9D56.definition: Visual release hallucinations, also called Charles Bonnet syndrome, refer to the experience of complex visual hallucinations in a person who has experienced partial or complete loss of vision. Hallucinations are exclusively visual, usually temporary, and unrelated to mental and behavioural disorders.
exclusions: Schizophrenia or other primary psychotic disorders

9D92.title: Specific vision dysfunctions
9D92.definition: Specific visual dysfunctions refer to functional deficits in higher cerebral centres. Such dysfunctions may exist with or without visual impairment of the eyes and the lower visual system.

9D90.2.title: Moderate vision impairment
synonyms: visual impairment category 2, in both eyes
inclusions: visual impairment category 2, in both eyes

AA03.title: Otomycosis
AA03.definition: Fungal infection of the ear. Otomycosis is due to Aspergillus spp., especially A. niger, in 75% or more of cases and Candida in most of the remainder.

AA01.title: Cellulitis of external ear
AA01.definition: A diffuse subacute bacterial infection of the soft tissues of the external ear, most commonly due to beta-haemolytic streptococci. It may arise within an apparently healthy external ear but may complicate both inflammatory and infective forms of otitis externa.

AA10.title: Seborrhoeic otitis externa
AA10.definition: Seborrhoeic dermatitis affecting the skin of the external ear. It is usually accompanied by evidence of seborrhoeic dermatitis at other sites. In mild cases it may be asymptomatic but it can present acutely with severe pain, oedema and exudation. Longstanding cases may be complicated by chronic lymphoedema and occlusion of the external auditory canal.

AA1Z.title: Noninfectious inflammation of external ear, unspecified
synonyms: Noninfectious inflammation of external ear, unspecified

AA12.title: Chondrodermatitis nodularis
AA12.definition: A common pressure-induced painful nodule or ulcer affecting the external ear. It results from ischaemia of skin and underlying cartilage from a focal point of high pressure from the weight of the recumbent head. The site of involvement is dependent on the shape of the pinna (most commonly the helix is involved but in some individuals it is the antihelix which is more prominent) and whether the sufferer is limited to sleeping on one side and is thus unable to spare the ear from constant pressure when lying in bed.

AA11.title: Acute noninfectious otitis externa
AA11.definition: Rapid onset of eczematous inflammation of the outer ear the cause of which cannot be more precisely classified.
exclusions: Allergic contact dermatitis of external ear
Irritant contact dermatitis of external ear

9E1Y.title: Other specified diseases of the visual system
synonyms: Other specified diseases of the visual system
Certain specified disorders of the visual organs
Microcornea - rod-cone dystrophy - cataract - posterior staphyloma
Disorders of vision or visual functioning

AA0Y.title: Other specified infectious diseases of external ear
synonyms: Other specified infectious diseases of external ear
Acute bacterial inflammation of external ear

9E1Z.title: Diseases of the visual system, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases of the visual system, unspecified

AA3Y.title: Other specified otitis externa
synonyms: Disorders of external ear in diseases classified elsewhere

AA04.title: Perichondritis of external ear
AA04.definition: Perichondritis is an infection of the tissue surrounding the cartilage of the outer ear, the perichondrium. It usually results from injury to the ear from ear surgery, ear piercing (especially piercing of the cartilage), or trauma from contact sports. The most common bacterium causing perichondritis is Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Presenting features include pain, redness and swelling of the auricle, and fever.

AA02.title: Malignant otitis externa
AA02.definition: Malignant otitis externa is a rare life-threatening infective complication of otitis externa. It is due in the majority of cases to Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Organisms penetrate from the external ear canal into the surrounding deeper tissues resulting in osteomyelitis of the temporal bone and risks of damage to adjacent cranial nerves and septic thrombo-emboli to the brain. Advanced age, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and immunosuppression are risk factors.
synonyms: Pseudomonas aeruginosa osteomyelitis of the temporal bone

AA40.Y.title: Other specified acquired deformity of external auditory canal
synonyms: Other specified acquired deformity of external auditory canal

AA0Z.title: Infectious diseases of external ear, unspecified
synonyms: Infectious diseases of external ear, unspecified

AA40.1.title: Acquired stenosis of external auditory canal
AA40.1.definition: Acquired stenosis of external auditory canal was described as resulting from a number of different causes. Since then, histology and imaging studies of this disease have shown that a common cascade of inflammatory changes resulting from these different causes is the primary pathogenesis leading to medial canal fibrosis. Once there is complete obstruction of the external auditory canal, surgery is the primary treatment.
synonyms: Acquired stenosis of external auditory canal
acquired stricture of external auditory canal

AA1Y.title: Other specified noninfectious inflammation of external ear
synonyms: Other specified noninfectious inflammation of external ear

AA41.Y.title: Other specified acquired deformity of pinna
synonyms: Other specified acquired deformity of pinna
benign idiopathic cystic chondromalacia of the pinna

AA42.title: Impacted cerumen
AA42.definition: Impacted cerumen is the presence of occlusive aural wax in the external ear canal. Wax may cause tinnitus or otalgia and removal may be required to allow adequate otoscopic examination and/or alleviate symptoms.

AA4Y.title: Other specified noninflammatory disorders of the external ear
synonyms: Other specified noninflammatory disorders of the external ear

AA4Z.title: Noninflammatory disorders of the external ear, unspecified
synonyms: Noninflammatory disorders of the external ear, unspecified

AA91.0.title: Chronic tubotympanic suppurative otitis media
AA91.0.definition: Having a tympanic membrane perforation for at least three months, chronic suppurative otitis media has traditionally been classified into safe and unsafe type. Chronic tubotympanic suppurative otitis media is considered "safe" (meaning it is unlikely to become a worse problem for the patient) if it involves a central perforation of the pars tensa with the inflammatory process affecting the mucosa of the middle ear cleft.

AA8Z.title: Nonsuppurative otitis media, unspecified
synonyms: nonsuppurative otitis media, not specified as acute or chronic
Chronic nonserous nonmucoid nonsuppurative otitis media
chronic allergic otitis media, unspecified ear
Nonpurulent chronic otitis media with effusion
Chronic nonsuppurative otitis media with purulent effusion

AA82.title: Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media
AA82.definition: Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media is probably the most common form of sub-acute middle ear disease found in the developed world. It typically lingers following otitis media, when the fluid in the ear, formed by the infection, does not clear spontaneously. The tympanic membrane is intact but the middle ear is liquid- fluid filled. This presumably puts the middle ear at risk for further infection and often worsens hearing by about 30 dB. This is most frequently found in children and can interfere with language acquisition and learning.
synonyms: Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media
Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media with transudative
Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media with exudative
Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media with effusion
Chronic serous or mucoid otitis media with nonpurulent effusion
chronic nonsuppurative otitis media with serous effusion
chronic mucoid otitis media, simple or unspecified
chronic mucoid otitis media, unspecified ear

AA91.1.title: Chronic atticoantral suppurative otitis media
AA91.1.definition: Chronic suppurative otitis media has traditionally been classified into safe and unsafe type. Chronic atticoantral suppurative otitis media which is unsafe type is typified by a marginal perforation of the posterosuperior pars tensa or pars flaccida.
synonyms: Chronic atticoantral disease with posterior or superior marginal perforation of ear drum
Persistent mucosal disease with posterior or superior marginal perforation of ear drum

AA41.0.title: Cauliflower ear
AA41.0.definition: Cauliflower ear is the end result of fibrosis of the skin and soft tissues of the pinna following a traumatic subperichondrial haematoma, usually due to trauma. It manifests as permanent swelling and deformity of the ear, described as resembling a cauliflower. It is found most commonly amongst men involved in contact sports such as boxing, wrestling, martial arts and rugby football.
synonyms: Deformity of pinna following traumatic perichondrial haematoma

AA90.title: Acute suppurative otitis media
AA90.definition: Acute suppurative otitis media is defined as an inflammation of the middle ear which erupts suddenly and passes quickly. It is characteristic to have a middle-ear infection behind a reddened eardrum.
synonyms: acute or subacute suppurative otitis media
acute or subacute purulent otitis media

AA40.Z.title: Acquired deformity of external auditory canal, unspecified

AA81.title: Acute nonserous nonsuppurative otitis media
synonyms: acute and subacute nonsuppurative otitis media, NOS
Acute and subacute allergic otitis media
Acute and subacute sanguinous otitis media
Acute or subacute exudative otitis media
Acute or subacute otitis media with effusion
Acute or subacute seromucinous otitis media
Acute or subacute transudative otitis media

AA80.title: Acute serous or mucoid otitis media
AA80.definition: Acute serous or mucoid otitis media is a collection of non-infected fluid in the middle ear that has developed as a result of a upper respiratory infection.
synonyms: Acute serous or mucoid otitis media
Acute or subacute secretory otitis media
Acute or subacute serous otitis media

AB10.Y.title: Other specified disorders of Eustachian tube
synonyms: Other specified disorders of Eustachian tube

AB18.title: Discontinuity or dislocation of ear ossicles
synonyms: Discontinuity or dislocation of ear ossicles

AB13.Y.title: Other specified perforation of tympanic membrane
synonyms: Other specified perforation of tympanic membrane
Persistent post traumatic perforation of ear drum

AA91.2.title: Other chronic suppurative otitis media
AA91.2.definition: This involves a perforation (hole) in the tympanic membrane and active bacterial infection within the middle ear space for several weeks or more. There may be enough pus that it drains to the outside of the ear (otorrhea), or the purulence may be minimal enough to only be seen on examination using a binocular microscope.
synonyms: Chronic otitis media with purulent effusion

AB11.1.title: Chronic mastoiditis
AB11.1.definition: Persistent or recurrent inflammation of the space in the mastoid bone. It is often a complication of otitis media.
synonyms: chronic mastoiditis with opacification of mastoid

AB0Y.title: Other specified otitis media
synonyms: Otitis media in diseases classified elsewhere
Otitis media in viral diseases classified elsewhere
Otitis media in bacterial diseases classified elsewhere
Otitis media due to Streptococcus pneumoniae

AB13.2.title: Other marginal perforations of tympanic membrane
synonyms: Other marginal perforations of tympanic membrane

AB13.0.title: Central perforation of tympanic membrane
AB13.0.definition: A temporary or persistent opening in the central portion of the tympanic membrane. Clinical signs depend on the size, location, and associated pathological condition.

AB11.0.title: Acute mastoiditis
AB11.0.definition: Rapid onset inflammation of the mastoid bone, located in the skull just behind the ear. It is often a complication of otitis media.

AA9Z.title: Suppurative otitis media, unspecified whether acute or chronic
synonyms: Suppurative otitis media, unspecified whether acute or chronic

AB11.Y.title: Other specified mastoiditis or related conditions
synonyms: Other specified mastoiditis or related conditions
Mastoiditis in infectious or parasitic diseases classified elsewhere

AB1Y.title: Other specified diseases of middle ear or mastoid
synonyms: Other specified diseases of middle ear or mastoid
Certain specified disorders of tympanic membrane
Certain specified disorders of middle ear or mastoid

AB16.title: Tympanosclerosis
AB16.definition: Tympanosclerosis is a scarring process with a remarkable variability in its localization within the middle ear. It can lead to conductive hearing loss.

AB15.title: Chronic myringitis
AB15.definition: Persistent or recurrent inflammation of the tympanic membrane.
synonyms: chronic myringitis without mention of otitis media

AB13.1.title: Attic perforation of tympanic membrane
synonyms: attic perforation of tympanic membrane, unspecified ear

AB30.1.title: Labyrinthitis
AB30.1.definition: Labyrinthitis is an inflammatory disorder of the inner ear (labyrinth) producing disturbances of balance and hearing to varying degrees. It can be caused by bacterial or viral infections and autoimmune processes.
synonyms: Inner ear infection, not elsewhere classified

AB30.Y.title: Other specified acute vestibular syndrome
synonyms: Acute vestibular syndrome in diseases classified elsewhere
Acute vestibular syndrome due to cerebrovascular disease
Acute vestibular syndrome due to acute attack of episodic vestibular disorder
Acute vestibular syndrome due to anxiety or fear-related disorders
Acute vestibular syndrome due to injury to the head

AB1Z.title: Diseases of middle ear or mastoid, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases of middle ear or mastoid, unspecified
Disorder of middle ear and mastoid, unspecified

AB30.0.title: Vestibular neuritis
AB30.0.definition: Vestibular neuritis (also known as vestibular neuronitis) may be described as acute, sustained dysfunction of the peripheral vestibular system with secondary nausea, vomiting, and vertigo. Important negative features include aural fullness and hearing loss.

AB31.4.title: Disembarkment syndrome
AB31.4.definition: Disembarkment syndrome, or Mal de debarquement (MdD) occurs when habituation to unfamiliar motion patterns like traveling on a boat, train, or airplane, becomes resistant to re-adaption on return to stable conditions. It results in an illusion of self motion typically described as rocking, bobbing, or swaying. Brief periods of MdD (hours) are common in healthy individuals, this otherwise natural phenomenon can become persistent in some individuals.

AB31.0.title: Meniere disease
AB31.0.definition: Meniere Disease (MD) is a chronic progressive inner ear disease, with endolymphatic hydrops. It is characterised by recurrent attacks of debilitating spontaneous vertigo lasting from 20 minutes to up to 12 hours, accompanied by a sense of fullness and tinnitus in the affected ear, and ipsilateral fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) in the low or low and middle frequencies. There may be nystagmus during attacks and falls are frequent. When known, etiology should be added.

AB31.Y.title: Other specified episodic vestibular syndrome

AB14.title: Acute myringitis
AB14.definition: Myringitis is the inflammation of the tympanic membrane, often involving painful blisters on the tympanic membrane. It can develop as self-maintained primary disease of the TM (primary myringitis) or as an effect of an inflammatory process of adjacent tissues of the external or middle ear (secondary myringitis). Myringitis may be accompanied by hearing impairment and a sensation of congestion and earache. It is generally a viral or bacterial infection and may occur with otitis media. After 3 weeks, acute myringitis becomes subacute and, within 3 months, chronic.

AB31.1.title: Vestibular migraine
AB31.1.definition: Recurrent attacks of moderate to severe vestibular symptoms lasting from 5 minutes to 72 hours in patients with a past or ongoing history of migraine headaches. Vestibular symptoms are usually spontaneous and positional vertigo, head motion-induced and visual vertigo as well as head motion-induced dizziness with nausea. Attacks of vestibular symptoms may occur together or independently of migraine symptoms like headache, photophobia, phonophobia or visual aura.

AB31.6.title: Vestibular paroxysmia
AB31.6.definition: Vestibular paroxysmia (VP) is characterised by recurrent spells of vertigo or dizziness, lasting seconds to minutes, often many times a day. Attacks usually occur spontaneously but may occasionally be induced by changes of head position (which then needs to be distinguished from benign paroxysmal positioning vertigo). Possible accompanying symptoms are short attacks of tinnitus or changes in hearing. In the attack-free interval mild to moderate impairments of vestibular or audiological function may be found. Neurovascular cross-compression of the eighth nerve is the assumed mechanism.

AB31.5.title: Autoimmune inner ear disease
AB31.5.definition: Autoimmune inner ear disease (AIED) is a clinical syndrome of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) >30dB at one or more frequencies progressing over a period of 3-90 days. Progression of SNLH >15dB at one frequency or >10dB in two frequencies in at least one ear should be demonstrated. Vestibular symptoms may be present in 50% of patients and systemic autoimmune disease (SAD) coexists in 30% of patients.

AB31.2.title: Benign positional paroxysmal vertigo
AB31.2.definition: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is defined as an abnormal sensation of motion that is elicited by certain critical provocative physical positions of the patient (e.g. becoming dorsal recumbent). The provocative positions usually trigger specific eye movements (e.g. nystagmus). The character and direction of the nystagmus is specific to the part of the inner ear affected and the underlying pathophysiology.

Benign positional paroxysmal vertigo lateral canal

AB32.0.title: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness
AB32.0.definition: Persistent non-vertiginous dizziness, unsteadiness, or both lasting three months or more. Symptoms are present most days, often increasing throughout the day, but may wax and wane. Momentary flares may occur spontaneously or with sudden movement. Affected individuals feel worst when upright, exposed to moving or complex visual stimuli, and during active or passive head motion. These situations may not be equally provocative. Typically, the disorder follows occurrences of acute or episodic vestibular or balance-related problems. Symptoms may begin intermittently, and then consolidate. Gradual onset is uncommon.

AB33.title: Otosclerosis
AB33.definition: Otosclerosis is a genetically mediated metabolic bone disease that affects the otic capsule and stapes. It is an autosomal dominant disorder with varying penetrance and expressivity. Usually symptomatic hearing loss from otosclerosis develops early in the third decade of life, although onset in the teenage years does occur.

AB32.5.title: Chronic bilateral vestibulopathy
AB32.5.definition: Bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) results from impaired vestibular function of both inner ears. It is clinically characterised by postural imbalance and unsteadiness of gait that worsens in darkness and on uneven ground, head or body movement-induced oscillopsia. If known, the etiology should be added to the diagnosis.
synonyms: Chronic bilateral vestibulopathy due to ototoxic agents
Chronic bilateral vestibulopathy due to bilateral schwannoma

AB31.3.title: Superior canal dehiscence syndrome
AB31.3.definition: Superior canal dehiscence syndrome (SCDS) occurs when thin or dehiscent bone over the superior semicircular canal, best demonstrated on CT, allows pressure transmission between the canal and the intracranial space. Vertigo and nystagmus may occur when the canal is stimulated by loud sounds or changes in middle ear or intracranial pressure. Hyperacusis to bone-conducted sounds can cause conductive hearing loss, pulsatile tinnitus, or autophony (hearing one’s own body sounds as loud or distorted). While the bony defect may be congenital, head trauma can be the final step that opens a functionally mobile labyrinthine window.

AB34.0.title: Idiopathic bilateral vestibulopathy
AB34.0.definition: This results as the culmination of damage done to both inner ears and causes problems in vision, hearing and motor coordination.

AB35.title: Labyrinthine fistula
AB35.definition: Labyrinthine fistula is a condition in which an abnormal communication is present between the perilymphatic space of the inner ear and the middle ear (usually at or adjacent to the round or oval window). The manifestations of this disease vary in severity and complexity, commonly ranging from very mild to incapacitating.

AB37.title: Noise effects on inner ear
AB37.definition: Noise toxicity can cause hearing loss, either transient or permanent, and impairment. Noise-induced hearing loss typically begins in the high-pitched frequency range of human voices communication.

AB51.0.title: Acquired conductive hearing loss
AB51.0.definition: Conductive hearing loss occurs when there is a problem conducting sound waves anywhere along the route through the outer ear, tympanic membrane (eardrum), or middle ear (ossicles), bilateral.

AB51.2.title: Acquired mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss
AB51.2.definition: Conductive hearing loss occurs when there is a problem conducting sound waves anywhere along the route through the outer ear, tympanic membrane (eardrum), or middle ear (ossicles). Sensorineural hearing loss is a type of hearing loss in which the root cause lies in the vestibulocochlear nerve (Cranial nerve VIII), the inner ear, or central processing centres of the brain. This diagnosis refers to a mix of both conductive and sensorineural hearing loss.
synonyms: Acquired mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss

AB51.1.title: Acquired sensorineural hearing loss
AB51.1.definition: Sensorineural hearing loss is a type of hearing loss in which the root cause lies in the vestibulocochlear nerve (Cranial nerve VIII), the inner ear, or central processing centres of the brain.

AB57.title: Auditory synaptopathy or neuropathy
AB57.definition: Normal outer hair cell function but lacking synchrony of neural transmission of auditory information due to damage of inner hair cells or their synapses or of the spiral ganglion cells or of the auditory nerve

AB54.definition: The term presbycusis refers to sensorineural hearing impairment in elderly individuals. Characteristically, presbycusis involves bilateral high-frequency hearing loss associated with difficulty in speech discrimination and central auditory processing of information.

It is a form of ischaemic cardiomyopathy causing systolic ventricular dysfunction that relates to a spectrum of perfusion contraction matching and mismatching, including myocardial infarction, stunning, hibernation and scarring.

BA60.1.title: Other pericarditis as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
BA60.1.definition: An inflammation of the pericardium that can produce chest pain, which occurs as early as the first day and as late as 6 weeks after acute myocardial infarction. The pain of pericarditis radiates to either trapezius ridge. Transmural myocardial infarction is responsible for local pericardial inflammation. Transient pericardial friction rubs are relatively common in patients with transmural infarction within the first 48 hours. An acute fibrinous pericarditis occurs commonly after transmural infarction, whereas the risk of haemorrhagic pericarditis is increased by anticoagulation.
synonyms: Other pericarditis as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
Pericarditis as current complication following acute myocardial infarction, with effusion
Pericarditis as current complication following acute myocardial infarction, without effusion

BA60.9.title: Cardiogenic shock, unrelated to mechanical complications, as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
BA60.9.definition: The most severe clinical expression of left ventricular failure and is associated with extensive damage to the left ventricular myocardium after acute myocardial infarction, unrelated to a mechanical defect such as ventricular septal or papillary muscle rupture. Shock is defined as systolic blood pressure (BP) < 90 mmHg and organ hypoperfusion.
synonyms: Cardiogenic shock, unrelated to mechanical complications, as current complication following acute myocardial infarction

BA60.4.title: Cardiac rupture as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
BA60.4.definition: A tearing of acutely infarcted tissue after acute myocardial infarction, which may involve the papillary muscles, interventricular septum, or free wall of either ventricle.
synonyms: Cardiac rupture as current complication following acute myocardial infarction

BA60.2.title: Ventricular aneurysm as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
BA60.2.definition: A discrete dyskinetic area of the left ventricular wall with a broad neck after acute myocardial infarction. The wall of the true aneurysm is thinner than the rest of the left ventricle; it is usually composed of fibrous tissue and necrotic muscle, occasionally mixed with viable myocardium. In contrast, pseudoaneurysms are composed of organised hematoma and pericardium and lack any elements of the original myocardial wall.
synonyms: Ventricular aneurysm as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
ventricular aneurysm following acute myocardial infarction

BA60.0.title: Dressler syndrome
BA60.0.definition: A condition of postmyocardial infarction (1 to 8 weeks), characterised by a set of associated symptom, including malaise, fever, pericardial discomfort, leukocytosis, an elevated sedimentation rate, and a pericardial effusion. Patients with this syndrome usually demonstrate localised fibrous pericarditis containing polymorphonuclear leukocytes.

BA60.7.title: Mural thrombus as current complication following acute myocardial infarction
BA60.7.definition: A blood clot formed on the endoventricle or endoatirium, usually overlying dyskinetic or akinetic area of the ventricular infarction after acute myocardial infarction.

BA60.3.title: Ventricular septal defect as current complication following acute myocardial infarction

Rupture of the septum with an anterior infarction tends to be apical in location, whereas inferior infarctions are associated with perforation of the basal septum.

BB01.3.title: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
BB01.3.definition: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is characterised by the persistence of thromboemboli in the form of organised tissue obstructing the pulmonary arteries. BA82.title: Coronary artery dissection

BB00.0.definition: Acute pulmonary thromboembolism is defined as a partial or complete occlusion of a pulmonary arterial branch with the abrupt onset of related symptoms, such as dyspnoea, tachypnoea, chest pain, cough and blood-tinged sputum. BB20.0.title: Infectious pericarditis
BB20.0.definition: A disease of the pericardium, caused by a secondary infection with a bacterial, viral, or fungal source. This disease is characterised by fever, odynophagia, cough, fatigue, or chest pain. Confirmation is by identification of the bacterial, viral, or fungal agent in a blood sample.

BB03.0.title: Acquired pulmonary venous obstruction
BB03.0.definition: A postnatal pathologic condition of one or more pulmonary vein(s) in which flow is impeded or blocked due to narrowing or atresia.

BB25.title: Pericardial effusion
BB25.definition: Pericardial effusion is an abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pericardial sac. Noninflammatory diseases such as chronic renal failure, circulatory congestion, hypothyroidism and amyroidosis can cause pericardial effusion.

BB24.title: Haemopericardium
BB24.definition: This is hemopericardium caused by diseases not elsewhere classified. Hemopericardium generally refers to blood in the pericardial sac of the heart. It is clinically similar to a pericardial effusion, and, depending on the volume and rapidity with which it develops, may cause cardiac tamponade.

BB60.1.title: Nonrheumatic mitral valve stenosis
BB60.1.definition:
Mitral stenosis is narrowing of the passage through the mitral valve due to fibrosis, and calcinosis in the leaflets and chordal areas.
The most common reason of mitral stenosis is rheumatic fever. Except rheumatic fever; SLE, Malignant Sarcoid, Active Infective Endocarditis, Gout Whipple's Disease, Massive Annular calcification cause to the mitral stenosis.

BB40.title: Acute or subacute infectious endocarditis
synonyms: Acute or subacute infectious endocarditis, laterality not specified
Acute or subacute infective endocarditis, left-sided
Acute or subacute infective endocarditis, right-sided
Endocarditis of truncal valve or neo-aortic valve of truncal origin
Endocarditis of the neoaortic valve of pulmonary origin

BB23.title: Cardiac tamponade
BB23.definition: Cardiac tamponade is a clinical syndrome caused by the accumulation of fluid in the pericardial space, resulting in reduced ventricular filling and subsequent hemodynamic compromise. Cardiac tamponade is a medical emergency, the complications of which include shock, and death.

BB22.title: Constrictive pericarditis
BB22.definition: Chronic fibrous pericarditis due to the presence of dense fibrous tissue between the parietal and visceral layers of pericardium and neighbouring structures.

BB4Y.title: Other specified acute or subacute endocarditis

acute or subacute tricuspid valve nonrheumatic endocarditis

BB60.0.title: Rheumatic mitral valve stenosis
BB60.0.definition: Mitral stenosis refers to narrowing of the mitral valve orifice, resulting in impedance of filling of the left ventricle in diastole. It is usually caused by rheumatic heart disease.

BB62.Y.title: Other specified nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse
synonyms: Other specified nonrheumatic mitral valve prolapse

BB72.0.title: Rheumatic aortic stenosis with insufficiency
BB72.0.definition: Aortic stenosis from chronic rheumatic heart disease is typically associated with aortic insufficiency. The valve commissures and cuspis become adherent and fused, and the valve orifice becomes small. Upon auscultation, S2 may be single because the aortic leaflets are immobile and do not produce an aortic closure sound

BB62.0.title: Rheumatic mitral valve prolapse
BB62.0.definition: This is a rheumatic valvular heart disease characterised by the displacement of an abnormally thickened mitral valve leaflet into the left atrium during systole.

BB70.0.title: Rheumatic aortic valve stenosis
BB70.0.definition: Aortic stenosis caused by scarring of the aortic valve due to rheumatic fever as a child or young adult. In aortic stenosis, the aortic valve does not open fully. This decreases blood flow from the heart.

BB80.0.title: Rheumatic tricuspid valve stenosis
BB80.0.definition: Tricuspid stenosis is almost always rheumatic in origin. Tricuspid stenosis results in the narrowing of the orifice of the tricuspid valve of the heart.

BB63.1.title: Nonrheumatic mitral stenosis with insufficiency
BB63.1.definition: This is a non-rheumatic valvular heart disease characterised by the narrowing of the orifice of the mitral valve of the heart, with regurgitation.

BB63.0.title: Rheumatic mitral stenosis with insufficiency
BB63.0.definition: Mitral stenosis and mitral insufficiency occur in patients with rheumatic heart disease.

BB62.1.title: Degenerative mitral valve prolapse
BB62.1.definition: This is a degenerative valvular heart disease characterised by the displacement of an abnormally thickened mitral valve leaflet into the left atrium during systole.

BB71.0.title: Rheumatic aortic valve insufficiency
BB71.0.definition: Aortic insufficiency is the leaking of the aortic valve of the heart that causes blood to flow in the reverse direction during ventricular diastole, from the aorta into the left ventricle. Rheumatic fever causes the valve cusps to retract.
exclusions: Active or acute rheumatic endocarditis of aortic valve

BB63.Z.title: Mitral valve stenosis with insufficiency, unspecified

BB61.0.title: Rheumatic mitral valve insufficiency
BB61.0.definition:
Mitral insufficiency can be caused by conditions such as rheumatic fever.
Mitral insufficiency is leakage of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during systole.
exclusions: Active or acute endocarditis of mitral valve

BB74.title: Aortic valvar prolapse
BB74.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the aortic valve in which part or all of one or more of the aortic valve leaflets is on the ventricular side of the plane of the inferior aspect of the attachments of the aortic valve leaflets.

BB82.0.title: Rheumatic tricuspid valve stenosis with insufficiency
BB82.0.definition: Tricuspid valve insufficiency due to leaflet abnormalities may be secondary to rheumatic heart disease. When due to the latter, it generally occurs in combination with tricuspid stenosis

BB90.0.title: Rheumatic pulmonary valve stenosis
BB90.0.definition: This is a rheumatic heart valve disorder in which outflow of blood from the right ventricle of the heart is obstructed at the level of the pulmonic valve.

BC42.0.title: Giant cell myocarditis
BC42.0.definition: Giant cell myocarditis is a form of dilated cardiomyopathy secondary to myocardial inflammation that is characterised by widespread infiltration of giant cells (abnormal masses produced by the fusion of macrophages) associated with other inflammatory cells and heart muscle cell destruction.

BC41.0.title: Acquired interventricular communication

BC43.11.title: Non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
BC43.11.definition: Non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy that has no fixed or dynamic intraventricular narrowing sufficient to result in a significant pressure gradient between the ventricular apex and the outflow valve (aortic or pulmonary).

BC42.3.title: Rheumatic myocarditis
BC42.3.definition: Rheumatic myocarditis is cardiac inflammation and scarring triggered by an autoimmune reaction to group A streptococci infection resulting acutely in pancarditis involving inflammation of the myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium and chronically by valve fibrosis.
synonyms: inactive or quiescent rheumatic fever with myocarditis
dilated cardiomyopathy due to rheumatic fever

BC43.10.title: Familial-genetic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
BC43.10.definition: Familial isolated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the presence of non-syndromic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in multiple members of a pedigree, or in the presence of a genetic mutation known to be significantly associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Additional information: Candidate cytoskeletal and Z disk–encoding genes, most of whom are hypothesized to lead to abnormalities in force transmission, include δ-sarcoglycan, β-sarcoglycan, desmin, lamin A/C, metavinculin, muscle LIM protein, titin, α-actinin-2, nebulette, myopalladin, and ZASP (Z band alternatively spliced PDZ domain protein)
