CB40.4.definition: Compensatory emphysema is a condition in which one portion of the lung increases in size and function, when another portion is destroyed or temporarily useless. It occurs, for instance, in association with pneumonias, pleural effusions and pneumothorax. Anatomically, there is found an enlargement of the normal lung; there are no variations from the normal structure; the unaffected lung, as a result of distention, has an increased vital capacity and is able to perform a greater amount of work than when in its usual condition. The tissues show no similarity to those truly emphysematous. This change is in no way related to true emphysema and the term should not be used, as it creates great confusion in the literature. Its use is no more justified than that of speaking of the compensatory enlargement of a kidney, when the opposite kidney has been removed, as of a compensatory nephritis. True emphysema can never compensate for diseased lung tissue, because the emphysematous lung is totally or almost totally functionless.

CB2Z.title: Pleural, diaphragm or mediastinal disorders, unspecified
synonyms: Pleural, diaphragm or mediastinal disorders, unspecified

CB41.10.title: Chronic respiratory failure, Type I
CB41.10.definition: When chronic respiratory failure causes a low level of oxygen in the blood without a high level of carbon dioxide, it's called hypoxemic chronic respiratory failure.
synonyms: Hypoxic chronic respiratory failure, Type I

CB22.0.title: Fibrosing mediastinitis
CB22.0.definition: Fibrosing mediastinitis, also known as sclerosing mediastinitis or mediastinal fibrosis, is a disorder characterised by an excessive fibrotic reaction in the mediastinum. It can result in compromise of airways, great vessels, and other mediastinal structures, with morbidity directly related to the location and extent of fibrosis. The commonest cause is histoplasmosis, of which it is a rare late complication, but it may also occur in association with other infections and with systemic autoimmune disorders such as Behçet disease, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and retroperitoneal fibrosis.
synonyms: Fibrosing mediastinitis in association with systemic autoimmune disease

DA00.0.title: Cheilitis
DA00.0.definition: Cheilitis is the generic term given to inflammatory conditions of the lip.
synonyms: Angular cheilitis due to bacterial infection
Angular cheilitis exacerbated by mechanical factors
Angular cheilitis exacerbated by nutritional deficiency

CB41.11.title: Chronic respiratory failure, Type II
CB41.11.definition: When chronic respiratory failure causes a high level of carbon dioxide in the blood, it's called hypercapnic chronic respiratory failure.
synonyms: Hypercapnic chronic respiratory failure, Type II

DA00.2.title: Pigmentary abnormalities of lips
DA00.2.definition: This is an abnormality in the material that changes the colour of reflected or transmitted light as the result of wavelength-selective absorption, of the lips.

CB41.2Z.title: Respiratory failure, unspecified
synonyms: Respiratory failure, unspecified as acute or chronic

CB41.20.title: Respiratory failure, unspecified, Type I
CB41.20.definition: This is when the PaCO2 may be normal or low. It is typically caused by a ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) mismatch; the volume of air flowing in and out of the lungs is not matched with the flow of blood to the lungs. The basic defect in type 1 respiratory failure is failure of oxygenation
synonyms: Hypoxic respiratory failure, unspecified, Type I

DA01.0Y.title: Other specified disturbances of oral epithelium
synonyms: Other specified disturbances of oral epithelium

DA01.01.title: Hairy leukoplakia
DA01.01.definition: Oral hairy leukoplakia is a focal epithelial hyperplasia of the oral mucosa associated with Epstein-Barr virus. It is closely associated with HIV and occurs in both immunocompromised and immunocompetent HIV-infected individuals. It is also, however, found in uninfected people who are immunosuppressed, e.g. organ transplant recipients. It presents as white patches with a corrugated or hairy appearance affecting particularly the lateral borders of the tongue.

CB41.01.title: Acute respiratory failure, Type II
CB41.01.definition: When acute respiratory failure causes a high level of carbon dioxide in the blood, it's called hypercapnic acute respiratory failure.
synonyms: Hypercapnic acute respiratory failure, Type II

CB7Z.title: Diseases of the respiratory system, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases of the respiratory system, unspecified

CB64.title: Transfusion related acute lung injury
CB64.definition: This is a serious blood transfusion complication characterised by the acute onset of non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema following transfusion of blood products.

DA00.1.title: Self-induced lip trauma
DA00.1.definition: Self-inflicted damage to lips by biting, picking, chewing etc.

DA01.02.title: Wandering rash of the mouth
DA01.02.definition: The counterpart of geographic tongue affecting other parts of the oral epithelium. It is less common than geographic tongue.

CB41.21.title: Respiratory failure, unspecified, Type II
CB41.21.definition: Type 2 respiratory failure is caused by inadequate ventilation; both oxygen and carbon dioxide are affected. Defined as the build up of carbon dioxide levels (PaCO2) that has been generated by the body.
synonyms: Hypercapnic respiratory failure, unspecified, Type II

CB62.title: Postprocedural subglottic stenosis
synonyms: subglottic stenosis due to medical procedure

DA01.11.title: Oral mucositis
DA01.11.definition: Ulcerative mucositis is the inflammation of the oral mucosa with inflammation, ulceration and frequently with bleeding.
synonyms: Oral mucositis due to cancer chemotherapy
Oral mucositis due to graft-versus-host disease
Oral mucositis due to other specified cause

DA01.13.title: Erythema multiforme with oral ulceration
DA01.13.definition: This is a skin condition of unknown cause, possibly mediated by deposition of immune complex (mostly IgM) in the superficial microvasculature of the skin and oral mucous membrane that usually follows an infection or drug exposure.

DA01.2Y.title: Other specified granuloma or granuloma-like lesions of oral mucosa
synonyms: Other specified granuloma or granuloma-like lesions of oral mucosa
Lobular capillary haemangioma of oral mucosa
Traumatic ulcerative granuloma with stromal eosinophilia
TUGSE - [Traumatic ulcerative granuloma with stromal eosinophilia]

DA01.15.title: Mouth ulcers
DA01.15.definition: Oral ulceration of other specified or unspecified type.

DA01.1Y.title: Other specified noninfectious erosive or ulcerative disorders of oral mucosa
synonyms: Other specified noninfectious erosive or ulcerative disorders of oral mucosa
Oral ulceration due to immunobullous disease
Oral mucosal involvement by immunobullous disorder classified elsewhere
Oral ulceration due to physical injury

DA01.1Z.title: Noninfectious erosive or ulcerative disorders of oral mucosa, unspecified

DA01.12.title: Chronic ulcerative stomatitis
DA01.12.definition: Chronic ulcerative stomatitis (CUS) is a rare disease which presents with chronic oral mucosal erosions and ulceration resembling erosive lichen planus but refractory to standard therapies. It typically occurs in older women. Diagnosis requires the demonstration of speckled granular perinuclear IgG deposits in the basal and parabasal layers of oral epithelium (stratified epithelium-specific antinuclear or SES-ANA pattern). There is increasing evidence that CUS is an autoimmune disease provoked by circulating IgG antibodies directed against delta-Np63, an isoform of the p53 family of nuclear transcription factors which is present around the nuclei of normal oral epithelial basal keratinocytes. CUS normally responds to treatment with hydroxychloroquine.

DA01.10.title: Oral aphthae or aphtha-like ulceration
DA01.10.definition: This is a frequent small, shallow, painful ulceration in the oral mucosa. Recurrent oral ulceration that clinically resembles recurrent aphthous stomatitis but presents atypically, including commencement after adolescence, with fever, with a strong family history, or failing to resolve with age.
synonyms: Periodic fever - aphthous stomatitis - pharyngitis - adenopathy
PFAPA - [Periodic fever - aphthous stomatitis - pharyngitis - adenopathy] syndrome

DA01.14.title: Drug-induced oral ulcer
DA01.14.definition: Ulceration of the oral mucosa attributable to medication. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and cytotoxic drugs such as methotrexate are well recognised causes but many others have been incriminated.

DA01.20.title: Giant cell granuloma, central
DA01.20.definition: A benign condition of the jaws. It is twice as likely to affect women and is more likely to occur in individuals between the age of 20 and 40. Central giant cell granulomas are more common in the mandible and often cross the midline.
synonyms: Central giant cell reparative granuloma of jaw

DA01.21.title: Orofacial granulomatosis
DA01.21.definition: Orofacial granulomatosis (OFG) is an uncommon clinicopathological entity characterised by persistent and/or recurrent lymphoedema and fissuring of the lips and oral mucosa (the latter resulting in a "cobblestone" appearance), oral ulceration and the presence on biopsy of non-caseating granulomas. OFG may be an early manifestation of Crohn disease, sometimes presenting months or years before bowel disease. Some cases are associated with dental infections, sarcoidosis, food allergy or contact allergy. Granulomatous cheilitis is a form of OFG confined to the lips. Rarely, OFG may be associated with fissured tongue and facial palsy (Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome).

DA01.00.title: Oral leukoplakia
DA01.00.definition: Leukoplakia is a condition where areas of keratosis appear as adherent white patches on the mucous membranes of the oral cavity. Leukoplakia may affect other gastrointestinal tract mucosal sites, or mucosal surfaces of the urinary tract and genitals.

DA05.Y.title: Other specified cysts of oral or facial-neck region
synonyms: Other specified cysts of oral or facial-neck region
epidermoid cyst of oral soft tissue
epidermal cyst of oral soft tissue

DA01.30.title: Cellulitis or abscess of soft tissues of the mouth
DA01.30.definition: Infection of the soft tissues of the mouth resulting in cellulitis and/or abscess formation.
synonyms: Cellulitis or abscess of soft tissues of the mouth
Submandibular abscess with mention of mediastinal, parapharyngeal or cervical extension
Submandibular abscess without mention of mediastinal, parapharyngeal or cervical extension
Submandibular space abscess, not elsewhere classified

DA04.2.title: Sialoadenitis
DA04.2.definition: Sialoadenitis (or Sialadenitis) is an inflammation of the salivary gland. It is often associated with pain, tenderness, redness, and gradual localised swelling of the affected area.
synonyms: inflammation of salivary duct or gland
Infection of salivary duct or gland
Suppuration of salivary duct or gland

DA02.31.title: Irritant contact gingivostomatitis
DA02.31.definition: Inflammation of gingivae and oral mucosa due to contact with irritants.

DA05.1.title: Developmental nonodontogenic cysts of oral region
DA05.1.definition: Cysts that arise from non-odontogenic (non-tooth forming) tissue. By definition, the cysts are lined by epithelium. These cysts include for example; nasopalatine duct cyst, palatal cyst of the neonate, globulomaxillary cyst and more.
synonyms: Developmental nonodontogenic cysts of oral region

DA04.6.title: Disturbances of salivary secretion
DA04.6.definition: A group of conditions characterised by an increase or decrease in saliva secretion.

DA03.2.title: Atrophy of tongue papillae
synonyms: Central papillary atrophy of the tongue
inclusions: Central papillary atrophy of the tongue

DA03.5.title: Macroglossia
DA03.5.definition: Macroglossia is the medical term for a large or enlarged tongue. It may be due to a variety of congenital and acquired conditions. Isolated macroglossia has no determinable cause. It is seen commonly in Down syndrome. The most common causes of tongue enlargement are vascular malformations (e.g. lymphangioma or haemangioma) and muscular hypertrophy. It may, however, be due to infiltration, as with primary systemic amyloidosis.

DA06.0.title: Inflammatory conditions of jaws
synonyms: Abscess of maxilla with mention of retromaxillary extension or extention into fossa canina
Abscess of maxilla without mention of retromaxillary extension or extention into fossa canina

DA02.1.title: Xerostomia
DA02.1.definition: Dry mouth. This may result from many causes including dehydration, salivary gland dysfunction, suppression of saliva production by drugs (e.g. anticholinergics) or habitual mouth-breathing.
synonyms: Xerostomia due to disturbance of salivary secretion
Dry mouth due to sicca syndrome
Xerostomia due to other specified salivary gland disorder

DA01.4Z.title: Irritative hyperplasia of oral mucosa, unspecified
synonyms: Irritative hyperplasia of oral mucosa, unspecified

DA04.8.title: Sialoschesis
DA04.8.definition: Suppression of the secretion of saliva.

DA01.3Y.title: Other specified infections of lips or oral mucosa
synonyms: Other specified infections of lips or oral mucosa

DA05.Z.title: Cysts of oral or facial-neck region, unspecified
synonyms: Cysts of oral or facial-neck region, unspecified
Cysts of oral or facial-neck region
cyst of oral soft tissue NOS

DA03.1.title: Geographic tongue
DA03.1.definition: A condition characterised by migratory glossitis and loss of dorsal papillae with a map-like appearance that gives origin to the name.

DA01.40.title: Papillary hyperplasia of oral mucosa
DA01.40.definition: This is an oral pathologic condition that appears in the mouth as an overgrowth of tissue usually beneath a denture and is associated with poor denture hygiene, denture overuse, and ill-fitting dentures.

DA04.3.title: Abscess of salivary gland
DA04.3.definition: This is a collection of pus (neutrophils) that has accumulated within the salivary gland because of an inflammatory process in response to either an infectious process (usually caused by bacteria or parasites) or other foreign materials.

DA01.Y.title: Other specified disorders of oral mucosa
synonyms: Other specified disorders of oral mucosa
Miscellaneous inflammatory disorders of oral mucosa
Oral mucosal disorders attributable to mechanical damage

DA01.3Z.title: Infections of lips or oral mucosa, unspecified

DA02.0.title: Genetic or developmental disorders involving lips or oral mucosa
DA02.0.definition: A group of genetic and developmental disorders characterised by abnormal facial development that particularly involves the lips and oral mucosa.
synonyms: Genetic or developmental disorders involving lips or oral mucosa
Oral mucosal fragility and ulceration due to epidermolysis bullosa classified elsewhere
Genetic or developmental disorder classified elsewhere involving lips or oral mucosa

DA04.0.title: Atrophy of salivary gland
DA04.0.definition: Salivary gland atrophy is a wasting or decrease in size of salivary gland, which is not sufficient to cause necrosis. It may occur in response to poor nutrition, lack of use (disuse or immobilization), reduction in blood supply, loss of nerve supply, chronic cell injury, or ageing etc. It is including Sjögren's syndrome, irradiation therapy and obstructive sialadenitis.

DA02.30.title: Allergic contact gingivostomatitis
DA02.30.definition: Allergic contact dermatitis affecting the gingivae and oral mucosa.

DA05.0.title: Developmental odontogenic cysts
DA05.0.definition: Cysts derived from odontogenic (tooth forming) tissue, usually containing fluid or semisolid material, which develop during various stages of odontogenesis.
synonyms: odontogenic developmental cyst of oral cavity
Follicular eruption of cyst of jaw

DA04.5.title: Mucocele of salivary gland
DA04.5.definition: This is a clinical term used to describe a bluish, soft, often fluctuant swelling caused by either blockage or rupture of a salivary gland duct.
synonyms: cyst of salivary gland or duct
Ranula of salivary gland of floor of mouth

DA03.Y.title: Other specified diseases of tongue
synonyms: Atrophy of tongue, not elsewhere classified

DA04.4.title: Sialolithiasis
DA04.4.definition: Sialolithiasis is a condition where a calcified mass forms within a salivary gland, usually in the duct of the submandibular gland. The usual symptoms are pain and swelling of the affected salivary gland, both of which get worse when salivary flow is stimulated.
synonyms: Calculus of salivary gland or duct
Stone of salivary gland or duct
inclusions: Calculus of salivary gland or duct
Stone of salivary gland or duct

DA04.Y.title: Other specified diseases of salivary glands
synonyms: Other specified diseases of salivary glands
Salivary duct obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Acquired deformity of salivary gland or duct

DA01.2Z.title: Granuloma or granuloma-like lesions of oral mucosa, unspecified

DA07.3.title: Disturbances in tooth formation
DA07.3.definition: A group of conditions characterised by disturbances in tooth formation.
exclusions: Hutchinson teeth and mulberry molars in congenital syphilis

DA07.1.title: Nonfluoride enamel opacities
DA07.1.definition: This is a condition characterised by enamel opacities, white spots, or visibly lighter areas on a tooth’s surface, not attributed to fluorine, which occur in low-fluoride areas.

DA07.0.title: Fluoride related opacities or lesions
DA07.0.definition: This is a fluoride related abnormality in the tissue of an organism (in layman's terms, "damage"), usually caused by disease or trauma.

DA06.3.title: Stafne mandibular bone cavity
DA06.3.definition: Although commonly called a Stafne cyst, this entity is not a true cyst but rather a cavity due to a focal cortical defect of the medial aspect of the mandible. It is found most frequently in middle-aged men and is usually discovered radiologically as an incidental finding. Its importance is that it may be difficult to distinguish from other radiolucent lesions in the mandible such as myeloma or metastatic squamous carcinoma. The cavity is usually filled by part of the submandibular salivary gland or adjacent fat and it is thought to result from remodelling of the bone by adjacent salivary tissue. Stafne cysts are most frequently seen in middle-aged men. The estimated prevalence ranges around 0.10-0.48%. Pathology: Stafne cysts are thought to result from remodelling of the bone by adjacent salivary tissue, and have been noted to regress following resection of the gland nearby. They generally appear in the area between the mandibular first molar and the mandibular angle 6.

DA07.4.title: Root anomaly
DA07.4.definition: Common presence of fused roots showed by X-ray film that short or long root, supernumerary root, or fused roots. These root anomalies are commonly seen in permanent molars, especially in third molars which are the most anomaly in one fused root, 2 or 3 fused roots, even 4 fused roots, round apical root or dilacerations.

DA07.7.title: Embedded teeth
DA07.7.definition: an unerupted tooth, usually completely covered with bone
exclusions: embedded teeth with abnormal position of such teeth or adjacent teeth

DA07.61.title: Ankylosis of teeth
DA07.61.definition: Tooth ankylosis is the solid fixation of a tooth, resulting from fusion of the cementum and alveolar bone, with obliteration of the periodontal ligament. It is uncommon in deciduous dentition, and very rare in permanent teeth.
synonyms: failure of exfoliation of primary tooth

DA07.60.title: Teething syndrome
DA07.60.definition: Gum and jaw discomfort when an infant’s teeth emerges. Teething typically starts between 4 and 7 months of age and lasts until about the age of 3 years. Most common symptoms include irritability, crying, lack of appetite, red and swollen gums, drooling, and inability to sleep.

DA07.8.title: Impacted teeth
DA07.8.definition: An impacted tooth is a tooth that is all the way or partially below the gum line and is not able to erupt properly. Wisdom teeth (third molars) are the most commonly impacted teeth
exclusions: impacted teeth with abnormal position of such teeth or adjacent teeth

DA08.0.title: Dental caries
DA08.0.definition: A condition characterised by localised destruction of calcified tissue, initiated on the tooth surface by decalcification of the enamel, followed by the enzymatic lysis of organic structures, resulting in cavity formation.
synonyms: Caries of infancy associated with breast feeding
Caries of infancy associated with bottle feeding

DA08.Y.title: Other specified diseases of hard tissues of teeth
synonyms: Other specified diseases of hard tissues of teeth

DA07.Y.title: Other specified disorders of tooth development or eruption
synonyms: Other specified disorders of tooth development or eruption
Intrinsic staining of teeth, not elsewhere classified

DA07.6Y.title: Other specified disturbances in tooth eruption
synonyms: Other specified disturbances in tooth eruption
Failure of exfoliation associated with lack of succedaneous tooth
Failure of resorption of root of tooth

DA06.2.title: Exostosis of jaw
DA06.2.definition: Formation of bone mass on the vestibular, buccal or facial side of the maxilla or the mandibular jaw where it may affect the lingual aspect; exostoses are more frequent in the maxillary bone.

DA08.11.title: Abrasion of teeth
DA08.11.definition: Abrasion is abnormal tooth surface loss resulting from direct friction forces between the teeth and external objects or from frictional forces between contacting teeth components in the presence of an abrasive medium.

DA08.3.title: Nontraumatic fracture of tooth
DA08.3.definition: Discontinuity of tooth structure in vertical or horizontal direction of the long axis of a tooth and which may affect enamel and/or dentine. This condition is referred as incomplete fracture and may be related to flexural loads acting on the teeth. In some cases the dental pulp may become affected.
synonyms: Incomplete fracture not involving vital pulp
Complete nontraumatic fracture not involving vital pulp
Nontraumatic fracture of tooth involving vital pulp
Nontraumatic fracture of crown of tooth, enamel and dentin, with pulp exposure
Nontraumatic fracture of crown of tooth, enamel only
inclusions: Incomplete fracture not involving vital pulp
Complete nontraumatic fracture not involving vital pulp

DA08.10.title: Excessive attrition of teeth
DA08.10.definition: The pathological wearing away of tooth substance as a result of tooth-to-tooth contact.

DA07.Z.title: Disorders of tooth development or eruption, unspecified
synonyms: Disorders of tooth development or eruption, unspecified
Disorders of tooth development or eruption

DA08.Z.title: Diseases of hard tissues of teeth, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases of hard tissues of teeth, unspecified
Diseases of hard tissues of teeth

DA08.14.title: Pathological resorption of teeth
DA08.14.definition: Tooth resorption, external, resorption of calcified dental tissue, beginning on the external surface, usually at the apex or the lateral surface of the root, as a result of tissue reaction in the periodontal or pericoronal tissue, increasing in severity with age.
synonyms: external resorption of root of tooth

DA08.15.title: Posteruptive colour changes of dental hard tissues
DA08.15.definition: This is a condition characterised by colour changes of the dental hard tissues after tooth eruption.
synonyms: Posteruptive colour changes of dental hard tissues

DA0A.1.title: Loss of teeth due to accident, extraction or local periodontal disease
synonyms: Loss of teeth due to accident, extraction or local periodontal disease
Dental arch length loss due to loss of permanent teeth

DA08.13.title: Abfraction
DA08.13.definition: Theoretical concept of loss of tooth structure not caused by dental caries

DA08.2.title: Chronic dental injuries
DA08.2.definition: A group of conditions characterised by persistent or long-lasting damage caused by an external force applied to the tooth resulting from intentional or unintentional means.

DA08.4.title: Deposits on teeth
DA08.4.definition: In dentistry, calculus or tartar is a form of hardened dental plaque.

DA08.12.title: Erosion of teeth
DA08.12.definition: Tooth erosion is a gradual and irreversible loss of the normally hard surface of the tooth due to chemical, not bacterial, processes.
synonyms: Erosion of teeth due to diet
Erosion of teeth due to drugs or medicaments
Erosion of teeth due to persistent vomiting

DA0C.1.title: Aggressive periodontitis
DA0C.1.definition: A type of periodontal disease and includes localised aggressive periodontitis (LAP), and Generalised aggressive periodontitis (GAP).

DA0A.Y.title: Other specified disorders of teeth and supporting structures
synonyms: Other specified disorders of teeth and supporting structures

DA0A.3.title: Retained dental root
DA0A.3.definition: Complete or fragment of root structure that remains in the jaw usually as result of fracture during the corresponding tooth extraction procedure.

DA0A.0.title: Exfoliation of teeth due to systemic causes
DA0A.0.definition: Premature loss of teeth associated with systemic disease usually results from some change in the immune system or connective tissue.
synonyms: Exfoliation of teeth due to systemic causes

DA0A.Z.title: Unspecified disorders of teeth and supporting structures
synonyms: Unspecified disorders of teeth and supporting structures
Certain specified disorders of teeth or supporting structures
disease of supporting structures of teeth NOS

DA0B.5.title: Developmental or acquired deformities or conditions of gingiva
DA0B.5.definition: This is a major developmental difference in the shape of a body part or organ compared to the average shape of that part.
synonyms: Developmental or acquired deformities or conditions of gingiva

DA0B.Y.title: Other specified gingival diseases
synonyms: Desquamative gingivitis due to known cause classified elsewhere
Desquamative gingivitis of unknown or unspecified cause

DA0B.6.title: Pericoronitis
DA0B.6.definition: A gum condition in which irritation and inflammation are produced by the crown of an incompletely erupted tooth.

DA0C.0.title: Acute periodontitis
DA0C.0.definition: This is an acute disease affecting the tooth-supporting structures, i.e. gingiva, alveolar bone and periodontal membrane.
exclusions: Acute apical periodontitis of pulpal origin

DA0C.2.title: Periodontosis
DA0C.2.definition: Periodontosis defined as a disease of the periodontium occurring in an otherwise healthy adolescent and characterised by a rapid loss of the alveolar bone around more than one tooth of the permanent dentition.

DA0C.Y.title: Other specified periodontal disease
synonyms: Periodontitis as a manifestation of systemic diseases
Periodontal disease complications of diabetes mellitus

DA0C.31.title: Noma
DA0C.31.definition: This is a devastating infectious disease which destroys the soft and hard tissues of the oral and para-oral structures.

DA0C.4.title: Abscess of periodontium
DA0C.4.definition: localised purulent infection of periodontal tissues; common clinical feature in patients with moderate or advanced periodontitis.

DA0D.1.title: Gingival enlargement
DA0D.1.definition: An abnormal overgrowth of gingival tissues.
synonyms: hypertrophy of mucous membrane of gums

DA0D.3.title: Hypoplasminogenaemia
DA0D.3.definition: Severe hypoplasminogenaemia or type 1 plasminogen (plg) deficiency is a systemic disease characterised by markedly impaired extracellular fibrinolysis leading to the formation of ligneous (fibrin-rich) pseudomembranes on mucosae during wound healing.

DA0D.2.title: Gingival or edentulous alveolar ridge lesions associated with trauma
DA0D.2.definition: Damage of gingival or mucosal lesions resulting from external stimuli. Common causes of traumatic ulcers include: denture irritation, biting, injuries, burns and friction irritation from sharp or fractured teeth.
synonyms: Gingival or edentulous alveolar ridge lesions associated with trauma
Hypertrophy of mucous membrane alveolar ridge

DA0E.1.title: Anomalies of jaw-cranial base relationship
DA0E.1.definition: This is a congenital or acquired abnormality in which the portion of the skull that holds the upper jaw deviates from the normal form, function, or position.
synonyms: anomalies of relationship of jaw to cranial base

DA0E.8.title: Temporomandibular joint disorders
DA0E.8.definition: This is an umbrella term covering acute or chronic pain, especially in the muscles of mastication and/or inflammation of the temporomandibular joint, which connects the mandible to the skull.
synonyms: Articular disc disorder of temporomandibular joint
Temporomandibular joint disc displacement, with reduction
Temporomandibular joint disc displacement, without reduction
Undifferentiated inflammatory polyarthritis of temporomandibular joint

DA0E.2.title: Anomalies of dental arch relationship
DA0E.2.definition: This is a congenital or acquired abnormality in which dental arch relationship deviate from normal form, function, or position.
synonyms: unspecified anomaly of dental arch relationship
Posterior lingual occlusion of mandibular teeth

DA0E.51.title: Angle class I malocclusion
DA0E.51.definition: The maxillary first permanent molar is in slight distoversion in relation to the mandibular first permanent molar, and the mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary molar is aligned with the buccal groove of the mandibular molar.

DA20.3Y.title: Other specified perforation of oesophagus
synonyms: superficial injury of thoracic portion of oesophagus

DA0E.3.title: Anomalies of tooth position
DA0E.3.definition: Dental anomalies are craniofacial abnormalities of form, function, or position of the teeth, bones, and tissues of the jaw and mouth. Anomalies of tooth position can be classified in ectopic, transmigration, transposition, rotation.
synonyms: abnormal spacing of tooth or teeth
Impacted or embedded teeth with abnormal position of such teeth or adjacent teeth

DA0D.Y.title: Other specified disorders of gingival or edentulous alveolar ridge
synonyms: Other specified disorders of gingival or edentulous alveolar ridge
Drug-induced swellings of gingival or edentulous alveolar ridge
peripheral giant cell granuloma of gingiva

DA0F.Y.title: Other specified sensory disturbances affecting orofacial complex
synonyms: Other specified sensory disturbances affecting orofacial complex

DA20.1.title: Diverticulum of oesophagus, acquired
DA20.1.definition: Diverticulum of oesophagus is a disorder having out-pouchings from the oesophageal wall.
synonyms: Diverticulum of oesophagus, acquired, with complication
Diverticulum of oesophagus, acquired without complication

DA0F.0.title: Burning mouth syndrome
DA0F.0.definition: Chronic burning mouth pain is chronic orofacial pain with an intraoral burning or dysaesthetic sensation that recurs for more than two hours per day on 50 % of the days over more than three months, without evident causative lesions on clinical investigation and examination. It is characterised by significant emotional distress (anxiety, anger/frustration or depressed mood) or interference with orofacial functions such as eating, yawning, speaking etc. Chronic burning mouth pain is multifactorial: biological, psychological and social factors contribute to the pain condition. The diagnosis is appropriate independently of identified biological or psychological contributors unless another diagnosis would better account for the presenting symptoms.

DA0E.0Y.title: Other specified major anomalies of jaw size
synonyms: Other specified major anomalies of jaw size
Other specified anomalies of jaw size

DA0E.00.title: Micrognathia
DA0E.00.definition: Apparently reduced length and width of the mandible when viewed from the front but not from the side. This is a bundled term comprising shortening and narrowing of the mandible and chin.

DA0Z.title: Diseases or disorders of orofacial complex, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases or disorders of orofacial complex, unspecified
diseases of oral cavity, salivary glands and jaws

DA21.1.title: Motility disorder of cervical or upper oesophagus
DA21.1.definition: Motility disorder of cervical and upper oesophagus is a condition characterised by choke, swallow air, regurgitate fluid into the nose, or experience discomfort in swallowing food due to incompetence of upper oesophageal sphincter.
synonyms: Motility disorder of cervical or upper oesophagus
Dyskinesia of cervical and upper oesophagus
inclusions: Dyskinesia of cervical and upper oesophagus

DA20.0.title: Oesophageal obstruction
DA20.0.definition: Hindrance of the passage of luminal contents in the oesophagus. Obstruction of oesophagus can be partial or complete, and caused by intrinsic or extrinsic factors.
exclusions: Congenital stenosis or stricture of oesophagus
Anatomical alteration due to gastro-oesophageal reflux disease

DA0F.Z.title: Sensory disturbances affecting orofacial complex, unspecified
synonyms: Sensory disturbances affecting orofacial complex, unspecified

DA0E.0Z.title: Major anomalies of jaw size, unspecified
synonyms: Major anomalies of jaw size, unspecified

DA21.20.title: Hypertensive peristalsis
DA21.20.definition: This is a motility disorder of oesophagus characterised by hypertensive peristalsis. This motility abnormality includes nutcracker oesophagus that has been reported in association with dysphagia, non-cardiac chest pain, and heartburn.

DA0E.6.title: Dentofacial functional abnormalities
DA0E.6.definition: Temporomandibular joint disorder (TMJ) is the name given to a group of symptoms that cause pain in the head, face, and jaw. The symptoms include headaches, soreness in the chewing muscles, and clicking or stiffness of the joints. They often have psychological as well as physical causes.
synonyms: Malocclusion due to tongue, lip or finger habits

DA20.30.title: Spontaneous rupture of oesophagus
DA20.30.definition: Spontaneous perforation of the oesophageal wall. This most commonly results from a sudden increase in intraoesophageal pressure combined with relatively negative intrathoracic pressure caused by straining or vomiting. This is known as effort rupture of the oesophagus or Boerhaave's syndrome.

DA21.21.title: Hypotensive peristalsis
DA21.21.definition: This is a motility disorder of oesophagus characterised by hypotensive peristalsis. The peristaltic dysfunction likely leads to impaired volume clearance.

DA20.Y.title: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the oesophagus
synonyms: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the oesophagus

DA0Y.title: Other specified diseases or disorders of orofacial complex
synonyms: Other specified diseases or disorders of orofacial complex
Diseases of teeth, gingiva and dentofacial anomalies
Certain specified diseases or disorders of orofacial complex
Oral focal infection affecting other body systems

DA20.Z.title: Acquired anatomical alterations of the oesophagus, unspecified
synonyms: Acquired anatomical alterations of the oesophagus, unspecified
Acquired anatomical alterations of the oesophagus

DA0E.7.title: Dentofacial parafunctional disorders
DA0E.7.definition: Bruxism is a repetitive jaw-muscle activity characterised by clenching or grinding of the teeth and/or by bracing or thrusting of the mandible. Bruxism has two distinct circadian manifestations: it can occur during sleep (indicated as sleep bruxism) or during wakefulness (indicated as awake bruxism)

DA0E.50.title: Class II division 2 malocclusion
DA0E.50.definition: This condition relates to Angle’s classification of occlusion in which the first permanent maxillary molar position is aligned or in an anterior relationship to that of the mandibular first permanent molar, such that the mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary molar is mesial to the buccal groove of the mandibular molar and the central incisors are in linguoversion.

DA0E.4.title: Food impaction
DA0E.4.definition: The forcible wedging of food between adjacent teeth during mastication, producing gingival recession and pocket formation.

DA20.2.title: Oesophageal web
DA20.2.definition: Oesophageal web is a thin membrane located in the middle or upper oesophagus, resulting in pain and dysphagia.

DA21.22.title: Spastic peristalsis
DA21.22.definition: This is a motility disorder of oesophagus characterised by hypercontractile spastic peristalsis, known as "jackhammer oesophagus" in the presence of normal lower oesophageal sphincter (LES) relaxation. This category also includes diffuse oesophageal spasm (DES) with uncoordinated contraction characterised by reduced distal latency on oesophageal manometry.

DA21.Y.title: Other specified motility disorders of oesophagus
synonyms: Other specified motility disorders of oesophagus
Certain specified motility disorder of oesophagus

DA21.2Y.title: Other specified disorder of oesophageal peristalsis
synonyms: Other specified disorder of oesophageal peristalsis

DA23.0.title: Barrett epithelium
DA23.0.definition: Barrett epithelium is defined as those having circumferential columnar metaplasia of oesophagus from the esophago-gastric junction. Recently, from the view of adeno-carcinogenesis of the oesophagus, the term of Barrett epithelium require the histological confirmation of specialized intestinal metaplasia.

DA24.1.title: Eosinophilic oesophagitis
DA24.1.definition: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is an inflammatory condition in which the wall of the oesophagus becomes filled with a large number of eosinophils. It is diagnosed based on typical oesophageal symptoms and oesophageal mucosal biopsies demonstrating oesophageal epithelial infiltration with eosinophils.

DA23.1.title: Dysplasia of Barrett epithelium
DA23.1.definition: Dysplasia of Barrett epithelium is defined as neoplastic epithelium that remains confined within the basement membrane of Barrett oesophagus. Dysplasia of Barrett epithelium is considered as a precursor of adenocarcinoma arising in Barrett Oesophagus.
synonyms: High grade dysplasia of Barrett epithelium
Low grade dysplasia of Barrett epithelium

DA21.3.title: Disorder of lower oesophageal sphincter function
DA21.3.definition: Disorder of lower oesophageal sphincter function is a condition characterised by dysphagia, chest pain, heartburn and regurgitation due to incompetence of lower oesophageal sphincter.
synonyms: Disorder of lower oesophageal sphincter function
lack of reflex relaxation of lower oesophageal sphincter

DA21.0.title: Achalasia
DA21.0.definition: Achalasia is an oesophageal smooth muscle motility disorder characterised by a loss of peristalsis in the distal oesophagus and a failure of lower oesophageal sphincter (LES) relaxation. Basic mechanism is the degeneration of neurons (ganglion cells) in the myenteric plexuses in the oesophageal wall, but the cause is still unclear.

DA23.Y.title: Other specified columnar metaplastic epithelium of the oesophagus
synonyms: Other specified columnar metaplastic epithelium of the oesophagus

DA23.2.title: Barrett ulcer
DA23.2.definition: Barrett ulcer is defined as ulceration in columnar epithelium of oesophagus.

DA24.20.title: Chemical oesophagitis
DA24.20.definition: This is oesophageal inflammation caused by chemical injury including alkaline or acid solutions.

DA24.21.title: Drug-induced oesophagitis
DA24.21.definition: This refers to a drug-induced inflammation of the oesophagus. Medications can induce oesophageal abnormalities via both systemic effects and by causing direct oesophageal mucosal injury, so-called ‘pill-induced’ oesophagitis.

DA24.00.title: Oesophageal phlegmon
DA24.00.definition: A spreading diffuse inflammatory process with formation of suppurative/purulent exudate or pus in the oesophageal wall. It often develops to a defined pocket of pus, oesophageal abscess. This is mainly due to the result of acute inflammation by bacterial infection.

DA24.Y.title: Other specified oesophagitis
synonyms: Oesophagitis associated with human immunodeficiency virus disease
Oesophagitis due to systemic autoimmune diseases

DA24.2Z.title: Oesophagitis due to external causes, unspecified
synonyms: Oesophagitis due to external causes, unspecified

DA23.Z.title: Columnar metaplastic epithelium of the oesophagus, unspecified
synonyms: Columnar metaplastic epithelium of the oesophagus, unspecified
Columnar metaplastic epithelium of the oesophagus

DA25.3Y.title: Oesophageal ulcer due to other specified external causes
synonyms: Oesophageal ulcer due to other specified external causes
Oesophageal ulcer due to endoscopic procedures
Oesophageal ulcer due to sequelae of endoscopic therapy
Oesophageal ulcer due to foreign body
Oesophageal ulcer due to injury and trauma
Oesophageal ulcer due to prosthetic device

DA25.10.title: Bacterial oesophageal ulcer
DA25.10.definition: Ulcer in the mucosa of oesophagus due to bacterial infection.

DA25.12.title: Parasitic oesophageal ulcer
DA25.12.definition: Ulcer in the mucosa of oesophagus due to parasitic infection.

DA25.2.title: Oesophageal ulcer due to allergic or immunologic disorder
DA25.2.definition: Oesophageal ulcer or erosion due to allergic disorders or systemic immunologic disorders.
synonyms: Oesophageal ulcer due to allergic or immunologic disorder
Oesophageal ulcer due to collagen diseases
Oesophageal ulcer due to eosinophilic disorder

DA25.30.title: Chemical oesophageal ulcer
DA25.30.definition: This is oesophageal ulcer caused by chemical injury including alkaline or acid solutions.
synonyms: Ulcer of oesophagus due to ingestion of chemicals
Ulcer due to ingestion and impaction of button battery cell
inclusions: Ulcer of oesophagus due to ingestion of chemicals

DA26.01.title: Oesophageal varices without bleeding
synonyms: Oesophageal varices without bleeding in diseases classified elsewhere
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in viral hepatic diseases
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in alcoholic liver disease
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in schistosomiasis
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in hepatic fibrosis
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in primary biliary cholangiopathy
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in primary biliary cirrhosis
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in autoimmune hepatitis
Oesophageal varices without bleeding in toxic liver disease

DA25.31.title: Drug-induced oesophageal ulcer
synonyms: Ulcer of oesophagus due to ingestion of drugs and medicaments
inclusions: Ulcer of oesophagus due to ingestion of drugs and medicaments

DA25.3Z.title: Oesophageal ulcer due to external causes, unspecified
synonyms: Oesophageal ulcer due to external causes, unspecified
Oesophageal ulcer due to external causes

DA25.0.title: Oesophageal erosion
DA25.0.definition: Oesophageal erosion represents a mucosal breach extending up to, but not through, the muscularis mucosa. Oesophageal erosion due to gastro-oesophageal reflux disease is excluded from here.

DA40.1.title: Gastric fistula, acquired
DA40.1.definition: Acquired gastric fistula is an opening through the gastric wall and into the peritoneal cavity, into another organ and vessels that normally do not connect, or through the abdominal wall.

DA26.1.title: Angiodysplasia or arteriovenous malformation of oesophagus
DA26.1.definition: Enlarged or widened blood vessels with thin walls that are similar to varicose veins. It can be a source of gastrointestinal bleeding and anaemia.
synonyms: Angiodysplasia or arteriovenous malformation of oesophagus

DA25.11.title: Fungal oesophageal ulcer
DA25.11.definition: Ulcer in the mucosa of oesophagus due to fungal infection.

DA26.0Z.title: Oesophageal varices, unspecified
synonyms: Downhill varices of the oesophagus with bleeding

DA26.Z.title: Vascular disorders of the oesophagus, unspecified
synonyms: Vascular disorders of the oesophagus, unspecified

DA40.Y.title: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the stomach
synonyms: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the stomach

DA26.Y.title: Other specified vascular disorders of the oesophagus
synonyms: Other specified vascular disorders of the oesophagus

DA25.13.title: Viral oesophageal ulcer
DA25.13.definition: Ulcer in the mucosa of oesophagus due to viral infection.

DA40.4.title: Hourglass stricture and stenosis of stomach
DA40.4.definition: This is a structural change of stomach in which one more or less completely divided into two parts, resembling an hourglass in shape, due to often scarring which complicates chronic gastric ulcer.
synonyms: Hourglass stricture and stenosis of stomach

DA40.3.title: Gastric diverticulum
DA40.3.definition: Gastric diverticulum is a disorder having out-pouchings from the gastric wall.

DA40.0.title: Gastric outlet obstruction
DA40.0.definition: Gastric outlet obstruction is a disorder characterised by epigastric abdominal pain and postprandial vomiting due to mechanical obstruction mostly at the level of the pylorus.
synonyms: Gastric stenosis due to other causes

DA26.2.title: Intramural haemorrhage of oesophagus
DA26.2.definition: Hematoma in the oesophageal wall that can be formed spontaneously or as a result of trauma, toxic ingestion, or endoscopic procedures. It is rarely observed.
synonyms: Intramural haemorrhage due to endoscopic procedures
Intramural haemorrhage due to injury or trauma

DA41.1.title: Acute dilatation of stomach
DA41.1.definition: Acute dilatation of stomach is a disorder due to acute enlargement of the gastric cavity by over-distention, resulting in the retention of food and the products of digestion in the stomach.
synonyms: acute postoperative dilatation of the stomach

DA26.3.title: Gastro-oesophageal laceration-haemorrhage syndrome
DA26.3.definition: Bleeding from tears in the mucosa at the junction of the stomach and oesophagus, usually caused by severe vomiting, retching or coughing.

DA25.Y.title: Other specified oesophageal ulcer
synonyms: Oesophageal ulcer due to other diseases classified elsewhere

DA41.2.title: Acid hypersecretion
DA41.2.definition: Acid hypersecretion is a condition due to basal hypersecretion of gastric acid in the stomach, resulting in peptic ulcer and steatorrhoea.

DA40.5.title: Gastroptosis
DA40.5.definition: This is the abnormal downward displacement of the stomach.

DA43.2.title: Arteriovenous malformation of stomach
DA43.2.definition: Arteriovenous malformation is a vascular lesion in which arteries and veins are tangled and not connected by capillaries.

DA40.2.title: Gastric volvulus
DA40.2.definition:
Gastric volvulus is an uncommon clinical entity defined as an abnormal rotation (twisting) of all or part of the stomach by more than 180 degrees, creating a closed-loop obstruction of the flow of material through the stomach. It can result in incarceration and strangulation, with variable loss of blood supply. 
Although rare in childhood, a wandering spleen may also be associated with gastric volvulus, because they share a common etiology: congenital absence of intraperitoneal visceral attachments.

DA41.Y.title: Other specified gastroduodenal motor or secretory disorders
synonyms: Other specified gastroduodenal motor or secretory disorders
Certain specified gastroduodenal motility or secretory disorders

DA41.00.title: Gastroparesis
DA41.00.definition: Gastroparesis is a disorder in which the stomach takes too long to empty its contents principally due to malfunction of vagus nerve.

DA43.0.title: Gastric varices
DA43.0.definition: Abnormally dilated veins developed as portosystemic shunts in the lining of stomach (fundus and/or cardia) in patients with portal hypertension. Once gastric varices develop, they continue to grow, and bleeding from gastric varices can be fatal.

DA26.00.title: Oesophageal varices with bleeding
synonyms: Oesophageal varices with bleeding in diseases classified elsewhere
Oesophageal varices with bleeding in schistosomiasis
Oesophageal varices with bleeding in liver disorders
Oesophageal varices with bleeding in viral hepatic disease
Oesophageal varices with bleeding in autoimmune hepatitis

DA41.Z.title: Gastroduodenal motor or secretory disorders, unspecified
synonyms: Gastroduodenal motor or secretory disorders, unspecified

DA41.3.title: Achlorhydria
DA41.3.definition: Achlorhydria is a condition due to the absence of gastric acid in the stomach, resulting in indigestion and malabsorption.

DA40.Z.title: Acquired anatomical alterations of the stomach, unspecified
synonyms: Acquired anatomical alterations of the stomach, unspecified
Acquired anatomical alterations of the stomach

DA43.1.title: Angiodysplasia of stomach
DA43.1.definition: Small vascular malformation of the stomach. Most lesions are less than 10mm in size and often observed in multiple sites. It can be a source of gastrointestinal bleeding and anaemia.

DA51.4Z.title: Duodenitis of unknown aetiology with specific endoscopic or pathologic features, unspecified
synonyms: Duodenitis of unknown aetiology with specific endoscopic or pathologic features, unspecified
Duodenitis of unknown aetiology with specific endoscopic or pathologic features

DA51.2.title: Lymphocytic duodenitis
DA51.2.definition: Chronic duodenitis characterised by a dense infiltration of benign lymphocytes into the epithelium and lamina propria. Lymphocytic duodenitis may present early gluten-induced damage.

DA51.40.title: Acute haemorrhagic duodenitis of unknown aetiology
synonyms: Acute haemorrhagic duodenitis of unknown aetiology

DA52.0.title: Duodenal varices
DA52.0.definition: Abnormally dilated veins developed as portosystemic shunts in the lining of duodenum in patients with portal hypertension. Once duodenal varices develop, they continue to grow, and bleeding from duodenal varices can be fatal.

DA51.60.title: Duodenal phlegmon
DA51.60.definition: A spreading diffuse inflammatory process with formation of suppurative/purulent exudate or pus in the duodenal wall. It often develops to a defined pocket of pus, duodenal abscess. This is mainly due to the result of acute inflammation by bacterial infection.

DA51.41.title: Granulomatous duodenitis of unknown aetiology
DA51.41.definition: A rare disease characterised by the presence of granulomas within the duodenal mucosa or submucosa. Common causes are Crohn’s disease (CD), disseminated sarcoidosis and infections (tuberculosis [TB], syphilis, fungal).

DA51.5Y.title: Duodenitis due to other specified external causes
synonyms: Duodenitis due to other specified external causes

DA51.51.title: Drug-induced duodenitis
DA51.51.definition: Acute or chronic duodenitis induced by taking some known duodenal mucosal damaged agents such as NSAIDs and aspirin.

DA43.4.title: Diffuse vascular ectasia of stomach
DA43.4.definition: Tortuous dilated blood vessels in the pyloric antrum radiating outward from the pylorus (so-called watermelon stomach). It may cause both acute and chronic gastrointestinal haemorrhage.

DA51.5Z.title: Duodenitis due to external causes, unspecified
synonyms: Duodenitis due to external causes, unspecified

DA51.50.title: Alcoholic duodenitis
synonyms: Inflammation of the duodenal mucosa due to alcohol use
inclusions: Inflammation of the duodenal mucosa due to alcohol use

DA44.0.title: Hyperplastic polyp of stomach
DA44.0.definition: Due to over growth of gastric foveolar epithelial cells. The histological background of hyperplastic polyp is atrophic gastritis, mostly caused by long-term H. pylori infection.

DA43.Z.title: Vascular disorders of the stomach, unspecified
synonyms: Vascular disorders of the stomach, unspecified

DA51.Y.title: Other specified duodenitis
synonyms: Duodenitis due to diseases classified elsewhere

DA50.1.title: Diverticulum of duodenum
DA50.1.definition: Diverticulum of duodenum is a disorder having out-pouchings from the duodenal wall.

DA50.3.title: Deformity of duodenum, acquired
DA50.3.definition: Changes of duodenum in response to the influence by duodenal disease, compression of other organs around the duodenum.

DA43.Y.title: Other specified vascular disorders of the stomach
synonyms: Other specified vascular disorders of the stomach
Other or unspecified vascular disorders of the stomach

DA50.0.title: Obstruction of duodenum
DA50.0.definition: Hindrance of the passage of luminal contents in the duodenum. Obstruction of duodenum can be partial or complete, and caused by intrinsic or extrinsic factors. Simple obstruction is associated with diminished or stopped flow of luminal contents. Strangulating obstruction is associated with impaired blood flow to the duodenum in addition to obstructed flow of luminal contents.
synonyms: Vascular compression of third duodenum, acquired

DA44.1.title: Fundic gland polyp of stomach
DA44.1.definition: Due to hyperplasia of fundic gland cells. Fundic polyp rises on fundic gland area without atrophic gastritis. Most cases show H. pylori negative.

DA44.2.title: Hamartomatous polyp of stomach
DA44.2.definition: Formed of dilated oxyntic glands and irregularly deformed oxyntic glands histologically. Most of them are located in the gastric body or the fundus.

DA50.Y.title: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the duodenum
synonyms: Other specified acquired anatomical alterations of the duodenum

DA50.Z.title: Acquired anatomical alterations of the duodenum, unspecified
synonyms: Acquired anatomical alterations of the duodenum, unspecified
Acquired anatomical alterations of the duodenum

DA50.2.title: Fistula of duodenum
DA50.2.definition: Fistula of duodenum is an opening through the duodenal wall and into the peritoneal cavity, into another organ and vessels that normally do not connect, or through the abdominal wall.

DA43.3.title: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
DA43.3.definition: Changes in the mucosa of the stomach in patients with portal hypertension; by far the most common cause of this is cirrhosis of the liver.

DA51.1.title: Eosinophilic duodenitis
DA51.1.definition: A disease characterised by eosinophilic infiltration of various layers of duodenum in the absence of any known cause of eosinophilia.

DA51.0.title: Helicobacter-pylori associated duodenitis
DA51.0.definition: Duodenitis with Helicobacter pylori infection. H. pylori can be colonized on gastric metaplasia epithelium at bulb, and induce duodenitis.

DA52.Y.title: Other specified vascular disorders of the duodenum
synonyms: Other specified vascular disorders of the duodenum
Superior mesenteric artery syndrome of duodenum

DA60.3.title: Stress ulcer of stomach
DA60.3.definition: Stress ulcers of stomach are acute mucosal lesions occurring in critically ill patients that may result in acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. They are usually superficial erosions but can develop into ulcers. Stress ulcers of stomach may develop anywhere within the stomach but are more likely to occur in fundic mucosa, which lines the body and fundus of the stomach.

DA60.5.title: Lymphocytic gastric ulcer
DA60.5.definition: Gastric ulcer caused by lymphocytic gastritis.

DA53.0.title: Hyperplastic duodenal polyp
DA53.0.definition: Due to overgrowth of gastric foveolar type epithelial cells in duodenum.

DA60.1.title: Helicobacter pylori associated gastric ulcer
DA60.1.definition: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a gram-negative bacillus that is found in the mucous layer overlying gastric epithelium, within epithelial cells and attached to mucous cells, leading to inflammation. It accounts for the majority of gastric ulcer. H. pylori that involves the acid-producing mucosa of the stomach can lead to hypochlorhydria or achlorhydria, and subsequent gastric ulceration.
exclusions: Helicobacter pylori associated and drug-induced gastric ulcer

DA52.Z.title: Vascular disorders of the duodenum, unspecified
synonyms: Vascular disorders of the duodenum, unspecified

DA60.0.title: Gastric erosion
DA60.0.definition: Gastric erosion represents a mucosal breach extending up to, but not through, the muscularis mucosa. Gastric erosion may constitute a phase of ulcer development or accompany some forms of gastric ulcer.

DA52.2.title: Arteriovenous malformation of duodenum
DA52.2.definition: Arteriovenous malformation is a vascular lesion in which arteries and veins are tangled and not connected by capillaries. Dilated weak-walled blood vessels in the duodenum usually close to the inside surface. They appear as very red areas, and tend to bleed easily with minimal trauma.

DA60.4.title: Eosinophilic gastric ulcer
DA60.4.definition: Gastric ulcer caused by eosinophilic gastritis.

DA52.1.title: Angiodysplasia of duodenum
DA52.1.definition: Ectasia of duodenal submucosal veins and overlying mucosal capillaries. Most lesions are less than 10mm in size, and multiple lesions are frequent. On endoscopy, flat or slightly elevated, reddish, roundish or starry lesions are observed.

DA60.2.title: Helicobacter pylori associated and drug-induced gastric ulcer
synonyms: Helicobacter pylori associated and drug-induced gastric ulcer

DA62.0.title: Anastomotic erosion
DA62.0.definition: Anastomotic erosion represents a mucosal breach extending up to, but not through, the muscularis mucosa. Anastomotic erosion may constitute a phase of ulcer development or accompany some forms of anastomotic ulcer.

DA60.62.title: Drug-induced gastric ulcer
DA60.62.definition: Medications such as NSAIDs can cause gastric ulcer. Other drugs that may increase the risk of ulceration include potassium chloride, concomitant use of steroids with NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, and mycophenolate mofetil.
synonyms: Ulcer of the stomach due to NSAID - [non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug]
exclusions: Helicobacter pylori associated and drug-induced gastric ulcer

DA60.6Z.title: Gastric ulcer due to external causes, unspecified
synonyms: Gastric ulcer due to external causes, unspecified
Gastric ulcer due to external causes

DA63.0.title: Duodenal erosion
DA63.0.definition: Duodenal erosion represents a mucosal breach extending up to, but not through, the muscularis mucosa. Duodenal erosion may constitute a phase of ulcer development or accompany some forms of duodenal ulcer.

DA62.Y.title: Other specified anastomotic ulcer
synonyms: Anastomotic ulcer due to diseases classified elsewhere
Anastomotic ulcer due to Crohn disease
Anastomotic ulcer due to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
Anastomotic ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without complication
gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without haemorrhage or perforation

DA62.2.title: Drug-induced anastomotic ulcer
DA62.2.definition: Drug-induced anastomotic ulcer is an ulcer at the anastomosis that is caused by drug ingestion. NSAID is considered as one of the risk factors for anastomotic ulcer.

DA63.3.title: Stress ulcer of duodenum
DA63.3.definition: Stress ulcers of duodenum are acute mucosal lesions occurring in critically ill patients that may result in acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. They are usually superficial erosions but can develop into ulcers.

DA62.3.title: Peptic anastomotic ulcer
DA62.3.definition: Anastomotic ulcer, peptic is an ulcer resulting from the effects of gastric acid on the susceptible intestinal mucosa.

DA63.2.title: Helicobacter-pylori associated and drug-induced duodenal ulcer
synonyms: Helicobacter-pylori associated and drug-induced duodenal ulcer

DA60.Y.title: Other specified gastric ulcer
synonyms: Gastric ulcer due to diseases classified elsewhere

Gastric ulcer due to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome

DA60.6Y.title: Other specified gastric ulcer due to external causes
synonyms: Other specified gastric ulcer due to external causes

DA63.60.title: Bacterial duodenal ulcer
DA63.60.definition: Duodenal ulcer caused by infection with bacteria. This includes mycobacterium, Treponema pallidum (syphilis bacterium) and other bacterial infections in the duodenum.
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to bacterial infections

DA63.1.title: Helicobacter-pylori associated duodenal ulcer
DA63.1.definition: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a gram-negative bacillus that is found in the mucous layer overlying gastric epithelium, within epithelial cells and attached to mucous cells, leading to inflammation. In the case of duodenal ulcers, H. pylori is believed to infect the gastric antrum or ectopic gastric mucosa in the duodenum. This is associated with increased acid production and duodenal ulceration.

DA60.7.title: Infectious secondary gastric ulcer
DA60.7.definition: Gastric ulcer due to infectious diseases other than Helicobacter pylori, such as bacteria such as mycobacterium, virus, fungus and parasites.
synonyms: Gastric ulcer due to infectious diseases classified elsewhere
Gastric ulcer due to bacterial infections
Gastric ulcer due to viral infections
Gastric ulcer due to fungal infections
Gastric ulcer due to parasitic infections

DA63.4.title: Eosinophilic duodenal ulcer
DA63.4.definition: Duodenal ulcer caused by eosinophilic duodenitis

DA62.1.title: Helicobacter pylori associated anastomotic ulcer
DA62.1.definition: Helicobacter pylori associated anastomotic ulcer is an ulcer at the anastomosis that is associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. Helicobacter pylori infection is considered as one of the risk factors for anastomotic ulcer.

DA63.61.title: Viral duodenal ulcer
DA63.61.definition: Duodenal ulcer caused by infection with virus. Infectious diseases such as cytomegalovirus and herpes simplex virus are often associated with duodenal ulcer.
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to viral infections

DA90.1.title: Congenital intestinal transport defect
DA90.1.definition: This is a congenital disease of the small intestinal mucosa that presents with intractable diarrhoea and malabsorption of nutrients in young children, due to defect of transporter of nutrients in enterocytes.

DA7Z.title: Diseases of the stomach or the duodenum, unspecified
synonyms: Diseases of the stomach or the duodenum, unspecified

DA63.5Y.title: Duodenal ulcer due to other specified external causes
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to other specified external causes

DA63.6Z.title: Infectious duodenal ulcer, unspecified

DA63.5Z.title: Duodenal ulcer due to external causes, unspecified

Duodenal ulcer due to external causes

Congenital malabsorptive diarrhoea due to paucity of enteroendocrine cells
Intractable diarrhoea - choanal atresia - eye anomalies
Other specified congenital enteropathy involving intestinal mucosa development
Congenital intestinal disease due to an enzymatic defect

DA63.Y.title: Other specified duodenal ulcer
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to diseases classified elsewhere
Duodenal ulcer due to coeliac disease
Duodenal ulcer due to Crohn disease

Duodenal ulcer due to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome

DA63.62.title: Fungal duodenal ulcer
DA63.62.definition: Duodenal ulcer caused by infection with fungus. This includes infection with candida and other fungal infections in the duodenum.
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to fungal infections

DA90.2.title: Congenital intestinal motility disorders
DA90.2.definition: This is a congenital disorder of the small intestinal intestine that presents severe impairment or change of bowel movement often associated with malabsorption of nutrients in young children.
synonyms: Intestinal Congenital motility disorders due to mitochondrial disease

DA63.50.title: Drug-induced duodenal ulcer
DA63.50.definition: Medications such as NSAIDs can cause duodenal ulcer. Other drugs that may increase the risk of ulceration include potassium chloride, concomitant use of steroids with NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, and mycophenolate mofetil.
synonyms: Duodenal ulcer due to NSAID - [non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug]

DA91.3Y.title: Other specified obstructive ileus of small intestine due to impaction
synonyms: Other specified obstructive ileus of small intestine due to impaction

DA91.Y.title: Other specified obstruction of small intestine
synonyms: Other specified obstruction of small intestine
Obstruction of small intestine due to compression or stenosis

DA90.Z.title: Nonstructural developmental anomalies of small intestine, unspecified
synonyms: Nonstructural developmental anomalies of small intestine, unspecified
Nonstructural developmental anomalies of small intestine

DA92.0.title: Fistula of small intestine
DA92.0.definition: A small intestinal fistula is defined as an abnormal communication between the small intestine and another epithelialized surface such as the skin or an adjacent loop of bowel.

DA91.2.title: Intestinal adhesions or bands of small intestine with obstruction
DA91.2.definition: Small bowel obstruction resulting from intraabdominal adhesion due to laparotomy, trauma, and intraabdominal inflammation such as endometriosis.
synonyms: Intestinal adhesions or bands of small intestine with obstruction
Postoperative obstruction of the small intestine

DA90.0.title: Syndromic diarrhoea
DA90.0.definition: Syndromic diarrhoea (SD), also known as phenotypic diarrhoea (PD) or tricho-hepato-enteric syndrome (THE), is a congenital enteropathy presenting with early-onset of severe diarrhoea requiring parenteral nutrition (PN), associated with facial dysmorphism, woolly and poorly pigmented hair and liver disease, with extensive fibrosis or cirrhosis, in about half of the patients.

DA92.1.title: Pneumatosis intestinalis of small intestine
DA92.1.definition: Pneumatosis intestinalis is a rare condition characterised by multiple, gas-filled cysts, typically within the subserosa and submucosa of the small intestine.

DA91.0.title: Intussusception of small intestine
DA91.0.definition: Intussusception occurs when a segment of bowel invaginates, or telescopes, into adjacent distal bowel, leading to obstruction and possibly ischemic injury.

DA91.3Z.title: Obstructive ileus of small intestine due to impaction, unspecified
synonyms: Obstructive ileus of small intestine due to impaction, unspecified
Obstructive ileus of small intestine due to impaction

DA91.1.title: Volvulus of small intestine
DA91.1.definition: A volvulus is an abnormal twisting of the intestine around the axis of its own mesentery, resulting in obstruction of the more proximal bowel. Twisting of the mesentery may involve the mesenteric vessels and so make the involved loop particularly susceptible to strangulation and gangrene, with resulting perforation, peritonitis, and sepsis.

DA91.31.title: Enterolith of small intestine
DA91.31.definition: This is a mineral concretion or calculus formed anywhere in the gastrointestinal system, but in this case the small intestine.

DA91.30.title: Gallstone ileus of small intestine
DA91.30.definition: Small bowel obstruction due to stenosis resulting from impaction of gallstones.

DA94.2Y.title: Other specified allergic or dietetic enteritis of small intestine
synonyms: Other specified allergic or dietetic enteritis of small intestine
Allergic enteritis due to food hypersensitivity

DA94.22.title: Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome
DA94.22.definition: A non-IgE-mediated intestinal hypersensitivity cell-mediated persistent chronic inflammation of the enteric tract which primarily affects children. The most common causal foods are: cow’s milk, soy, rice, oat, meat. In cases of chronic exposure, the most frequent symptoms are emesis, diarrhoea, poor growth and lethargy. In cases of re-exposure after restriction, the patient can present emesis, diarrhoea, hypotension (15%) 2 hours after ingestion.

DA94.00.title: Primary nonspecific ulceration of small intestine
DA94.00.definition: Primary or simple ulcer of the small intestine occurring beyond the duodenum is rare. The lesion includes single ulcers within the jejunum and ileum of unknown etiology. Non-specific ulcer accompanied with Behcet disease is classified elsewhere in EGD.
synonyms: Primary nonspecific ulceration of small intestine

DA94.3Z.title: Enteritis or ulcer of small intestine due to other external causes, unspecified
synonyms: Enteritis or ulcer of small intestine due to other external causes, unspecified
Enteritis or ulcer of small intestine due to other external causes
Enteritis and ulcer of small intestine due to endoscopic procedures

DA96.02.title: Malabsorption or intolerance of specific nutrients
DA96.02.definition: Food intolerance is a term used for difficulty in digesting a food due to various physiological responses associated with a particular food, or compound found. Food intolerance should not be mistaken for food allergy, which is primarily involving the immune reaction against the food.
synonyms: Malabsorption or intolerance of specific nutrients
Malabsorption due to intolerance to carbohydrate
Malabsorption due to intolerance to fat
Malabsorption due to intolerance to protein
Intestinal disease due to vitamin absorption anomaly
Malabsorption due to intolerance, not elsewhere classified
Malabsorption due to intolerance to of starch

DA94.31.title: Enteritis or ulcer of small intestine due to radiation
synonyms: Enteritis or ulcer of small intestine due to radiation

DA96.05.title: Intestinal failure
DA96.05.definition: The reduction of gut function below the minimum necessary for the absorption of macronutrients and/or water and electrolytes, such that intravenous supplementation is required to maintain health and/or growth.

DA94.2Z.title: Allergic or dietetic enteritis of small intestine, unspecified
synonyms: Allergic or dietetic enteritis of small intestine, unspecified
Allergic or dietetic enteritis of small intestine

DA96.0Y.title: Other specified intestinal malabsorption
synonyms: Structural enterocyte defects due to other diseases
