transitory disorder of potassium balance in newborn

KB63.30.title: Hypokalaemia of newborn
KB63.30.definition: Hypokalaemia is defined as serum potassium less than 3.5 mmol/L.

KB6Z.title: Transitory endocrine or metabolic disorders specific to fetus or newborn, unspecified
synonyms: Transitory endocrine or metabolic disorders specific to fetus or newborn, unspecified

KB63.5.title: Metabolic bone disease of prematurity
KB63.5.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by bone abnormalities in a newborn due to abnormalities of minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, magnesium or vitamin D associated with the child being born prior to completing 37 weeks of gestation.

KB81.0.title: Neonatal eosinophilic oesophagitis
KB81.0.definition: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is an inflammatory condition, possibly caused by food allergy, in which the wall of the oesophagus becomes filled with a large number of eosinophils. It can be confused with acid reflux disease but it can be differentiated if neonate does not respond to anti-reflux medications.

KB80.title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease in newborn
KB80.definition: A condition which develops when the reflux of stomach contents causes the newborn to vomit with associated discomfort, difficulty feeding and/or weight loss.

KB63.4.title: Transitory tyrosinaemia of newborn
KB63.4.definition: Clinically asymptomatic elevated blood tyrosine level caused by late fetal maturation of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase, usually detected on newborn bloodspot screening. Most commonly seen in premature infants receiving milk formulae with high protein content. Generally considered benign and resolves by 4-6 weeks of age.

KB82.title: Prenatal gastric perforation
KB82.definition: Prenatal gastric perforation is a perforation or hole of the wall of the stomach that occurs while the baby is in utero. This is a rare and life-threatening condition in a neonate.

KB64.title: Transitory neonatal hypoparathyroidism
KB64.definition: Defined as hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphatemia and low serum parathyroid hormone that improves spontaneously but may last from weeks to months.

KB63.31.title: Hyperkalaemia of newborn
KB63.31.definition: Hyperkalaemia is defined as serum potassium greater than 5.5 mmol/L.

KB83.title: Postnatal gastric perforation
KB83.definition: Postnatal gastric perforation is a spontaneous or traumatic penetration or hole of the wall of the stomach that occurs after birth. This is a rare and life-threatening condition in a neonate.

KB84.title: Postnatal isolated ileal perforation
KB84.definition: Post natal bowel perforation, generally in the terminal ileum. Can be confused with necrotizing enterocolitis, but generally occurs earlier (2-5 days of age) and does not involve extensive bowel necrosis.

KB85.1.title: Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation due to intestinal atresia or stenosis
synonyms: Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation due to intestinal atresia or stenosis
Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to intestinal atresia or stenosis

Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to intraluminal obstruction

Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to in utero volvulus

KB86.1.title: Postnatal intestinal perforation due to in utero volvulus
synonyms: Postnatal intestinal perforation due to in utero volvulus
Postnatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to in utero volvulus

KB87.0.title: Intestinal obstruction due to inspissated milk
KB87.0.definition: Mechanical intestinal obstruction in premature infants due to hard milk curds formed when high-energy formula or powdered milk is fed in the presence of reduced intestinal motility and increased absorption of water from the colon. The site of obstruction is the terminal ileum, the ileocaecal valve, or the colon. The manifestations include constipation, abdominal distension, and vomiting (progressively bilious or faecal).
synonyms: Intestinal obstruction due to inspissated milk

Postnatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to drugs

Postnatal intrauterine intestinal perforation secondary to intestinal atresia or stenosis

KB86.Z.title: Postnatal intestinal perforation, unspecified

KB87.3.title: Transitory ileus of newborn
KB87.3.definition: Transient intestinal obstruction of functional rather than anatomical origin which is not uncommon in the first few days of life. As surgery may be strongly contraindicated in this group, the differential diagnosis is extremely important.

KB87.1.title: Meconium plug without ileus
KB87.1.definition: Meconium plug, also referred to as functional immaturity of the colon, is an obstruction in the newborn colon. It is usually a transient disorder of the newborn and is characterised by delayed passage of meconium and intestinal dilatation.
synonyms: meconium obstruction in fetus or newborn

KB87.2.title: Meconium ileus without perforation
KB87.2.definition: The meconium sometimes becomes thickened and congested in the terminal ileum, a condition known as meconium ileus. Meconium ileus is among the most common causes of intestinal obstruction in the newborn, accounting for 9-33% of neonatal intestinal obstructions. A symptom of both Hirschsprung’s disease and cystic fibrosis is the failure to pass meconium. Some babies have a blockage in their colon that may look like meconium ileus (a meconium plug), and they have small left colon syndrome. This means the last part of their colon is smaller than normal.

KB87.4.title: Meconium ileus with perforation
KB87.4.definition: Complicated meconium ileus with bowel perforation with varying degrees of meconium peritonitis.

KB86.3.title: Postnatal intestinal perforation due to intraluminal obstruction
synonyms: Postnatal intestinal perforation due to intraluminal obstruction
Postnatal intestinal perforation secondary to intraluminal obstruction

synonyms: Other specified necrotising enterocolitis of newborn

KB89.1.title: Short bowel syndrome in neonate
KB89.1.definition: Short bowel syndrome in neonate is a condition originating in the perinatal period in which nutrients are not properly absorbed due to either surgical removal of a large portion of the small intestine or rarely due to the complete dysfunction of a large segment of small intestine.

KB8A.title: Neonatal haematemesis or melaena due to swallowed maternal blood
KB8A.definition: A less serious, self-limiting case of haematemesis and melena which can occur in newborns two to three days after delivery, due to swallowed maternal blood.
synonyms: Neonatal haematemesis or melaena due to swallowed maternal blood

KB89.0.title: Neonatal malabsorption due to endocrine secreting tumour
synonyms: Neonatal malabsorption due to endocrine secreting tumour
Neonatal malabsorption secondary to endocrine secreting tumour

KB89.Y.title: Other specified neonatal malabsorption syndromes

KB88.Z.title: Necrotising enterocolitis of newborn, unspecified
synonyms: necrotising enterocolitis of fetus and newborn
necrotizing enterocolitis in fetus or newborn
necrotising enterocolitis in fetus or newborn

KB8C.title: Noninfectious neonatal diarrhoea
KB8C.definition: Non-infectious causes of diarrhoea in neonates. Childhood diarrhoea is most often caused by infection. Much less often, however, it is due to other causes - e.g., malabsorption or dietary intolerance, endocrine abnormalities, hormone-secreting tumours, pancreatic and liver dysfunction. Non-infectious causes of diarrhoea may have other systemic signs and symptoms. Neonates are at particular risk of dehydration and malnutrition.

KB8B.title: Neonatal peritonitis
KB8B.definition: Neonatal peritonitis may be bacterial or chemical in origin. The majority of cases of bacterial peritonitis are due to intestinal perforations, ruptured omphaloceles, or ischemic intestinal necrosis. Although most babies had peritonitis secondary to intestinal perforation subsequent to intestinal obstruction, many instances are unexplained perforation, possibly secondary to defects in the intestinal musculature or visceral ischemia. The less common chemical peritonitis is due to prenatal intestinal perforation with extrusion of sterile meconium into the peritoneal cavity. The two types may coexist if an antenatal perforation remains open after birth, allowing bacterial contamination of the previously sterile peritoneum.

KB8Y.title: Other specified digestive system disorders of fetus or newborn
synonyms: Other specified digestive system disorders of fetus or newborn

KB8Z.title: Digestive system disorders of fetus or newborn, unspecified
synonyms: Digestive system disorders of fetus or newborn, unspecified

KC0Z.title: Genitourinary system disorders specific to the perinatal or neonatal period, unspecified
synonyms: Genitourinary system disorders specific to the perinatal or neonatal period, unspecified

KC00.title: Congenital hydrocele
KC00.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the buildup of watery fluid around one or both testicles of a newborn that is present at birth.

KC20.1.title: Umbilical cutis or polyp of newborn
KC20.1.definition: An umbilical cord polyp is a congenital lesion resulting from persistence of the omphalomesenteric duct. It originates from either the omphalomesenteric duct or from urachal remnants. The polyp may contain intestinal mucosa.
synonyms: Umbilical cutis or polyp of newborn

KC01.title: Congenital renal failure
KC01.definition: A severe irreversible decline in the ability of kidneys to remove wastes, concentrate urine, and maintain electrolyte balance; blood pressure; and calcium metabolism which existed at, or often before, birth.

KC22.0.title: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn
synonyms: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn
exclusions: Subcutaneous fat necrosis due to birth injury

KC20.Y.title: Other specified conditions involving the umbilical cord
synonyms: Other specified conditions involving the umbilical cord

KC21.1.title: Neonatal toxic erythema
KC21.1.definition: Neonatal toxic erythema is a common rash in neonates, appearing in up to half of newborns carried to term, usually between day 2-5 after birth; it does not occur outside the neonatal period and typically resolves within first two weeks of life. It is characterised by blotchy erythema with crops of evanescent small white or yellow papules or pustules. It is a benign condition and is thought to cause no discomfort to the baby.

KC21.Y.title: Other specified inflammatory dermatoses of the newborn
synonyms: Other specified inflammatory dermatoses of the newborn
Down syndrome leukemoid reaction-associated transient neonatal pustulosis

KC22.2.title: Sclerema neonatorum
KC22.2.definition: Sclerema neonatorum is an uncommon condition which typically affects gravely ill, preterm neonates in the first week of life. It manifests as a diffuse hardening of skin and subcutaneous adipose tissue such that the skin cannot be pitted or picked up and pinched into a fold. Histologically there is minimal inflammation without fat necrosis. It is associated with a high mortality.

KC20.Z.title: Conditions involving the umbilical cord, unspecified
synonyms: Conditions involving the umbilical cord, unspecified

KC21.2.title: Perianal dermatitis of the newborn
KC21.2.definition: Perianal dermatitis of the newborn presents with perianal erythema during the first week of life, which in more severe forms may progress to oedema and superficial erosion of perianal skin. Although it usually occurs alone, perianal dermatitis may sometimes be associated with primary irritant napkin dermatitis. It is commoner in infants receiving cow's milk formulations than in breast-fed infants; it is assumed that it represents an irritant response to faecal constituents.

KC22.1.title: Cold panniculitis of the newborn
KC22.1.definition: Cold panniculitis resulting either from exposure of neonates to low environmental temperature or from local application of cold objects (e.g. ice packs for management of neonatal supraventricular tachycardia). The newborn are particularly susceptible as a result of a high saturated/unsaturated fat ratio in subcutaneous fat with a consequent elevation of the freezing point of fat.

KC21.Z.title: Inflammatory dermatoses of the newborn, unspecified

KC22.Y.title: Other specified neonatal disorders of subcutaneous fat
synonyms: Other specified neonatal disorders of subcutaneous fat

KC21.0.title: Neonatal acne
KC21.0.definition: Acne presenting at birth or shortly afterwards, generally with predominantly comedonal lesions of the cheeks and a paucity of inflammatory lesions. It is thought to be due to hyperactivity of the sebaceous glands stimulated by neonatal androgens from the testes in boys and adrenals in girls.

KC23.title: Neonatal disorders of the oral mucosa
synonyms: Neonatal disorders of the oral mucosa
Dental lamina cyst of the newborn

KC0Y.title: Other specified genitourinary system disorders specific to the perinatal or neonatal period
synonyms: Other specified genitourinary system disorders specific to the perinatal or neonatal period

KC24.title: Neonatal nutritional disorders affecting the skin
KC24.definition: A range of nutritional disorders presenting in the neonatal period with skin manifestations. They may result from inadequate maternal nutrition or from problems with neonatal absorption of minerals such as zinc.
synonyms: Neonatal nutritional disorders affecting the skin
Neonatal macronutrient deficiency affecting the skin
Neonatal marasmus due to fetal malnutrition

Skin manifestation of other specified neonatal mineral deficiency

KC3Y.title: Other specified skin disorders associated with prematurity
synonyms: Other specified skin disorders associated with prematurity

KC22.Z.title: Neonatal disorders of subcutaneous fat, unspecified
synonyms: Neonatal disorders of subcutaneous fat, unspecified

KC31.title: Congenital erosive or vesicular dermatosis healing with reticulated supple scarring
KC31.definition: A rare condition reported principally in premature neonates characterised by extensive erosions, vesicles, ulcerations and crusts affecting up to 75% of the body surface. The cause is unknown and the skin heals rapidly leaving faint reticulate scars.
synonyms: Congenital erosive or vesicular dermatosis healing with reticulated supple scarring

KC41.0.title: Breast engorgement of newborn
KC41.0.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the painful overfilling of the breasts of a newborn with milk.
synonyms: breast hypertrophy in fetus or newborn

KC50.title: Neonatal phototherapy burn
KC50.definition: Burn resulting from phototherapy administered to neonate, usually for the treatment of neonatal jaundice.

KC9Z.title: Disorders involving the integument of fetus or newborn, unspecified
synonyms: Disorders involving the integument of fetus or newborn, unspecified

KD10.title: Environmental hyperthermia of newborn
KD10.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a core body temperature above 37.5 degrees C (99.5 degrees F) in a newborn due to exposure of the newborn to prolonged or extremely high environmental temperature.

KC41.Y.title: Other specified conditions of integument specific to fetus and newborn
synonyms: Other specified conditions of integument specific to fetus and newborn
Other and unspecified oedema specific to fetus and newborn

KC41.1.title: Hydrops fetalis not due to haemolytic disease
KC41.1.definition: A fetal condition characterised by an accumulation of fluid or oedema in at least two fetal compartments, including subcutaneous compartments, the pleura, the pericardium, or the abdomen that is not due to the breakdown of red blood cells.
synonyms: Hydrops fetalis not due to haemolytic disease

KC5Y.title: Other specified postnatal iatrogenic skin injury
synonyms: Other specified postnatal iatrogenic skin injury
Adverse reaction to substance applied to neonatal skin

KC7Y.title: Other specified iatrogenic injuries involving the skin of the neonate
synonyms: Other specified iatrogenic injuries involving the skin of the neonate
Iatrogenic skin injury resulting from antenatal interventions

KD1Y.title: Other specified disturbances of temperature regulation of newborn
synonyms: Other specified disturbances of temperature regulation of newborn

KC40.Y.title: Other specified skin disorders in the neonate
synonyms: Other specified skin disorders in the neonate

KD12.0.title: Neonatal cold injury syndrome
KD12.0.definition: Neonatal cold injury syndrome is characterised by a core body temperature below 35°C (95°F) due to exposure of the newborn to prolonged or extremely low environmental temperatures. Clinically it is characterised by coldness to touch, apathy, immobility, decreased urine output and refusal of food. In addition oedema and redness of the extremities, especially the hands, feet, and face, are observed. It is commonly fatal and survivors may have evidence of brain damage.

KD1Z.title: Disturbances of temperature regulation of newborn, unspecified
synonyms: Disturbances of temperature regulation of newborn, unspecified
temperature regulation disorder, fetus or newborn

KD30.1.title: Birth depression with 5 minute Apgar score 4-6
KD30.1.definition: A condition characterised by cardiorespiratory and neurological depression, defined as an Apgar score between 4 and 6 at 5 minutes following birth.
synonyms: Birth depression with 5 minute Apgar score 4-6

KD30.0.title: Birth depression with 5 minute Apgar score 0-3
KD30.0.definition: A condition characterised by cardiorespiratory and neurological depression, defined as an Apgar score between 0 to 3 at 5 minutes following birth.
synonyms: Birth depression with 5 minute Apgar score 0-3

KD31.title: Wide cranial sutures of newborn
KD31.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally large separation between the bones of the skull of a newborn.

KD30.2.title: Birth depression with associated metabolic acidaemia of cord blood
synonyms: Birth depression with associated metabolic acidaemia of cord blood

KD32.0.title: Slow feeding of newborn
KD32.0.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a newborn who requires more than approximately 45 minutes per feeding.

KD32.Y.title: Other specified feeding problems of newborn
synonyms: Other specified feeding problems of newborn

KD33.title: Jittery baby, not elsewhere classified
KD33.definition: Jitteriness can occur on the first day of life. It can be caused by hypoglycaemia, hypocalcaemia, drug withdrawal, or other conditions.

KD35.title: Neonatal withdrawal syndrome from maternal use of drugs of addiction
KD35.definition: Intrauterine exposure to addictive drugs can lead to neonatal withdrawal symptoms. Withdrawal symptoms are usually neurological, preventing normal autonomic function. The clinical presentation of drug withdrawal is variable and dependent on several factors, such as, the type and dose of drug used and rate of metabolism and excretion of the mother and infant.
synonyms: Neonatal withdrawal syndrome from maternal use of drugs of addiction
Drug withdrawal syndrome in infant of dependent mother
inclusions: Drug withdrawal syndrome in infant of dependent mother
exclusions: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal anaesthesia or analgesia in pregnancy, labour or delivery

KD32.1.title: Underfeeding of newborn
KD32.1.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a newborn who consumes less than average for their age and weight and who seems hungry and unsatisfied after feeding, is fussy or cries a lot, does not produce several wet and soiled diapers each day, and who does not gain weight.

KD34.title: Reactions or intoxications due to drugs administered to fetus or newborn
KD34.definition: A group of paediatric substance-induced conditions associated with health interventions applied to a fetus or newborn using pharmaceutical products.
synonyms: Reactions or intoxications due to drugs administered to fetus or newborn
Grey syndrome from chloramphenicol administration in newborn
exclusions: Withdrawal symptoms from therapeutic use of drugs in newborn
Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to drugs or toxins transmitted from mother
reactions and intoxications from maternal opiates, tranquillizers and other medication
Neonatal withdrawal syndrome from maternal use of drugs of addiction
Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia due to drugs or toxins given to newborn

KD36.title: Withdrawal symptoms from therapeutic use of drugs in newborn
KD36.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the presence of symptoms due to drug withdrawal in a newborn.
synonyms: Withdrawal symptoms from therapeutic use of drugs in newborn

KD37.title: Exposure to tobacco smoke in the perinatal period
KD37.definition: Exposure to tobacco smoke in the perinatal period, both directly or through second hand smoke, can lead to: low birth weight, preterm delivery, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS or cot death), spontaneous abortion, or intrauterine growth retardation.
synonyms: Exposure to tobacco smoke in the perinatal period
exclusions: Fetus or newborn affected by maternal use of tobacco

KD32.2.title: Overfeeding of newborn
KD32.2.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a newborn who consumes too much food and has subsequent excessive vomiting or weight gain beyond normal averages.

KD39.1.title: Fetus or newborn affected by chorionic villous sampling
KD39.1.definition: Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) is a procedure where a small sample of the placenta is removed, either through the cervix or abdomen. Risks when performing CVS include: injury to the fetus or mother from the needle, infection to the mother from a punctured bowel or contaminated skin, or Rhesus sensitisation. Injury or infection can lead to miscarriage, although this is rare.
synonyms: Fetus or newborn affected by chorionic villous sampling

KD32.4.title: Failure to thrive in newborn
KD32.4.definition: When newborn’s current weight or rate of weight gain is significantly below that of other newborns of similar age and gender.

KD39.2.title: Fetus or newborn affected by fetal blood sampling
KD39.2.definition: Fetal blood sampling involves extracting a sample of fetal blood from the umbilical cord using a needle and an ultrasound as a guide. It is used to detect fetal abnormalities and is generally performed after the completion of 18 weeks of gestation. Risks to the fetus and newborn include: miscarriage, bleeding from the needle entry site, uterine infection and temporary slowing of the baby’s heart rate following the procedure.
synonyms: Fetus or newborn affected by fetal blood sampling
Fetus or newborn affected by cordocentesis
Fetus or newborn affected by accidental damage during fetal blood sampling
inclusions: Fetus or newborn affected by cordocentesis

KD32.3.title: Neonatal difficulty in feeding at breast
KD32.3.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by a newborn who has difficulty breastfeeding associated with problematic latching on to the breast, poor sucking reflex, structural anomalies, or other issues.
synonyms: Neonatal difficulty in feeding at breast

KD39.0.title: Fetus or newborn affected by amniocentesis
KD39.0.definition: Amniocentesis involves extracting a small sample of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus. Risks include miscarriage or injury if the needle comes into contact with the fetus or placenta.
synonyms: Fetus or newborn affected by amniocentesis
Fetus or newborn affected by trauma from amniocentesis

KD39.3.title: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of fetal surgery
KD39.3.definition: A condition in the fetus due to an unfavourable evolution of a condition (complication) associated with a surgical health intervention applied to the fetus.
synonyms: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of fetal surgery
Adverse outcome following fetal skin biopsy

KD38.title: Meconium staining
KD38.definition: Green or yellowish appearing amniotic fluid, indicating presence of meconium. The newborn’s skin, nail beds or the umbilical cord may be stained.

KD39.4.title: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of intrauterine fetal surgery
KD39.4.definition: Fetal surgery is the surgical treatment of a fetus still present in the uterus. It is performed when the fetus is suffering from a birth defect and is not expected to survive the delivery or live long after birth. It allows for the fetus to survive to birth, so that further corrective surgery can then be performed. Fetal surgery can be done in the following ways: fetoscopic surgery by using a fibreoptic scope to enter the uterus through small surgical openings, open fetal surgery by performing a hysterotomy which is an opening of the uterus, or radiofrequency ablation which cuts off the blood supply to a tumour.
synonyms: Fetus or newborn affected by complications of intrauterine fetal surgery

KD39.Y.title: Other specified complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified
synonyms: Other specified complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified
Fetus or newborn affected by unspecified intrauterine procedure
Fetus or newborn affected by other intrauterine procedures

KD3A.title: Termination of pregnancy, affecting surviving fetus or newborn
KD3A.definition: Termination of pregnancy (TOP) refers to a medically directed miscarriage, and this can be performed using pharmacological or surgical methods.
synonyms: Termination of pregnancy, affecting surviving fetus or newborn
abortion of pregnancy, affecting surviving fetus or newborn

KD39.Z.title: Complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified, unspecified
synonyms: Complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified, unspecified
Complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified

KD3Y.title: Other specified disorders originating in the perinatal period
synonyms: Other specified disorders originating in the perinatal period

KD3B.0.title: Antepartum fetal death
KD3B.0.definition:
Antepartum fetal death is a fetal death before the onset of labour. If vital status of the fetus at the onset of labour is unknown, consider it was antepartum if there is presence of signs of maceration at the time of delivery.

Macerated stillbirth - is the complete expulsion or extraction from a woman of a fetus following a fetal death at 22 or more completed weeks of gestation; or if gestational age is not available with a birthweight of 500g or more with skin showing signs of maceration.

Antepartum stillbirth - is the complete expulsion or extraction from a woman of a fetus following an antepartum fetal death at 22 or more completed weeks of gestation; or if gestational age is not available with a birthweight of 500 grams or more.

KD3B.1.title: Intrapartum fetal death
KD3B.1.definition:
Intrapartum fetal death is a fetal death during labour. If vital status of the fetus at the onset of labour is unknown, consider it was intrapartum if there is fresh skin appearance or no signs of maceration at the time of delivery.

Intrapartum stillbirth - is the complete expulsion or extraction from a woman of a fetus following an intrapartum fetal death at 22 or more completed weeks of gestation; or if gestational age is not available with a birthweight of 500 grams or more.

LA00.3.title: Amyelencephaly
LA00.3.definition: Amyelencephaly is the absence of both the brain and spinal cord.

KD5Z.title: Conditions originating in the perinatal or neonatal period, unspecified
synonyms: Conditions originating in the perinatal or neonatal period, unspecified

LA00.0Y.title: Other specified anencephaly
synonyms: Bone anomaly of skull, with anencephaly
absence of skull bone with anencephaly

KD3B.Z.title: Unspecified time of fetal death, cause not specified
synonyms: Unspecified time of fetal death, cause not specified

LA00.00.title: Craniorachischisis
LA00.00.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to close completely during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by complete absence of the skull, extensive defects in the vertebrae and skin, and absence of the brain.

LA00.Y.title: Other specified anencephaly or similar anomalies
synonyms: Other specified anencephaly or similar anomalies

LA00.1.title: Iniencephaly
LA00.1.definition: Iniencephaly is a rare form of neural tube defect in which a malformation of the cervico-occipital junction is associated with a malformation of the central nervous system. The cardinal features are occipital bone defect, partial or total absence of cervicothoracic vertebrae, fetal retroflexion of the head and characteristic absence of the neck. It is associated with malformations of the central nervous (spina bifida and/or anencephaly), gastrointestinal (omphalocele) and cardiovascular systems.

LA02.01.title: Myelomeningocele without hydrocephalus
LA02.01.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to close completely during fetal development. This condition is characterised by nerve damage. This condition may also present with syringomyelia, hip dislocation, headache, nausea, vomiting, blurry vision, balance problems, bladder control problems, meningitis, or mental impairment.
synonyms: Total spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus
Thoracolumbosacral spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus
Lumbosacral spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus
Cervical spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus
Cervicothoracic spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus
Upper thoracic spina bifida cystica without hydrocephalus

LA02.02.title: Myelocystocele
LA02.02.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to close completely during fetal development. The condition is characterised by skin covered lumbosacral masses, an arachnoid lined meningocele that is directly continuous with the spinal subarachnoid space, and a low lying hydromyelic spinal cord that traverses the meningocele and expands into a large terminal cyst. This condition can present with neural damage and consequent impairment of function below the site of the myelocystocele.

LA01.title: Cephalocele
LA01.definition: A condition caused by failure of the skull to correctly close during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by herniation of the meninges. This condition may present with herniation of brain, or developmental delay. Confirmation is through observation of herniated meninges by imaging.

LA02.00.title: Myelomeningocele with hydrocephalus
LA02.00.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by nerve damage and hydrocephalus. This condition may also present with syringomyelia, hip dislocation, headache, nausea, vomiting, blurry vision, balance problems, bladder control problems, meningitis, or mental impairment.
synonyms: Total spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
Thoracolumbosacral spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
congenital dorsal spina bifida with hydrocephalus
Lumbosacral spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
congenital lumbar spina bifida with hydrocephalus
congenital lumbosacral spina bifida with hydrocephalus
Cervical spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
congenital cervical spina bifida with hydrocephalus
Cervicothoracic spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
Upper thoracic spina bifida cystica with hydrocephalus
Upper thoracic spina bifida with hydrocephalus

LA02.1.title: Spina bifida aperta
LA02.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by nerve damage originating from a known location in the spine, signified by the presence of a meningocele or myelomeningocele. This condition may present with physical or mental impairment.
synonyms: Spina bifida aperta with tethered spinal cord
spina bifida aperta of thoracic spine
spina bifida aperta of cervical spine
Upper thoracic spina bifida without hydrocephalus

LA03.title: Arnold-Chiari malformation type II
LA03.definition: A condition caused by failure of the brain and spinal cord to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by extension of both cerebellar and brain stem tissue into the foramen magnum. This condition may present with partial or complete absence of the cerebellar vermis, myelomeningocele, neck pain, balance problems, muscle weakness, limb numbness, dizziness, vision problems, difficulty swallowing, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, vomiting, insomnia, depression, or impairment of motor skills.

LA04.0.title: Hydrocephalus with stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius
LA04.0.definition: Hydrocephalus with stenosis of aqueduct of Sylvius (HSAS) or Bickers-Adams syndrome is characterised by the association of hydrocephaly, severe intellectual deficit, spasticity and adducted thumbs, and is part of the L1 syndrome (see this term).
synonyms: Hydrocephalus with stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius
Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius
Atresia of the aqueduct of Sylvius
congenital obstruction of aqueduct of Sylvius
congenital stenosis of aqueduct of Sylvius
hydrocephalus with aqueduct of Sylvius stricture
inclusions: Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius

LA05.0.title: Microcephaly
LA05.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the head to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a head size that is significantly smaller than normal for their age and sex. This condition may also present with developmental delays, difficulties with balance and coordination, short stature, hyperactivity, mental retardation, seizures, or other neurological abnormalities.
synonyms: absence of skull bone with microcephaly
exclusions: Syndromes with microcephaly as a major feature

LA04.Y.title: Other specified congenital hydrocephalus
synonyms: Dilated ventricles due to developmental anomaly

LA05.4.title: Arrhinencephaly
LA05.4.definition: A condition caused by failure of the olfactory organs to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by absence of the olfactory bulbs and tracts.

LA05.2.title: Holoprosencephaly
LA05.2.definition: Holoprosencephaly is a brain malformation resulting from incomplete cleavage of the prosencephalon, occurring between the 18th and the 28th day of gestation and affecting both the forebrain and the face. In most of the cases, facial anomalies are observed: cyclopia, proboscis and median or bilateral cleft lip/palate in severe forms, and ocular hypotelorism or solitary median maxillary central incisor in minor forms. These latter midline defects can occur without the cerebral malformations (microforms). Children with HPE have many medical problems: developmental delay and feeding difficulties, epilepsy, and instability of temperature, heart rate and respiration. Endocrine disorders like diabetes insipidus, adrenal hypoplasia, hypogonadism, thyroid hypoplasia and growth hormone deficiency are frequent.
synonyms: Holoprosencephaly with congenital nasal pyriform aperture stenosis
Congenital stenosis of apertura pyriformis with holoprosencephaly
Congenital nasal pyriform aperture hypoplasia with holoprosencephaly

LA05.3.title: Corpus callosum agenesis
LA05.3.definition: Corpus callosum agenesis is the most common brain malformation and is characterised by total or partial absence of the main interhemispheric commissure, the corpus callosum.

LA05.60.title: Porencephaly
LA05.60.definition: Porencephaly is characterised by a circumscribed intracerebral cavity of variable size that may be bordered by abnormal polymicrogyric grey matter. In extreme cases, this cavity may result in a communication between the pial surface and the ventricle; this is termed schizencephaly.

LA05.50.title: Polymicrogyria
LA05.50.definition: Polymicrogyria (PMG) is a cerebral cortical malformation characterised by excessive cortical folding and by shallow sulci. Microscopic examination reveals abnormal cortical layering. Topographic distribution of PMG is variable, but bilateral symmetrical perisylvian PMG (BPP) is the most frequent form. PMG is manifested by mild intellectual deficit, epilepsy, and pseudobulbar palsy, which causes difficulties with speech learning and feeding. The severity of PMG is highly dependent on the location and size of the affected area.

LA05.51.title: Cortical dysplasia
LA05.51.definition: A condition caused by failure of the cortex to correctly develop during the antenatal period, or by trauma. This condition is characterised by epileptic seizures. This condition may also present with learning impairments.

LA05.8.title: Colpocephaly
LA05.8.definition: A condition caused by the white matter in the posterior cerebrum failing to develop or thicken during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the occipital horns – the posterior or rear portion of the lateral ventricles (cavities) of the brain – being larger than normal.

LA05.61.title: Schizencephaly
LA05.61.definition: Schizencephaly is a rare congenital cerebral malformation characterised by the presence of linear clefts in one or both hemispheres of the brain, extending from the lateral ventricles to the pial surface of the cortex, and that lead to a variety of neurological symptoms such as epilepsy, motor deficits, and psychomotor retardation.

LA05.62.title: Hydranencephaly
LA05.62.definition: A condition caused by failure of the cerebral hemispheres to develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a lack of a forebrain upon imaging. This condition may present with visual impairment, lack of growth, deafness, blindness, spastic quadriparesis, or intellectual deficits.

LA05.7.title: Brain cystic malformations
LA05.7.definition: A disease caused by expansion of the roof plate of the brain vesicle, or by extraaxial structures such as an arachnoid membrane or migrating ependymal cells. This disease is characterised by the presence of fluid filled cysts in the brain. This disease may present with asymmetry of the skull, brain compression, raised intracranial pressure, hydrocephalus, bleeding or seizures. This disease may also be asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of intracerebral cysts by imaging.
synonyms: Congenital brain third ventricle colloid cyst

LA06.0.title: Dandy-Walker malformation
LA06.0.definition: Dandy-Walker malformation is the association of three signs: hydrocephalus, partial or complete absence of the cerebellar vermis, and posterior fossa cyst contiguous with the fourth ventricle.
synonyms: congenital blocked foramen Magendie with hydrocephalus
Cystic cerebrospinal fluid collection due to Dandy walker malformation

LA05.1.title: Megalencephaly
LA05.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the brain to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by increased size or weight of an otherwise correctly formed brain. This condition may also present with seizures, motor deficits, mental retardation and mild cognitive impairment.

LA06.2.title: Focal cerebellar dysplasia
LA06.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the cerebellum to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition may present with hypotonia, facial deformities, abnormalities in eyes or in ocular motricity, cognitive deficiencies, or motor dysfunction. Confirmation is through observation of a malformed cerebellum by imaging.

LA06.Y.title: Other specified cerebellar structural developmental anomalies
synonyms: Other specified cerebellar structural developmental anomalies

LA06.1.title: Hypoplasia or agenesis of cerebellar hemispheres
LA06.1.definition: Cerebellar hypoplasia corresponds to underdevelopment of cerebellar structures that can involve the vermis and/or the cerebellar hemispheres from partial to total agenesis. It has been described in the context of various clinical entities: chromosomal anomalies, in utero exposure to toxins and infectious agents, metabolic disorders (disorders of glycosylation and CoQ10 deficiencies), and a wide variety of rare genetic neurological diseases. It can be confined to the cerebellum, or affect other CNS structures: the midbrain (molar tooth syndromes), pons and medulla (ponto-cerebellar hypoplasia), cerebral cortex (lissencephaly cerebellar hypoplasia syndromes).
synonyms: Hypoplasia or agenesis of cerebellar hemispheres

LA07.1.title: Diastematomyelia
LA07.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the spinal cord during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by separation of the spinal cord into two parts by a rigid or fibrous septum. This condition may present with misformed vertebrae, pain, weakness, impaired gait, sensory changes in the legs, or sphincter disturbance. Confirmation is through observation of a septum-bifurcated spinal cord by imaging.

LA05.Y.title: Other specified cerebral structural developmental anomalies
synonyms: Other specified cerebral structural developmental anomalies

LA07.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column
Other congenital malformations of spinal cord
Other specified congenital malformations of spinal cord
Congenital malformation of spinal cord, unspecified
congenital anomaly of spinal cord NOS
congenital anomaly of spinal cord or meninges NOS
congenital deformity of spinal cord NOS
congenital: deformity of spinal cord or meninges NOS
congenital disease or lesion of spinal cord or meninges NOS

LA07.3.title: Primary syringomyelia or hydromyelia
LA07.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the spinal canal to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a cavity within the spinal cord in which cerebrospinal fluid can accumulate. Confirmation is through observation of a fluid filled cavity within the spinal cord by imaging.
exclusions: Syringomyelia due to certain specified cause

LA07.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column
Malformations of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord and rachis
Malformations of the neuroenteric canal, spinal cord and rachis

LA0Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the nervous system, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the nervous system, unspecified

LA07.0.title: Primary tethered cord syndrome
LA07.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the spinal cord to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by tethering of the spinal cord to the spinal canal. This condition may present with lower back skin appendages, radicular pain, weakness, asymmetric hyporeflexia, spasticity, sensory changes, bowel or bladder dysfunction, or motor dysfunction. Confirmation is through observation of a tethered spinal cord by imaging.

LA07.4.title: Arnold-Chiari malformation type I
LA07.4.definition: A condition caused by failure of the cerebellum to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by extension of the cerebellar tonsils into the foramen magnum, without involving the brain stem. This condition may present as asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of the cerebellar tonsil extension by imaging.

LA11.3.title: Aniridia
LA11.3.definition: Aniridia is a congenital ocular malformation characterised by the complete or partial absence of the iris. It can be isolated or part of a syndrome (isolated and syndromic aniridia).

LA10.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes
congenital anomaly NOS of any part of eye
congenital deformity NOS of any part of eye
Anomaly of ocular muscle, not elsewhere classified

LA07.2.title: Amyelia
LA07.2.definition: A condition caused by malformation of the spinal cord during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by absence of sections of the spinal cord.

LA10.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes

LA11.5.title: Congenital corneal opacity
LA11.5.definition: A condition caused by failure of the cornea to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by opacity of the cornea.
synonyms: PPCD - [Posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy] C1 or C2

LA10.3.title: Congenital macrophthalmos
LA10.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the eye to develop correctly during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by enlargement of the globe of the eye.

LA11.0.title: Blue sclera
LA11.0.definition: A condition of the eye, characterised by transparency of the sclera such that the blue uvea is visible.

LA11.4.title: Coloboma of iris
LA11.4.definition: A disease of the eye, caused by trauma or congenital genetic mutation. This disease is characterised by notches or gaps in iris.
synonyms: coloboma of iris, choroid and retina

LA10.2.title: Buphthalmos
LA10.2.definition: A condition characterised by enlargement of the globe of the eye.

LA11.2.title: Anterior segment dysgenesis
LA11.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the anterior structures of the eye to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition may present with iris hypoplasia, irregular and misplaced pupils, hazy corneas, or attachments of the iris to the cornea.

LA11.1.title: Structural developmental anomalies of cornea
LA11.1.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the cornea to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA0Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the nervous system
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the nervous system

LA10.1.title: Clinical anophthalmos
LA10.1.definition: This refers to the clinical absence of one or both eyes. Both the globe (human eye) and the ocular tissue are missing from the orbit. The absence of the eye will cause a small bony orbit, a constricted mucosal socket, short eyelids, reduced palpebral fissure and malar prominence. Genetic mutations, chromosomal abnormalities, and prenatal environment can all cause anophthalmia. Anophthalmia is an extremely rare disease and is mostly rooted in genetic abnormalities.

LA11.62.title: Anomalies of pupillary function
LA11.62.definition: This is a group of conditions associated with pupillary function which is to regulate the amount of light that enters the eye controlled by the muscular structures of the iris.

LA11.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye
Malformations of anterior segment of eye
congenital malformations of anterior segment of eye

LA11.6Z.title: Structural disorders of the pupil, unspecified
synonyms: Structural disorders of the pupil, unspecified

LA11.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye
Structural developmental anomalies of the pupil

LA12.1.title: Congenital cataract
LA12.1.definition: Partial or complete opacity on or in the lens or capsule of one or both eyes, impairing vision or causing blindness; typically diagnosed at birth
synonyms: Anterior and posterior axial embryonal cataract

LA11.6Y.title: Other specified structural disorders of the pupil
synonyms: Other specified structural disorders of the pupil

LA13.2.title: Coloboma of macula
LA13.2.definition: A disease caused by malformation of the macula due to retinal inflammation during the antenatal period or by congenital genetic mutation. This disease is characterised by a clearly delineated defect in the macula.

LA13.1.title: Coloboma of choroid or retina
LA13.1.definition: A condition of the eye characterised by absence of the retina in the lower inside corner of the eye.
synonyms: Coloboma of choroid or retina, unilateral
Coloboma of choroid or retina, bilateral

LA12.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula

LA12.3.title: Spherophakia
LA12.3.definition: A disease of the eye, caused by homozygous mutations in the LTBP2 gene (isolated spherophakia), or by other genetic mutations. This disease is characterised by small, spherical lenses. This disease can also present with lenticular myopia, glaucoma, or sublation of the lens into the vitreous cavity.

LA13.3.title: Congenital vitreoretinal dysplasia
LA13.3.definition: Any disease caused by the maldevelopment of the vitreous and retina.

LA12.2.title: Congenital aphakia
LA12.2.definition: Congenital primary aphakia is a developmental eye defect characterised by an absence of the lens, and can be associated with variable secondary ocular defects (including aplasia/dysplasia of the anterior segment of the eye, microphthalmia, and in some cases absence of the iris, retinal dysplasia, or sclerocornea).

LA12.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula

LA13.6.title: Congenital malformations of choroid

LA14.01.title: Cryptophthalmia
LA14.01.definition: Isolated cryptophthalmia is a congenital abnormality in which the eyelids are absent and skin covers the ocular bulb, which is often microphthalmic.

LA13.76.title: Coloboma of optic disc
LA13.76.definition: Congenital abnormal optic disc appearance due to incomplete coaptation of the proximal end of the embryonic fissure in ocular development

LA14.07.definition: Isolated ankyloblepharon filiforme adnatum is characterised by the presence of single or multiple thin bands of connective tissue between the upper and lower eyelids, preventing full opening of the eye.

LA14.11.title: Agenesis of lacrimal ducts

congenital absence of lacrimal drainage structure

malformations of the eye, eyelid or lacrimal apparatus

LA21.0.title: Macrotia
LA21.0.definition:
1) Median longitudinal ear length greater than 2 SD above the mean and median ear width greater than 2 SD above the mean (objective). 
2) Apparent increase in length and width of the pinna (subjective).

LA21.2.title: Low-set ear
LA21.2.definition: The upper third of the pinna is not above a plane defined by the lateral canthi and the maximum convexity of the occiput.

LA21.Y.title: Other specified minor anomalies of pinnae
synonyms: Other specified minor anomalies of pinnae
Congenital absence of lobe of ear

LA21.3.title: Misshapen ear
LA21.3.definition: A condition caused by the malformation of the ear during the antenatal period.

LA22.1.title: Anotia
LA22.1.definition: Complete absence of any auricular structures.

LA22.4.title: Structural developmental anomalies of inner ear
LA22.4.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the inner ear to correctly develop during the antenatal period.
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of inner ear
congenital abnormal shape of inner ear

Congenital anomaly of organ of Corti

Structural developmental anomalies of cochlea and one or more including semicircular canal, vestibule, auditory canal

LA22.0.title: Microtia
LA22.0.definition:
Microtia is a congenital malformation of variable severity of the external and middle ear. Both hereditary factors (evidence for familial craniofacial microsomia and patterns suggestive of multifactorial inheritance)
and vascular accidents are involved in the etiology of the disease. Specific causative factors also can include maternal rubella during the first trimester of pregnancy. Microtia commonly involves the external canal and middle ear; hence, hearing can be affected. Microtia may present within a spectrum of branchial arch defects (hemifacial microsomia, craniofacial microsomia) or may manifest as an independent malformation. The microtic auricle consists of a disorganised remnant of cartilage attached to a variable amount of soft tissue lobule.

Congenital atresia of external auditory canal

LA30.1.definition: Hypodontia presents as a lack of one or a few (less than 6) permanent teeth, without any systemic disorders.

synonyms: congenital deformity of pinna of ear

LA23.title: Otocephaly
LA23.definition: Malplacement of the external ears with or without fusion microstomia, and persistence of the buccopharyngeal membrane likely being secondary effects of absence or hypoplasia of the mandibular arch.

LA30.4.title: Abnormalities of size or form of teeth
LA30.4.definition: A group of conditions characterised by abnormal size and form of teeth.
synonyms: Abnormalities of size or form of teeth

LA2Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the ear
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the ear

LA30.5Y.title: Other specified anomalies in tooth resorption or loss
synonyms: Other specified anomalies in tooth resorption or loss

LA30.2.title: Oligodontia
LA30.2.definition: A genetic condition characterised by the development of fewer than the normal number of teeth. The diagnosis of Oligodontia is usually made in cases in which more than six teeth are missing.

LA30.0.title: Anodontia
LA30.0.definition: Anodontia is a genetic disorder commonly defined as the absence of all teeth, affecting both temporary and permanent dentitions, and is extremely rarely encountered in a pure form without any associated abnormalities. Rare but more common than complete anodontia is hypodontia.
synonyms: total anodontia of permanent and deciduous teeth
Dental arch length loss secondary to congenitally missing teeth

LA30.3.title: Hyperdontia
LA30.3.definition: Hyperdontia is the condition of having supernumerary teeth, or teeth which appear in addition to the regular number of teeth.

LA30.50.title: Early exfoliation of teeth
synonyms: Premature shedding of primary deciduous tooth

LA30.5Z.title: Anomalies in tooth resorption or loss, unspecified
synonyms: Anomalies in tooth resorption or loss, unspecified
Anomalies in tooth resorption or loss

LA30.6.title: Amelogenesis imperfecta
LA30.6.definition: Amelogenesis imperfecta presents with a rare abnormal formation of the enamel or external layer of the crown of teeth. Amelogenesis imperfecta is due to the malfunction of the proteins in the enamel: ameloblastin, enamelin, tuftelin and amelogenin. People afflicted with amelogenesis imperfecta have teeth with abnormal colour: yellow, brown or grey; this disorder can afflict any number of teeth of both dentitions. The teeth have a higher risk for dental cavities and are hypersensitive to temperature changes as well as rapid attrition, excessive calculus deposition, and gingival hyperplasia.
synonyms: Hypomaturation hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta with taurodontism

LA30.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues
Solitary median maxillary central incisor syndrome

LA31.4.title: Microstomia
LA31.4.definition: A condition of the mouth, caused by congenital genetic mutation, burns, or injury. This condition is characterised by reduction in the size of the oral aperture with or without involvement of the entire oral cavity.

LA30.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues

LA31.3.title: Macrostomia
LA31.3.definition: Congenital macrostomia or transverse facial cleft is a rare congenital craniofacial anomaly. It is usually associated with deformities of other structures developed from the first and second branchial arches and is thought to be part of the manifestations of hemifacial microsomia, the second most common congenital craniofacial anomaly.

LA31.1.title: Hypoglossia or aglossia
LA31.1.definition: Isolated aglossia and hypoglossia are terms covering the spectrum from partial to total absence of the tongue. These congenital malformations have been classified as part of the group of oromandibular-limb hypogenesis syndromes (OLHS).

LA31.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue
structural developmental anomalies of mouth NOS
structural developmental anomalies of tongue NOS

LA31.0.title: Congenital macroglossia
LA31.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the tongue to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a larger than normal tongue.

LA40.1.title: Cleft lip, bilateral
LA40.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the upper lip to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by two fissures in the upper lip and a collapsed and stretched nose through one side of the upper lip. This condition may present with disruption of sucking or swallowing in neonates.
synonyms: Cleft lip without cleft palate, bilateral

LA31.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue

LA40.0.title: Cleft lip, unilateral
synonyms: Cleft lip without cleft palate, unilateral

LA42.1.title: Cleft soft palate
LA42.1.definition: Cleft velum is a fissure type embryopathy that affects in varying degrees the soft palate.

LA31.2.title: Ankyloglossia
LA31.2.definition: A condition of the tongue, caused by short, tight, lingual frenulum or fusion of the tongue to the floor of the mouth. This condition is characterised by difficulty in speech articulation due to limitation or restriction in tongue movement.
synonyms: Aberrant insertion of frenum of tongue

LA42.0.title: Cleft hard palate
LA42.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the palate to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a fissure extending across the palate, including the bony portion of the palate. This condition may present with disruption of sucking or swallowing in neonates.

LA42.2.title: Cleft uvula
LA42.2.definition: Bifid uvula is a fissure type embryopathy affecting the uvula at the back of the soft palate.

LA4Y.title: Other specified clefts of lip, alveolus or palate
synonyms: Other specified clefts of lip, alveolus or palate
Cleft hard palate with cleft soft palate

LA54.title: Microcheilia
LA54.definition: A condition caused by failure of the lips to develop correctly during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by below normal lip size.

LA51.title: Facial clefts
LA51.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the structures of the face to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by a partition in bone, soft tissue, or skin of the face.
synonyms: Median cleft of the upper lip or maxilla

LA55.title: Compression facies
LA55.definition: A disease caused by neurovascular compression of the facial nerve. This disease is characterised by facial spasm, and abnormal facial expression.

LA50.title: Congenital velopharyngeal incompetence
LA50.definition: A condition caused by failure of the velum to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by improper closing of the velopharyngeal sphincter, nasal speech, and difficulties in pronouncing certain letters or words.

LA53.title: Macrocheilia
LA53.definition: A condition characterised by above normal lip volume. This condition may present with difficulties in speaking, drinking, salivary control, or mastication.

LA56.title: Pierre Robin syndrome
LA56.definition: Pierre-Robin syndrome (or Pierre-Robin sequence) is characterised by triad of orofacial morphological anomalies consisting of retrognathism, glossoptosis and a posterior median velopalatal cleft. This condition is referred to as a sequence because the posterior cleft palate is a secondary defect associated with abnormal mandibular development: mandibular hypoplasia occurring early in gestation causes the tongue to be maintained high-up in the oral cavity, preventing fusion of the palatal shelves.

LA52.title: Facial asymmetry
LA52.definition: A condition caused by failure of the face to develop symmetrically during the antenatal period.

LA4Z.title: Clefts of lip, alveolus or palate, unspecified
synonyms: Clefts of lip, alveolus or palate, unspecified

LA5Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the face
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the face
Congenital malformations of lips, not elsewhere classified

LA60.title: Webbed neck
LA60.definition: A condition caused by failure of the tissues of the neck to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a broad neck due to lateral folds of skin. This condition may present with limited range of motion of the neck.

LA5Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the face, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the face, unspecified
Malformations of the face, mouth and teeth

LA6Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the neck, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the neck, unspecified

LA70.3.title: Congenital perforated nasal septum
LA70.3.definition: A condition caused by trauma during birth or by failure of the nasal septum to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of a hole in the nasal septum.

LA70.1.title: Bifid nose
LA70.1.definition: Isolated bifid nose is defined as a median cleft of the nose due to fusion anomalies of the medial nasal processes, that may involve the nasal tip only, or the nose on its length. Bifid nose may also be seen in multiple malformation syndromes like frontonasal dysplasia.
synonyms: congenital notching of tip of nose

LA70.2.title: Choanal atresia
LA70.2.definition: Any condition in neonates, caused by failure of the nose to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by narrowing or blockage of the nasal airway by tissue. This condition may also present with chest retraction unless child is breathing through mouth or crying, difficulty breathing, cyanosis, and inability to nurse and breathe at same time.

LA70.0.title: Arrhinia
LA70.0.definition: Also called nasal agenesis, it is a very rare anomaly in which external nose does not develop and the nasal cavity is totally or partially obliterated.

LA70.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum

LA6Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the neck
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the neck
Structural developmental anomalies of sternocleidomastoid muscle
congenital musculoskeletal deformities of sternocleidomastoid muscle

LA71.0.title: Congenital laryngomalacia
LA71.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the larynx to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This disease is characterised by collapse of the supraglottic structures into the airway during the inspiratory phase of respiration, resulting in inspiratory stridor. This disease may also present with regurgitation, emesis, cough, choking, slow feedings, weight loss, failure to thrive, tachypnoea, suprasternal and substernal retractions, cyanosis, pectus excavatum, or obstructive sleep apnoea. Confirmation is through verification of supraglottic collapse by flexible laryngoscopy.

LA70.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum
Malformations of the nose or cavum

LA71.3.title: Congenital subglottic stenosis
LA71.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the tracheal rings to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by inspiratory stridor. This condition may also present with shortness of breath, difficulty feeding, or failure to thrive. Confirmation is through observation of the stenosis by flexible laryngoscopy.

LA71.2.title: Laryngeal hypoplasia
LA71.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the pharynx and larynx to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a narrowed airway and protrusion of intestines through the belly button. This condition may also present with high pitched voice, spinal curvature, or learning difficulties.

LA71.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of larynx, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of larynx, unspecified

LA73.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of trachea
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of trachea

LA71.1.title: Laryngocele
LA71.1.definition: A condition of the larynx, characterised by an abnormal saccular dilatation of the appendix of the laryngeal ventricle of Morgagni. This condition may also present with cough, hoarseness, stridor, sore throat, or swelling of the neck. Alternatively this condition may be asymptomatic.

LA73.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of trachea, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of trachea, unspecified

LA73.1.title: Congenital tracheomalacia
LA73.1.definition: Congenital tracheomalacia is a relatively uncommon anomaly that results from an intrinsic weakness of the cartilaginous support of the trachea such that it is prone to collapse especially during expiration.

LA72.title: Laryngotracheooesophageal cleft
LA72.definition: A laryngo-tracheo-oesophageal cleft (LC) is a congenital malformation characterised by an abnormal, posterior, sagittal communication between the larynx and the pharynx, possibly extending downward between the trachea and the oesophagus. Five types of laryngo-tracheo-oesophageal cleft have been described based on the downward extension of the cleft, which typically correlates with the severity of symptoms: Type 0 laryngo-tracheo-oesophageal cleft to Type 4 laryngo-tracheo-oesophageal cleft (see these terms).

LA74.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of bronchi, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of bronchi, unspecified

LA74.1.title: Congenital bronchomalacia
LA74.1.definition: Bronchus characterised by excessive dynamic collapse

LA71.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of larynx
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of larynx

LA74.0.title: Congenital stenosis or atresia of bronchus
LA74.0.definition: A condition caused by interruption of a lobar, segmental, or subsegmental bronchus with peripheral mucus impaction, during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by hyperinflation of the blocked section of lung. This condition may present with respiratory distress, infiltrative pneumonia, or emphysema.
synonyms: Congenital stenosis or atresia of bronchus

LA73.0.title: Congenital stenosis of trachea
LA73.0.definition: Tracheal stenosis is a fixed intrinsic narrowing of the trachea. The narrowing can be localised to a short or long tracheal segment, often due to a complete tracheal ring. Alternatively, the tracheal lumen may become progressively narrow caudally.

LA74.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of bronchi
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of bronchi

LA75.0.title: Accessory lobe of lung
LA75.0.definition: An extra lobe of lung beyond the 3 on the right and the 2 on the left

LA75.5.title: Congenital lobar emphysema
LA75.5.definition: Congenital lobar emphysema is a developmental lung anomaly characterised by over distension of the affected lobe and leading to compression and displacement of adjacent normal lung tissue and mediastinum. In the majority of cases, symptoms appear during the neonatal period or in early childhood. Clinically, children present with signs of respiratory distress, frequently occurring with a lower respiratory tract infection that aggravates air trapping and renders the patient symptomatic.

LA75.4.title: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations
LA75.4.definition: A disease caused by failure of the bronchial structure to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This disease may present with severe respiratory distress in the newborn period, acute respiratory distress or infection later in life, or may be asymptomatic. This disease can be distinguished from other lesions and normal lung by polypoid projections of the mucosa, an increase in smooth muscle and elastic tissue within the cyst walls, an absence of cartilage in the cystic parenchyma, mucous secreting cells, and the absence of inflammation.
synonyms: CPAM type 0 - [Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 0]
CPAM type 1 - [Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 1]
CPAM type 2 - [Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 2]
CPAM type 3 - [Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 3]
CPAM type 4 - [Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 4]
exclusions: Cystic lung disease, acquired or unspecified

LA75.1.title: Agenesis of lung
LA75.1.definition: This refers to the absence or rudimentary residua of an undeveloped lung.
synonyms: congenital absence of lobe of lung

LA75.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of lungs
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of lungs

LA77.title: Congenital cyst of mediastinum
LA77.definition: A condition caused by failure of the anterior intestine or coelomic cavity to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition may be asymptomatic or may present with adjacent organ compression. Confirmation is observation of the cysts by imaging.

LA75.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of lungs, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of lungs, unspecified

LA76.title: Structural developmental anomalies of pleura
LA76.definition: Anomalies of the lining of the lung (visceral pleura) and thoracic cavity (parietal pleura)

LA7Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the respiratory system
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the respiratory system
Structural developmental anomalies of the larynx or lower respiratory organs
Congenital malformations of the larynx and lower respiratory tract

LA80.1.title: Dextrocardia
LA80.1.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the heart is predominantly to the right of the thoracic midline. This is independent of the orientation of the cardiac apex.

LA80.0.title: Laevocardia
LA80.0.definition: A congenital cardiovascular finding in which the heart is predominantly to the left of the thoracic midline.

LA80.3.title: Extrathoracic heart
LA80.3.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the heart is at least partially outside of the thorax.

LA7Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the respiratory system, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the respiratory system, unspecified

LA80.2.title: Mesocardia
LA80.2.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the heart is central or midline within the thorax.

LA81.title: Abnormal ventricular relationships
LA81.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the ventricular positions relative to each other or their laterality (sidedness) are abnormal.

LA82.title: Total mirror imagery
LA82.definition: A congenital malformation in which there is complete mirror-imaged arrangement of the internal organs along the left-right axis of the body.
synonyms: transposition of stomach, with complete transposition of viscera

LA75.6.title: Congenital sequestration of lung
LA75.6.definition: A medical condition wherein a piece of tissue that ultimately develops into lung tissue is not attached to the pulmonary arterial blood supply, as is the case in normally developing lung. As a result, this sequestered tissue is not connected to the normal bronchial airway. With intralobar sequestration, the lung tissue lies within the same visceral pleura as the lobe in which it occurs With extralobar sequestrations, an accessory lung is contained within its own pleura

LA83.title: Right isomerism
LA83.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation that is a variant of heterotaxy syndrome in which some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal right-sided structures.

LA80.Y.title: Other specified anomalous position-orientation of heart
synonyms: Other specified anomalous position-orientation of heart

LA85.21.title: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect
LA85.21.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation that is a variant of double outlet right ventricle with concordant atrioventricular connections that is associated with ventricular septal defect that is remote from the ventricular outflow tracts and usually within the inlet or trabecular muscular septum.
synonyms: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect
Double outlet right ventricle with remote ventricular septal defect
Double outlet right ventricle with uncommitted ventricular septal defect
Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed interventricular communication

LA84.title: Left isomerism
LA84.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation that is a variant of an heterotaxy syndrome in which some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal left-sided structures.

LA85.00.title: Congenitally corrected transposition of great arteries
LA85.00.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation in which the morphologically right atrium connects to the morphologically left ventricle, the morphologically left atrium connects to the morphologically right ventricle, the morphologically right ventricle connects to the aorta, and the morphologically left ventricle connects to the pulmonary trunk.
synonyms: Congenitally corrected transposition of great arteries
congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
corrected transposition of the great arteries
corrected transposition of the great vessels
congenitally corrected transposition of the great vessels
ccTGA - [congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries]
physiologically corrected transposition of the great arteries
physiologically corrected transposition of the great vessels

LA85.2Y.title: Other specified double outlet right ventricle
synonyms: Other specified double outlet right ventricle
Double outlet right ventricle with intact ventricular septum
DORV [double outlet right ventricle] & IVS [intact ventricular septum]

LA85.22.title: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis, ventricular septal defect type
LA85.22.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation that is a variant of double outlet right ventricle with concordant atrioventricular connections, a subaortic or doubly-committed (with absence or deficiency of the conal septum) ventricular septal defect, and unobstructed pulmonary outflow tract.
synonyms: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis, ventricular septal defect type
Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed interventricular communication without pulmonary stenosis (ventricular septal defect type)
Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic interventricular communication without pulmonary stenosis (ventricular septal defect type)
Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed interventricular communication without pulmonary stenosis (ventricular septal defect type)

LA85.23.title: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis, Fallot type
LA85.23.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation that is a variant of double outlet right ventricle with concordant atrioventricular connections, a subaortic or doubly-committed (with absence or deficiency of the conal septum) ventricular septal defect, and pulmonary outflow tract obstruction.

LA86.20.title: Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection

LA86.22.title: Scimitar syndrome
LA86.22.definition: A congenital cardiopulmonary malformation with “partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection of Scimitar type” and one or more of the following: hypoplasia of the right lung with bronchial anomalies, dextrocardia, hypoplasia of the right pulmonary artery, lobar lung sequestration, and anomalous systemic arterial supply to the lower lobe of the right lung directly from the aorta or its main branches.

LA87.00.title: Congenital tricuspid regurgitation

LA87.01.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the tricuspid valve in which there is narrowing or stricture (obstruction to flow).

LA87.11.title: Congenital mitral valvar stenosis
LA87.11.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the mitral valve in which there is narrowing or stricture of the valvar orifice (obstruction to flow).
synonyms: congenital stenotic deformity of mitral valve

LA87.10.title: Congenital mitral regurgitation
LA87.10.definition: A congenital cardiovascular finding in which there is backward flow through the mitral valve.

LA87.03.title: Ebstein malformation of tricuspid valve
LA87.03.definition:
A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle that is characterised by incomplete delamination of the septal and inferior (posterior) tricuspid valvar leaflets from the myocardium of the right ventricle, and varying degrees of downward (apical) rotational displacement of the functional annulus.

Additional information: associated cardiac anomalies include an interatrial communication, the presence of accessory conduction pathways and varying degrees of right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, including pulmonary atresia. In the setting of discordant atrioventricular and ventriculo-arterial connections ['Congenitally corrected transposition of great arteries'], 'Ebstein malformation of tricuspid valve' may be present.
synonyms: congenital Ebstein deformity of tricuspid valve

LA87.12.title: Dysplasia of mitral valve
