LB22.0.title: Congenital asplenia
LB22.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the spleen to develop during the antenatal period. This condition may present with pneumococcal sepsis. Confirmation is through verification of no spleen by imaging.

LB21.4.title: Partial agenesis of pancreas
LB21.4.definition: Partial agenesis of the pancreas is characterised by the congenital absence of a critical mass of pancreatic tissue. The severity of the disease depends on the amount of functional pancreatic tissue present. Pancreatic agenesis is commonly associated with other malformations, in particular pancreaticobiliary duct anomalies, leading to acute or chronic pancreatitis, hyperglycaemia (50% of cases), or, more rarely, polysplenia.

LB30.0Z.title: Renal agenesis or other reduction defects of kidney, unspecified
synonyms: Renal agenesis or other reduction defects of kidney, unspecified
Renal agenesis or other reduction defects of kidney

LB22.1.title: Polysplenia
LB22.1.definition: A condition caused by the development of supernumerary spleens during the antenatal period. This condition may present with cardiac defects, anomalies in abdominal organs, or may be asymptomatic.

LB30.1.title: Renal dysplasia
LB30.1.definition: A condition characterised by abnormal development of one or both kidneys.

LB30.2.title: Congenital single renal cyst
LB30.2.definition: A single cyst in a kidney, noted in utero or from birth. No other structural abnormality of the kidney or urinary tract noted.

LB30.3.title: Renal tubular dysgenesis
LB30.3.definition: Abnormal renal development and kidney formation secondary to an underlying condition or exposure.
synonyms: Renal tubular dysgenesis due to twin-twin transfusion
Renal tubular dysgenesis of genetic origin

LB30.4.title: Oligomeganephronia
LB30.4.definition: Oligomeganephronic renal hypoplasia is a severe developmental defect of both kidneys characterised by a reduced number of nephrons (the functional unit of the kidney), hypertrophic glomeruli with diameters twice the normal size, hypertrophic tubules and thickening of Bowman's capsule, occurring in the absence of a urinary tract malformation.

LB30.60.title: Lobulated kidney
LB30.60.definition: Any condition caused by incomplete fusion of the developing renal lobules during the antenatal period. This condition may be asymptomatic.

LB30.7.title: Ectopic or pelvic kidney
LB30.7.definition: A birth defect characterised by an abnormally positioned kidney; may be asymptomatic or result in urine blockage, infection or kidney stones

LB30.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of kidneys
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of kidneys

LB31.3.title: Exstrophy of urinary bladder
LB31.3.definition: Bladder exstrophy (or classic bladder exstrophy) is a congenital genitourinary malformation belonging to the spectrum of the exstrophy-epispadias complex and is characterised by an evaginated bladder plate, epispadias and an anterior defect of the pelvis, pelvic floor and abdominal wall.
synonyms: congenital exteriorized or extroverted bladder malposition

LB30.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of kidneys, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of kidneys, unspecified

LB31.2.title: Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction
LB31.2.definition: A disease caused by partial or complete obstruction of the urethra, during the antenatal period. This disease can present with enlarged bladder, oligohydramnios, or pulmonary hypoplasia. Confirmation is through observation of the obstruction by imaging.
synonyms: other atresia or stenosis of urethra or bladder neck
Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction due to atresia of urethra
Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction due to posterior urethral valve
Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction due to anterior urethral valve

LB31.0.title: Congenital hydronephrosis
LB31.0.definition: Congenital hydronephrosis is a renal urinary disease characterised by distension and dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces secondary to various congenital obstructive malformations of the kidneys and urinary tract that can evolve to renal atrophy.

LB31.1.title: Congenital primary megaureter
LB31.1.definition: Congenital primary megaureter is an idiopathic condition in which the bladder and bladder outlet are normal but the ureter is dilated to some extent. It may be obstructed, refluxing or unobstructed and not refluxing.
synonyms: Congenital primary megaureter, nonrefluxing and unobstructed form

LB30.8.title: Medullary sponge kidney
LB30.8.definition: A condition characterised by cystic or saccular dilatations of the medullary collecting ducts seen with radiocontrast filling. A predisposition to stones and associated often with renal tubular acidosis. There is no clear genetic predisposition.

LB30.61.title: Fused pelvic kidney
LB30.61.definition: A condition caused by failure of the kidneys to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of a single kidney, along the midline of the body. This condition may present with kidney stones, hydronephrosis, kidney infection, haematuria, or may be asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of a fused kidney by imaging.

LB31.8.title: Atresia or stenosis of ureter
LB31.8.definition: A condition caused by blockage or narrowing of the ureter due to failure to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition may present with bladder outlet obstruction, low amniotic fluid volume, pulmonary hypoplasia, megacystis, hydroureter, hydronephrosis, or renal dysplasia.

LB30.6Y.title: Other specified fusion anomaly of kidneys
synonyms: Other specified fusion anomaly of kidneys

LB30.62.title: Horseshoe kidney
LB30.62.definition: Horseshoe kidney is the most frequent renal fusion anomaly and is characterised by the union of the inferior poles of the two kidneys through an isthmus. Horseshoe kidney is in fact an anatomical anomaly rather than a disease, but it does lead to predisposition to certain conditions such as hydronephrosis, nephrolithiasis or pyelonephritis. One third of individuals with horseshoe kidney are asymptomatic, with the anomaly being discovered fortuitously during a radiological examination. Urogenital or renal vessel anomalies may be associated with the condition. For cases requiring treatment, various therapeutic approaches are available and choice of treatment depends on the associated pathology.

LB31.4.title: Congenital diverticulum of urinary bladder
LB31.4.definition: A condition caused by failure of the bladder to correctly develop. This condition is characterised by weakness in the bladder wall through which some of the lining of the bladder protrudes. This condition may present with urinary tract infections, difficulty voiding, or abdominal fullness. This condition may also be asymptomatic.

LB31.6.title: Congenital megalourethra
LB31.6.definition: A condition caused by failure of the penile corpora cavernosa and spongiosa to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by dilatation of the penile urethra. This condition may present with poor stream, swelling of the penis, megacystis, oligohydramnios, renal failure, or pulmonary hypoplasia.

LB31.5.title: Duplication of urethra
LB31.5.definition: A condition caused by failure of the urethra to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of a second passage from the bladder. This condition may present with double urinary stream, urination from the anus, or may be asymptomatic. Confirmation is through observation of a second urethra by imaging.

LB31.9.title: Agenesis of ureter
LB31.9.definition: A condition caused by failure of the ureter to develop during the antenatal period. Confirmation verification that one or more ureters are missing by imaging.

LB31.7.title: Megacystis-megaureter
LB31.7.definition: Megacystic-megaureter syndrome describes the presence of a massive primary non-obstructive vesicoureteral reflux and a large capacity, smooth, thin walled bladder due to the continual recycling of refluxed urine. Recurrent urinary infections are commonly associated with this condition.

LB31.A.title: Duplication of ureter
LB31.A.definition: A condition caused by failure of the ureter to correctly develop during the antenatal period, resulting in incorrect connection of the ureter to the kidney. This condition may present with ureteroureteral reflux, or ureteropelvic junction obstruction of the lower pole of the kidney in the case of incomplete duplication. Complete duplication may present with vesicoureteral reflux, ectopic ureterocele, or ectopic ureteral insertion. Confirmation is through observation of two ureters on one side by imaging.

LB31.D.title: Congenital vesico-uretero-renal reflux
LB31.D.definition: A condition caused by failure of the ureter to develop correctly during the antenatal period. This condition may present with urinary tract infection, or may be asymptomatic.

LB31.C.title: Congenital absence of bladder or urethra
LB31.C.definition: Any condition caused by failure of both the bladder and the urethra to develop during the antenatal period. This condition may result in fetal death, or sepsis and sever complications in cases of live births.
synonyms: Congenital absence of bladder or urethra

LB30.9.title: Multicystic renal dysplasia
LB30.9.definition: A condition characterised by abnormal development of the kidney, specifically in which the abnormal kidney does not form a reniform structure but rather, a collection of non-communicating cysts, with no renal functional tissue.

LB31.B.title: Malposition of ureter
LB31.B.definition: A condition caused by failure of the ureter to correctly develop during the antenatal period, resulting in partial or complete duplication of the ureter. This condition may present with hydronephrosis, urinary tract infection, or incontinence in females. Confirmation is through observation of an incorrectly positioned ureter by imaging.
synonyms: anomalous implantation of ureter or ureteric orifice
Displacement of ureter or ureteric orifice
deviation of ureter or ureteric orifice

LB40.0.title: Absence of vulva
LB40.0.definition: This is a birth defect or congenital abnormality of the female genitourinary system that manifests itself in the absence of the vulva.

LB41.1.title: Duplication of clitoris
LB41.1.definition: An anatomical anomaly present at birth in which there are two clitoral structures present.

LB3Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the urinary system
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the urinary system

LB31.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract

LB40.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of vulva, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of vulva, unspecified

LB3Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the urinary system, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the urinary system, unspecified

LB31.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract

LB40.1.title: Embryonic cyst of vulva
LB40.1.definition: Remnant tissue from embryological development of the pelvic organs presenting as a closed fluid sac in or on the tissue of the vulva.

LB40.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of vulva
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of vulva

LB41.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of clitoris
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of clitoris

LB40.2.title: Fusion of labia
LB40.2.definition: A condition of the labia commonly affecting females between 6 months and 6 years of age, caused by skin irritation during infancy. This condition is characterised by the sealing of the labia minor (usually completely) due to a thin membrane that seals the entrance to the vagina, leaving a very small gap for urination.

LB44.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix

LB43.1.title: Agenesis or aplasia of cervix
LB43.1.definition: A condition of the cervix, caused by the absence of primordial tissue development during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by improper or lack of development of the cervix.

LB45.1.title: 46,XX gonadal dysgenesis
LB45.1.definition: Karyotype 46 XX; Gonads: gonadal dysgenesis (streak gonads); Phenotype female with symptoms like primary amenorrhea, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, normal stature and no other abnormalities.

LB45.4.title: Accessory ovary
LB45.4.definition: A condition of the ovary, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by excess ovarian tissue situated near an anatomically correct ovary, which may or may not be connected to the original ovarian tissue.

LB43.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri

LB41.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of clitoris, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of clitoris, unspecified

LB44.2.title: Unicornuate uterus
LB44.2.definition: A uterine malformation where the uterus is formed from one only of the paired Müllerian ducts while the other Müllerian duct does not develop or develops only in a rudimentary fashion.
synonyms: Uterus with only one functioning horn
Incomplete unilateral aplasia of the Müllerian duct
Congenital absence of one uterine horn
Complete unilateral aplasia of the Müllerian duct

LB45.0.title: Congenital absence of ovary
LB45.0.definition: A condition of the ovary, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a female born with fewer than two ovaries.

LB44.3.title: Bicornuate uterus
LB44.3.definition: A condition of the uterus, caused by malformation in the development of the uterus during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a uterus with a bifurcated cephalo, and a unitary caudal part. Confirmation is by imaging.
synonyms: Doubling of uterus with doubling of cervix and vagina
Bicervical bicornuate uterus and blind hemi-vagina
Bicervical bicornuate uterus with patent cervix and vagina

LB42.1.title: Septate vagina
LB42.1.definition: A condition of the genitourinary system affecting females, caused by the absence of Mullerian duct fusion during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a transverse of longitudinal septum, partitioning the vagina into two parts. This condition may also present with dyspareunia, abnormal vaginal bleeding, or is asymptomatic. Confirmation is by imaging.
exclusions: doubling of vagina with doubling of uterus and cervix

LB42.2.title: Congenital rectovaginal fistula
LB42.2.definition: A condition of the genitourinary system affecting females, caused by an abnormality arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the formation of an abnormal passage between the rectum and the vagina.

LB44.0.title: Agenesis or aplasia of uterine body
LB44.0.definition: A condition of the uterus, caused by the absence of primordial tissue development during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by improper or lack of development of the uterine body.
synonyms: Agenesis or aplasia of uterine body

LB42.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of vagina
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of vagina

LB42.5.title: Stricture or atresia of vagina
LB42.5.definition: A condition of the vagina, caused by an abnormality arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by stenosis and occlusion of the vaginal opening.

LB42.4.title: Imperforate hymen
LB42.4.definition: A condition in which the hymen, the membrane that surrounds or partially covers the external vaginal opening, is harder than normal or is complete and sealed without any opening into the vaginal vault.

LB45.7.title: Accessory fallopian tube
LB45.7.definition: A condition of the fallopian tube, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the duplication of one or more fallopian tubes, commonly attached to the ampullary segment.

LB42.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of vagina, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of vagina, unspecified

LB44.6.title: Uterovaginal malformation due to diethylstilbestrol syndrome
LB44.6.definition: Fetal diethylstilbestrol syndrome is characterised by a group of symptoms likely to occur in children and grandchildren of a woman who was treated while pregnant with diethylstilbestrol (DES). The drug is a synthetic nonsteroidal oestrogen, used in the US until 1971 and in Europe until 1978 to try and prevent miscarriage, premature delivery, and other pregnancy complications. It has been estimated that 25% of female fetuses exposed to DES in utero during the first trimester have subsequently developed genital tract anomalies including vaginal adenosis, cervical malformations, vaginal septae, uterine cavity anomalies, or fallopian tube anomalies causing subsequent fertility problems.
synonyms: Uterovaginal malformation due to diethylstilbestrol syndrome

LB44.4.title: Septate uterus
LB44.4.definition: Longitudinal septum in uterus, subclassified as complete or partial

LB43.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri

LB45.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments

LB42.3.title: Tight hymenal ring
LB42.3.definition: A condition of the vagina, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by tightening of the hymen and stenosis of the external opening of the vagina, and dyspareunia.
synonyms: tight hymenal ring acquired or congenital

LB44.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix

LB45.5.title: Congenital absence of fallopian tube
LB45.5.definition: A condition of the fallopian tube, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a female born with fewer than two fallopian tubes.
synonyms: Congenital absence of fallopian tube, unilateral
Congenital absence of fallopian tube, bilateral

LB43.0.title: Embryonic cyst of cervix
LB43.0.definition: A condition of the cervix, caused by a cluster of cells that have formed a closed sac or structures left behind from development during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by air, fluid, or semi-solid material surrounded by a distinct membrane of cells with abnormal appearance and behaviour.

LB45.8.title: Embryonic cyst of fallopian tube
LB45.8.definition: A condition of the Fallopian tube, caused by the overgrowth of pelvic tissue during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by air, fluid, or semi-solid material surrounded by a distinct membrane of cells with abnormal appearance and behaviour.

LB44.5.title: Congenital fistulae between uterus and digestive and urinary tracts
LB44.5.definition: A condition caused by abnormal tissue development during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the formation of an abnormal passage between the uterus, digestive, and urinary tracts.
synonyms: Congenital fistulae between uterus and digestive and urinary tracts

LB42.0.title: Absence of vagina
LB42.0.definition: A condition of the genitourinary system affecting females, caused by an abnormality arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by vaginal agenesis.

LB51.title: Anorchia or microorchidia
LB51.definition: A disorder affecting males, caused by an abnormality occurring in sex development during the antenatal period. This disorder is characterised by individuals who are born with absence of the testes, or with testes that are deficient in size and function. Confirmation is by physical examination, identification of low testosterone levels but elevated follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone levels in a blood sample, or imaging.
synonyms: Absence or aplasia of testis, unilateral
Absence or aplasia of testis, bilateral

LB45.3.title: Congenital torsion of ovary
LB45.3.definition: A condition of the ovary, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a partial or complete rotation of the ovary, an occlusion to the venous or arterial blood supply of the ovary, severe lower abdominal pain that may radiate to the back, pelvis and thigh, and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or constipation.

LB45.9.title: Embryonic cyst of broad ligament
LB45.9.definition: Remnant tissue from embryological development of the development of the pelvic organs presenting as a closed fluid sac on the broad ligament.
synonyms: paravaginal cyst arising in Gartner duct

LB50.title: Micropenis or penis agenesis
LB50.definition: A condition caused by reduced androgen production during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by an absent, or unusually small penis. Confirmation is by measuring the length of a dorsal erectile penis.
synonyms: congenital absence or aplasia of penis

LB45.6.title: Atresia of fallopian tube
LB45.6.definition: A condition of the fallopian tube, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by unilateral or bilateral closure or absence of the fallopian tube(s), commonly within the proximal isthmic or proximal ampullary segments.

LB4Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the female genital system, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the female genital system, unspecified
Malformations of the female genital system
congenital malformations of uterus and cervix

LB4Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the female genital system
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the female genital system
Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck

LB45.2.title: Developmental ovarian cyst
LB45.2.definition: A condition in which an individual is born with a benign, functional cyst, or cysts, on one or more ovaries which result from enlargement of otherwise normal follicles during third trimester or early neonatal period.

LB45.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments

LB53.1.title: Hypospadias, penile
LB53.1.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis and an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens along the shaft of the penis. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB53.00.title: Hypospadias, coronal
LB53.00.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis, leading to an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens in the ventral portion of the coronal sulcus. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB53.01.title: Hypospadias, glandular
LB53.01.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis, leading to an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens at the site of the frenulum. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB52.0.title: Ectopic testis
LB52.0.definition: A condition of the testis, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the abnormal location of the testis away from the normal line of descent such as in the superficial inguinal pouch, perineal, abdominal, pelvic, crural, penile or femoral positions, and with normal testis and spermatic cord anatomy. Confirmation is by diagnostic laparoscopy to rule out an intra-abdominal, inguinal or absent/vanishing testis.

LB52.2.title: Undescended testicle, bilateral
LB52.2.definition: The situation in which both testicles in a male have not transitioned from the abdomen, and therefore appear absent from the scrotum.

LB53.4.title: Hypospadias, perineal
LB53.4.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis and an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens in the perineum. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB57.title: Agenesis of vas deferens
LB57.definition: A condition of the vas deferens affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the unilateral or bilateral absence of the vas deferens, azoospermia, and infertility.

LB54.title: Congenital chordee
LB54.definition: A condition caused by the development of fibrous bands of tissue along the corpus spongiosum and shortening of the ventral skin during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by ventral or dorsal curvature of the head of the penis at the junction with the shaft, most apparent during erection. This condition may also present with hypospadias.

LB52.1.title: Undescended testicle, unilateral
LB52.1.definition: The situation in which one of the two testicles in a male has not transitioned from the abdomen, and therefore appears absent from the scrotum.

LB53.2.title: Hypospadias, penoscrotal
LB53.2.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis, leading to an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens where the shaft of the penis meets the scrotum. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB55.title: Epispadias
LB55.definition: Epispadias is a congenital genitourinary malformation belonging to the spectrum of the exstrophy-epispadias complex and is characterised in males by an ectopic meatus or a mucosal strip in place of the urethra on the penile dorsum and in females by bifid clitoris and a variable cleft of the urethra.

LB56.title: Bifid scrotum
LB56.definition: A condition caused by failure of the scrotum to correctly develop during the antenatal period resulting in incomplete fusion of the labioscrotal folds. This condition is characterised by a deep midline cleft in the scrotum. This condition may be asymptomatic.

LB58.title: Polyorchidism
LB58.definition: A condition of the testes, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of more than two testicles. Confirmation is by imaging.

LB59.title: Hypoplasia of testis or scrotum
LB59.definition: A condition caused by incomplete development of the testis and scrotum during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a decrease or destruction in the number or size of cells testis and scrotal tissue.

LB6Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the breast
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the breast

LB5Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the male genital system, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the male genital system, unspecified
Malformations of the male genital system

LB62.title: Supernumerary breasts
LB62.definition: A condition caused by failure of the breasts to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by supernumerary breasts, with or without nipples. This condition may be asymptomatic.

LB63.title: Accessory nipple
LB63.definition: A condition caused by development of supernumerary nipples during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of nipples or nipple-like structures additional to the normal two. This condition may be asymptomatic.

LB53.3.title: Hypospadias, scrotal
LB53.3.definition: A condition caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and the ventral side of the penis, leading to an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens on the scrotum. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB5Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the male genital system
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of the male genital system
Absence or aplasia of spermatic cord
Absence or aplasia of seminal vesicles

LB60.title: Breast aplasia
LB60.definition: A condition caused by failure of the breast to develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a total lack of breast tissue. This condition may also present with absence of the nipple or pectoral muscle.
synonyms: Congenital absence of breast with absent nipple
agenesis of breast with absent nipple

LB6Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the breast, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of the breast, unspecified

LB70.00.title: Plagiocephaly
LB70.00.definition: Isolated synostotic plagiocephaly is a form of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis characterised by premature fusion of one coronal or lambdoid suture leading to skull deformity and facial asymmetry.

LB61.title: Absent nipple
LB61.definition: A condition caused by failure of the nipple to develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a total lack of a nipple. This condition may also present with absence of the breast or pectoral muscle.

LB71.1.title: Hypertelorism
LB71.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the facial bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by higher than normal distance between the eyes.

LB70.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of cranium, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of cranium, unspecified

LB70.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of cranium
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of cranium

LB70.3.title: Macrocephaly
LB70.3.definition: A condition characterised by above normal head size.

LB70.0Z.title: Craniosynostosis, unspecified
synonyms: congenital ossification of sutures of skull

LB70.1.title: Wormian bones
LB70.1.definition: Also known as intrasutural bone, is an additional bony segment interlocked in an existing cranial suture. A special form: Interparietal bone or Inca bone is an interlocked irregular isolated bone at the lambdoid suture. Although harmless it may be associated with craniofacial and other syndromes.

LB72.0.title: Cervical rib
synonyms: cervical or first extra rib syndrome
cervical or first supernumerary rib syndrome

LB71.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of facial bones
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of facial bones
Congenital asymmetry of the facial skeleton

LB71.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of facial bones, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of facial bones, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of facial bones

LB71.0.title: Hypotelorism
LB71.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the facial bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by lower than normal distance between the eyes.

LB72.1.title: Sprengel deformity
LB72.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the pectoral girdle to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by abnormal descent, and altered position and anatomy of the scapula. This condition may present with muscle hypoplasia.

LB73.10.title: Poland syndrome
LB73.10.definition: Poland syndrome is characterised by a unilateral absence or hypoplasia of the pectoralis major muscle (most frequently involving the sternocostal portion), and a variable degree of ipsilateral hand anomalies, including symbrachydactyly.

LB73.0.title: Occult spinal dysraphism
synonyms: Spina bifida occulta with tethered spinal cord

LB72.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle

LB73.21.title: Occipitalisation of atlas
LB73.21.definition: A condition caused by failure of the atlas and occiput to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by fusion of the atlas to the base of the occiput. This condition may present with headache, suboccipital stiffness, restricted motion, or dizziness. Confirmation is through observation of the fusion by imaging.

LB73.20.title: Klippel-Feil anomaly
LB73.20.definition: Klippel-Feil syndrome is characterised by improper segmentation of cervical segments resulting in congenitally fused cervical vertebrae.

LB73.13.title: Structural developmental anomalies of sternum
LB73.13.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the sternum to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB73.1Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of chest wall
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of chest wall

LB73.24.title: Segmentation anomalies of vertebrae
LB73.24.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the vertebrae to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by an abnormal number of fully developed vertebrae. Confirmation is through verification of absent or improperly formed vertebrae by imaging.

LB73.12.title: Accessory rib
LB73.12.definition: A condition caused by failure of the ribs to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a supernumerary rib arising from a cervical or lumbar vertebra. This condition may present with thoracic outlet syndrome, or may be asymptomatic.

LB73.26.title: Sacralisation of the last lumbar vertebra
synonyms: Sacralisation of the last lumbar vertebra

LB73.27.title: Lumbarisation of the first sacral vertebra
synonyms: Lumbarisation of the first sacral vertebra

LB73.1Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of chest wall, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of chest wall, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of chest wall

LB73.23.title: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the odontoid process of axis
synonyms: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the odontoid process of axis

LB73.25.title: Congenital scoliosis due to congenital bony malformation
LB73.25.definition: A condition caused by malformation of the ribs or spine. This condition is characterised by abnormal curving of the spine.
synonyms: Congenital scoliosis due to congenital bony malformation
congenital scoliosis due to anomalies of vertebra
Congenital scoliosis with failure of hemivertebra segmentation
congenital scoliosis with failure of segmentation
failure of hemivertebra segmentation with scoliosis
Hemivertebra fusion or failure of segmentation with scoliosis
Congenital scoliosis due to absence of vertebra

LB72.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle

LB73.22.title: Atlanto-axial instability or subluxation
LB73.22.definition: A condition caused by bony or ligamentous abnormality of the upper spinal column. This condition is characterised by excessive movement at the junction between C1 and C2 vertebrae. This condition may present with impaired rotation of the neck, neurological difficulties, or may be asymptomatic.

LB73.2Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of spine
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of spine
Absence of vertebra, not elsewhere classified

LB73.2A.title: Congenital spondylolisthesis
LB73.2A.definition: A condition caused by vertebral malformation, which allows the vertebra to slip forward over the sacrum. This condition may present with lower back pain, or may be asymptomatic.

LB73.2Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of spine, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of spine, unspecified

LB73.29.title: Caudal appendage
LB73.29.definition: A condition caused by development of a malformation on the lower back during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a cutaneous protrusion superior to the buttocks. This condition may be associated with occult spinal dysraphism.

LB73.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax

LB73.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax
Malformations of spine or bony thorax

LB74.0.title: Developmental dysplasia of hip
LB74.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the hip to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by slippage of the hip from the socket. This condition may present with outward turning of the leg, reduced movement on one side of the body, shortness of one leg, uneven skin folds on thigh or buttocks, walking difficulties, or inward rounding of the lower back.
synonyms: congenital dislocation of hip, unilateral, unspecified side

LB74.Z.title: Structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle, unspecified
synonyms: Structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle, unspecified
Structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle

LB74.3.title: Congenital coxa vara
LB74.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the hip joint to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a decrease in the femoral neck-shaft angle. This condition may present with a shortened leg, or a limp.

LB74.Y.title: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle
synonyms: Other specified structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle

LB74.4.title: Congenital coxa valga
LB74.4.definition: A condition caused by failure of the hip joint to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by an increase in the femoral neck-shaft angle.

LB75.0.title: Brachydactyly of fingers
LB75.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the fingers to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by below normal finger length.

LB74.2.title: Unstable hip
LB74.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the hip joint to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by looseness of the hip joint. This condition may present with dislocation, multidirectional intra-operative instability, abductor insufficiency, or neuromuscular disability.
synonyms: predislocation status of hip at birth

LB75.2.title: Symbrachydactyly of hands or feet
LB75.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the digits to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by short digits, which may be webbed. This condition may also present with missing digits, shortened metacarpals, or short limb sections.
synonyms: Symbrachydactyly of hands or feet, unilateral
Symbrachydactyly of hands or feet, bilateral

LB75.1.title: Brachydactyly of toes
LB75.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the toes to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by below normal toe length.

LB78.1.title: Polysyndactyly
LB78.1.definition: Polysyndactyly is a form of preaxial polydactyly of fingers characterised by the presence of a thumb showing the mildest degree of duplication, being broad, bifid or with radially deviated distal phalanx. Syndactyly of various degrees of third-and-fourth fingers is occasionally present. Two forms have been characterised: unilateral and bilateral.
synonyms: syndactyly of multiple and unspecified sites

LB78.0.title: Polydactyly of the thumb
LB78.0.definition: A condition caused by development of supernumerary thumbs during the antenatal period.

LB76.title: Triphalangeal thumb
LB76.definition: A condition caused by failure of the thumb to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a long, finger-like thumb with three phalanges instead of two. Isolated triphalangeal thumbs may be associated with genetic abnormality in the 7q36 region.

LB78.3.title: Polydactyly of toes
LB78.3.definition: Any condition caused by development of supernumerary toes during the antenatal period.

LB78.Y.title: Other specified polydactyly

LB77.title: Hyperphalangy
LB77.definition: Hyperphalangy is a congenital, non-syndromic limb malformation characterized by the presence of an accessory phalanx between metacarpal/metatarsal and proximal phalanx, or between any two other phalanges of a digit, excluding the thumb. Hypherphalangy is almost always bilateral and patients present no more than five digits and no other skeletal anomalies.

LB79.1.title: Webbed fingers
LB79.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the longitudinal interdigital necrosis that normally separates the fingers to during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of two or more fingers that are fused together.
synonyms: syndactyly of fingers without fusion of bone

inclusions: Complex syndactyly of toes with synostosis

LB79.3.title: Webbed toes
LB79.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the longitudinal interdigital necrosis that normally separates the toes during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of two or more toes that are fused together.
synonyms: Simple syndactyly of toes without synostosis
syndactyly of toes without fusion of bone
inclusions: Simple syndactyly of toes without synostosis

LB78.2.title: Postaxial polydactyly of fingers
LB78.2.definition: A condition caused by development of supernumerary fingers during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by fifth digit duplications.

LB80.0.title: Clinodactyly of fingers
LB80.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the fifth finger to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by bending of the fifth finger towards the fourth.

LB90.0.title: Humero-radio-ulnar synostosis
LB90.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the arm bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by direct fusion of the humerus to the ulnar and radial bones of the arm, and consequent inability to straighten the elbow joint. This condition may be associated with thalidomide embryopathy. Confirmation is through observation of humero-radio-ulnar fusion by imaging.

LB81.Y.title: Other specified congenital deformities of toes
synonyms: Other specified congenital deformities of toes

LB90.4.title: Madelung deformity
LB90.4.definition: Madelung disease, or deformity is a predominantly bilateral wrist anomaly characterised by shortened and bowed radii and long ulnae leading to dorsal dislocation of the distal ulna and limited mobility of the wrist and elbow.

LB90.3.title: Radio-ulnar synostosis
LB90.3.definition: A condition caused by failure of the arm bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by direct fusion of the ulnar and radial bones of the arm, and consequent limitation of rotational movement of the forearm. Confirmation is through observation of radio ulnar fusion by imaging.

LB90.5.title: Congenital digital clubbing
LB90.5.definition: Isolated congenital digital clubbing is a rare genodermatosis disorder characterised by enlargement of the terminal segments of fingers and toes with thickened nails without any other abnormality.

LB90.2.title: Humero-ulnar synostosis
LB90.2.definition: A condition caused by failure of the arm bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by direct fusion of the humerus and radial bones of the arm, and consequent inability to straighten the elbow joint. Confirmation is through observation of humero-ulnar fusion by imaging.

LB96.0.title: Congenital bowing of femur
LB96.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the femur to develop correctly during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by abnormal angling of the femur. Confirmation is through observation of the bowed femur by imaging.

LB96.1.title: Congenital bowing of tibia
LB96.1.definition: A condition caused by failure of the tibia to develop correctly during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by abnormal angling of the tibia. Confirmation is through observation of the bowed tibia by imaging.

LB96.Z.title: Congenital bowing of long bones, unspecified
synonyms: Congenital bowing of long bones, unspecified

LB96.Y.title: Other specified congenital bowing of long bones
synonyms: Other specified congenital bowing of long bones

LB97.0.title: Macrodactyly of fingers
LB97.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the fingers to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by overgrowth of bone and soft tissue, resulting in larger than normal fingers. This condition may be asymptomatic.

LB98.00.title: Talipes equinovarus
LB98.00.definition: A condition characterised by a foot that is fixated in adduction, in supination, and in varus. This condition may be associated with intrauterine position, genetic mutation, or can be idiopathic.

LB98.0Z.title: Congenital varus deformities of feet, unspecified
synonyms: Congenital varus deformities of feet, unspecified

LB98.02.title: Metatarsus varus
LB98.02.definition: A condition characterised by medial rotation of the cuneiform bones at the midtarsal joint, with associated medial deviation of the metatarsal, resulting in adduction and supination of the forefoot.

LB98.22.title: Talipes calcaneovalgus
LB98.22.definition: A condition caused by tightness of the muscles of the foot due to resting of the foot in a turned up position during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a foot that is turned upwards towards the shin.

LB98.21.title: Metatarsus valgus
LB98.21.definition: A condition caused by failure of the bones of the foot to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by rotation of the forepart of the foot outward from the midline of the body.

LB98.0Y.title: Other specified congenital varus deformities of feet
synonyms: Other specified congenital varus deformities of feet

LB98.2Z.title: Congenital valgus deformities of feet, unspecified

congenital valgus deformity of foot, unspecified

LB98.2Y.title: Other specified congenital valgus deformities of feet
synonyms: Other specified congenital valgus deformities of feet

LB95.title: Patella aplasia or hypoplasia
LB95.definition: Isolated patella aplasia-hypoplasia is an extremely rare genetic condition characterised by congenital absence or marked reduction of the patellar bone. This condition may present with discomfort or abnormal gait. Confirmation is through verification of the reduced or absent patella by imaging

LB98.20.title: Congenital hallux valgus
LB98.20.definition: A condition caused by failure of the hallux to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by angling of the hallux medial to the metatarsophalangeal joint.

LB98.1.title: Congenital pes planus
LB98.1.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the foot to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by severe rigid flat foot deformity.

LB98.3.title: Congenital pes cavus
LB98.3.definition: A condition characterised by a high arch of the foot that does not flatten with weight bearing.

LB99.3.title: Ulnar hemimelia
LB99.3.definition: Ulnar hemimelia is a congenital ulnar deficiency of the forearm characterised by complete or partial absence of the ulna bone.
synonyms: congenital absence of ulna with or without absence of some distal elements
congenital absence of ulna with or without absence of some, but not all, distal elements

LB99.2.title: Radial hemimelia
LB99.2.definition: Radial hemimelia is a congenital longitudinal deficiency of the radius bone of the forearm characterised by partial or total absence of the radius.
synonyms: congenital absence of radius with or without absence of some distal elements
congenital absence of radius with or without absence of some, but not all, distal elements

LB98.Y.title: Other specified congenital deformities of feet
synonyms: Other specified congenital deformities of feet

LB99.0.title: Amelia of upper limb
LB99.0.definition: A condition caused by the failure of an upper limb to develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by absence of the upper limb.
synonyms: congenital complete absence of upper limb
congenital complete absence of upper limb, unspecified side
transverse deficiency of arm, shoulder level

LB98.4.title: Congenital vertical talus
LB98.4.definition: Isolated congenital vertical talus is a rare pedal deformity recognizable at birth by a dislocation of the talonavicular joint, resulting in a characteristic radiographic near-vertical orientation of the talus.

LB98.5.title: Congenital hammer toe
LB98.5.definition: A condition characterised by angling downwards of the toe.

LB99.4.title: Congenital absence of upper arm or forearm with hand present
LB99.4.definition: A condition caused by the failure of the upper arm and forearm to develop during the antenatal period, but with the hand present. This condition is characterised by direct connection of the hand to the shoulder.

LB99.7.title: Adactyly of hands
LB99.7.definition: A condition caused by failure of the digits on the hand to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by absence of digits on the hand.

LB9A.1.title: Tibial hemimelia
LB9A.1.definition: Tibial hemimelia is a rare congenital anomaly characterised by deficiency of the tibia with a relatively intact fibula.
synonyms: congenital absence of tibia with or without absence of some distal elements
congenital absence of tibia with or without absence of some, but not all, distal elements

LB99.6.title: Acheiria
LB99.6.definition: A condition caused by failure of one or both hands to develop during the antenatal period.
synonyms: congenital absence of hand and finger
congenital absence of hand and wrist

congenital absence of forearm and hand

LB99.8.title: Split hand
LB99.8.definition: A condition caused by malformation of the hand during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a deep median cleft of the hand due to the absence of the central rays.

LB9A.2.title: Fibular hemimelia
LB9A.2.definition: Fibular hemimelia is a congenital longitudinal limb deficiency characterised by complete or partial absence of the fibula bone.
synonyms: congenital absence of fibula with or without absence of some distal elements
congenital absence of fibula with or without absence of some, but not all, distal elements

LB9A.3.title: Congenital absence of thigh or lower leg with foot present
LB9A.3.definition: Any condition caused by the failure of the thigh and lower leg to develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by direct connection of the foot to the hip.

Congenital absence of thigh or lower leg with foot present, bilateral

LB9A.6.title: Split foot
LB9A.6.definition: A condition caused by malformation of the foot during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a deep median cleft of the foot due to the absence of the central rays.

LB9A.8.title: Femoral agenesis or hypoplasia
LB9A.8.definition: Femoral agenesis/hypoplasia is a rare malformation of variable severity ranging from mild hypoplasia to complete absence of the femur.
synonyms: congenital absence of femur with or without absence of some, but not all, distal elements
congenital absence of femur, with or without absence of some distal elements

LB9A.4.title: Apodia

LB9A.5.title: Adactyly of feet
LB9A.5.definition: A condition caused by failure of the digits on the foot to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by absence of digits on the foot.

LC10.title: Dermal melanocytosis
LC10.definition: The presence at birth of functional melanocytes within the dermis. Most commonly this is as a result of incomplete migration of melanocytes to the epidermis as in lumbosacral dermal melanocytosis (Mongolian spot). Less commonly it is due to circumscribed hamartomatous proliferation of melanocytes in the dermis (e.g. Naevus of Ota).

LC50.0.title: Salmon patch
LC50.0.definition: A common skin condition of neonates, characterised by flat, deep-pink localised areas of capillary dilation that occur predominantly on the back of the neck, lower occiput, upper eyelids, upper lip, and bridge of the nose. The areas disappear permanently by about 2 years of age.

LC50.1.title: Port-wine stain
LC50.1.definition: A port-wine stain is defined as a macular telangiectatic area of skin which is present at birth and does not spontaneously involute. Port-wine stains may be localised or extensive and they are often associated with an underlying disorder.

LD20.00.title: Joubert syndrome
LD20.00.definition: Joubert syndrome is a genetic midbrain-hindbrain malformation syndrome characterised by congenital malformation of the brainstem and agenesis or hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis leading to an abnormal respiratory pattern, nystagmus, hypotonia, ataxia, and delay in achieving motor milestones.

LC60.title: Aplasia cutis congenita
LC60.definition: Congenital absence of skin. The commonest form presents as a defect limited to the scalp. It is also a component of a number of genetic syndromes.

LD20.01.title: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia
LD20.01.definition: Nonsyndromic pontocerebellar hypoplasias are a rare heterogeneous group of diseases characterised by hypoplasia and atrophy and/or early neurodegeneration of the cerebellum and pons. Eight subtypes named type 1-8 have been described, generally inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

LD20.1.title: Syndromes with lissencephaly as a major feature
LD20.1.definition: The term lissencephaly covers a group of rare malformations sharing the common feature of anomalies in the appearance of brain convolutions (characterised by simplification or absence of folding) associated with abnormal organisation of the cortical layers as a result of neuronal migration defects during embryogenesis. Children with lissencephaly have feeding and swallowing problems, muscle tone anomalies (early hypotonia and subsequently limb hypertonia), seizures (in particular, infantile spasms) and severe psychomotor retardation. Two large groups can be distinguished: classical lissencephaly (and its variants) and cobblestone lissencephaly.

LD20.3.definition: Any syndrome caused by failure of the prosencephalon to divide in two during the antenatal period. These syndromes may present with closely spaced eyes, cyclopia, flat nasal bridge, single maxillary central incisor, small head size, and clefts of the lip and palate.

LD24.01.definition: Hypochondroplasia is a skeletal dysplasia characterised by disproportionate short stature, mild lumbar lordosis and limited extension of the elbow joints.

LD24.00.title: Achondroplasia
LD24.00.definition: Achondroplasia is the most frequent form of chondrodysplasia and is a type of dwarfism characterised by short limbs, hyperlordosis, short hands, and macrocephaly with high forehead and saddle nose, with normal intellectual development.

LD24.02.title: Thanatophoric dysplasia
LD24.02.definition: Thanatophoric Dysplasia is a severe skeletal disorder that is lethal in the neonatal period. Two clinically defined TD subtypes have been classified: type I (TDI), characterised by micromelia with bowed femurs and, occasionally, by the presence of cloverleaf skull deformity of varying severity and type II (TDII), characterised by micromelia with straight femurs and a moderate to severe cloverleaf skull deformity.

LD24.03.title: Diastrophic dysplasia
LD24.03.definition: Diastrophic dwarfism is a rare autosomal recessive disorder marked by short stature with short extremities (final adult height is 120cm +/- 10cm), and joint malformations leading to multiple joint contractures (principally involving the shoulders, elbows, interphalangeal joints and hips)

LD24.10.title: Osteopetrosis
LD24.10.definition: Osteopetrosis ('marble bone disease') is a descriptive term that refers to a group of rare, heritable disorders of the skeleton characterised by increased bone density on radiographs. Osteopetrotic conditions vary greatly in their presentation and severity, ranging from neonatal onset with life-threatening complications such as bone marrow failure (as in classical or 'malignant' autosomal recessive osteopetrosis) to the incidental finding of osteopetrosis on radiographs (e.g. osteopoikilosis).

LD24.3.title: Spondyloepiphyseal or spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasias
LD24.3.definition: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasias (SED) are a heterogeneous group of congenital chondrodysplasias that specifically affect epiphyses and vertebrae. Their most frequent form is characterised by small neonatal size of ovid vertebrae and overall late growth of bones, more marked in the femoral heads, with a slightly irregular metaphyseal limit. Other clinical forms have been described, some of which were dominant and more or less severe with metaphyseal lesions, while others were recessive and included nephrotic syndrome, lymphopenia, and immune disorders (immune bone dysplasia).
synonyms: Mild spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia due to COL2A1 mutation with early-onset osteoarthritis

LD24.23.title: Yunis-Varon disease
LD24.23.definition: A disease caused by failure of multiple body systems to correctly develop during the antenatal period, due to mutation of the FIG4 gene. This disease is characterised by cleidocranial dysplasia, digital anomalies, and severe neurological involvement.

LD24.22.title: Cherubism
LD24.22.definition: Cherubism is a benign fibro-osseous hereditary disorder of childhood, limited to the lower half of the face, the maxilla and particularly the mandible, with bilateral painless swelling of jaws (giving the so-called cherubic look) associated with multicystic bone tumours and eyes-to-heaven appearance. Dentition is also abnormal at the sites concerned: tooth agenesis, noneruption, displacement, root resorption and malocclusions are common.

LD24.4.title: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasias
LD24.4.definition: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasias are a heterogeneous group of disorders associated with walking and growth disturbances that become evident during the second year of life. The disorders are characterised by platyspondyly (flattened vertebrae) and marked hip and knee metaphyseal lesions. The different forms of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia are distinguished by the localization and severity of involvement of the affected metaphyses.
synonyms: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with severe genu valgum
Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia - bowed forearms - facial dysmorphism

Dysplasia of head of femur, Meyer type

LD24.60.title: Pseudoachondroplasia
LD24.60.definition: Pseudoachondroplasia is a chondrodysplasia characterised by severe growth deficiency and deformations such as bow legs and hyperlordosis.

LD24.8Y.title: Other specified acromelic dysplasias
synonyms: Intellectual deficit - balding - patella luxation - acromicria

LD24.80.title: Langer-Giedion syndrome
LD24.80.definition: Langer-Giedion syndrome or trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type 2 is a chromosomal anomaly syndrome characterised by the association of intellectual deficit and numerous other anomalies including redundant skin, multiple cartilaginous exostoses, characteristic facies and cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses.

LD24.B1.title: Asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy
LD24.B1.definition: Asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy, also called Jeune syndrome, is a short-rib dysplasia characterised by a narrow thorax, short limbs and radiological skeletal abnormalities including "trident" aspect of the acetabula and metaphyseal changes.
synonyms: Asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy of the newborn

LD24.9.title: Acromesomelic dysplasias
LD24.9.definition: A group of rare disorders characterised by shortening of the bones of the forearms, lower legs, hands and feet.

LD24.61.title: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasias
LD24.61.definition: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasias (MED/EDMs) are characterised by epiphyseal anomalies causing joint pain early in life, recurrent osteochondritis and early arthrosis. The EDMs are a heterogeneous group of diseases with variable expression classed as MED/EDMs 1-6.
synonyms: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia due to collagen 9 anomaly
Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia with severe proximal femoral dysplasia

LD24.B0.title: Short rib-polydactyly syndrome
LD24.B0.definition: Short rib-polydactyly syndromes are a group of bone malformations characterised by a narrow thorax and polydactyly (usually preaxial). Prevalence as a group is unknown. The group is heterogeneous and includes Jeune syndrome and Ellis-Van Creveld syndrome, neither of which are lethal, together with lethal chondrodysplasias: Saldino-Noonan (type 1), Majewski (type 2), Verma-Naumoff (type 3) and Beemer-Langer (type 4).

LD24.C.title: Bent bone dysplasias
LD24.C.definition: Any syndromes are characterised by poor mineralization of the skull, craniosynostosis, hypoplastic pubis and clavicles, osteopenia, bent long bones, low-set ears, hypertelorism, midface hypoplasia, prematurely erupted fetal teeth, and micrognathia. These syndromes may be associated with mutation of the FGFR2 gene.

LD24.D.title: Slender bone dysplasias
LD24.D.definition: Any syndrome characterised by dwarfism, thin bones, multiple fractures, and prenatal or early postnatal death.
synonyms: Hypoparathyroidism - short stature - intellectual deficit - seizures

LD24.E.title: Bone dysplasias with multiple joint dislocations
LD24.E.definition: Any syndrome characterised by malformation of the musculoskeletal system during the antenatal period, which includes the dislocations of multiple joints.
synonyms: Bone dysplasias with multiple joint dislocations

LD24.51.title: Hypochondrogenesis
LD24.51.definition: A condition caused by failure of the skeletal system to correctly develop during the antenatal period, due to mutation of the COL2A1 gene. This condition is characterised by a small body, short limbs, underdeveloped lungs, flat and oval-shaped face, hypertelorism, micrognathia, enlarged abdomen, and ossification in the spine and pelvis. This condition may also present with a cleft palate.

LD24.F.title: Progressive ossification of skin, skeletal muscle, fascia, tendons or ligaments
synonyms: Progressive ossification of skin, skeletal muscle, fascia, tendons or ligaments

LD24.G0.title: Pfeiffer syndrome
LD24.G0.definition: Pfeiffer syndrome (associated with mutations in the FGFR1 and 2 gene) is a syndromic form of craniosynostosis characterised by the association of craniosynostosis. Often pansynostosis. Severe midface hypoplasia. Broad and deviated thumbs and big toes, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes. Hydrocephaly may be found occasionally, along with severe ocular proptosis, ankylosed elbows.

LD24.G1.title: Crouzon disease
LD24.G1.definition: Crouzon disease is a form of syndromic craniosynostosis characterised by craniosynostosis and facial hypoplasia.

LD24.H.title: Dysostoses with predominant vertebral and costal involvement
LD24.H.definition: Any syndrome characterised by malformation of the musculoskeletal system during the antenatal period, which includes dysgenesis of the vertebrae and intercostal cartilage.
synonyms: Dysostoses with predominant vertebral and costal involvement
Syndromic progressive noninfectious anterior vertebral fusion
exclusions: Spondylocostal dysostosis - anal and genitourinary malformations

LD24.G2.title: Apert syndrome
LD24.G2.definition: Apert syndrome is a syndromic craniosynostosis associated with mutations in the FGFR2 gene and characterised by premature closure of coronal suture and a later onset of pansynostosis. Pathognomonic is an osseous and membranous syndactyly of at least Digitus II-IV (fingers and toes). High incidence of midface hypoplasia with orbital and facial stenosis, cleft palate, vertebral fusion. Mental deficits in 30%.

LD24.J0.title: Nail-patella syndrome
LD24.J0.definition: Nail patella syndrome is a hereditary osteo-onychodysplasia characterised by nail dysplasia with triangular lunula, hypoplastic or absent patellas, iliac exostoses (`iliac horns') and dysplastic elbows.

LD24.Z.title: Syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
synonyms: Syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
Syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature

LD24.K0.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta
LD24.K0.definition: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) comprises a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterised by increased bone fragility, low bone mass, and susceptibility to bone fractures with variable severity. The most clinically relevant characteristic of all types of OI is bone fragility, which manifests as multiple spontaneous fractures.
synonyms: blue sclera with fragility of bone and deafness
white blue sclera - fragility of bone - deafness

LD24.JY.title: Other specified patellar dysostoses
synonyms: Patella aplasia - coxa vara - tarsal synostosis

LD25.00.title: Oral-facial-digital syndrome
LD25.00.definition: A condition caused by failure of the head and digits to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition may be associated with cleft or lobed tongue, noncancerous tumours or nodules of the tongue, abnormal shape or number of teeth, cleft palate, hyperplastic frenula of the lip or gums, cleft lip, hypertelorism, wide nose with broad, flat nasal bridge, syndactyly, brachydactyly, clinodactyly, polydactyly, polycystic kidney disease, neurological problems, bone abnormalities, vision loss, or heart defects.

LD24.KZ.title: Genetic bone diseases with decreased bone density, unspecified
synonyms: Genetic bone diseases with decreased bone density, unspecified
Genetic bone diseases with decreased bone density

LD24.Y.title: Other specified syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature
synonyms: Other specified syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature

LD25.2.title: Acrofacial dysostoses
LD25.2.definition: Any syndrome caused by failure of the face and limbs to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LD25.3.title: Craniofacial dysostoses
LD25.3.definition: Syndromes caused by abnormal development of skull and facial bones. They may present with acrocephaly, exophthalmos, hypertelorism, strabismus, parrot-beaked nose, or hypoplastic maxilla. Non-syndromic craniosynostosis, which is predominantly sporadic, is coded elsewhere.

LD25.Y.title: Other specified syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature
synonyms: Other specified syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature

LD25.Z.title: Syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
synonyms: Syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
Syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature

LD26.0.title: Combined reduction defects of upper and lower limbs
synonyms: Combined reduction defects of upper and lower limbs

LD26.2.title: Syndromes with limb duplication, polydactyly, syndactyly or triphalangism
LD26.2.definition: Any syndrome caused by failure of the limbs to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These syndromes are characterised by supernumerary limbs or digits, fused digits, or supernumerary phalanges.
synonyms: Syndromes with limb duplication, polydactyly, syndactyly or triphalangism
Mirror polydactyly - vertebral segmentation - limbs defects
Familial triphalangeal thumbs - big toe duplication
Polydactyly of a triphalangeal thumb, unilateral
Polydactyly of a triphalangeal thumb, bilateral

LD26.1.title: Complex brachydactylies
LD26.1.definition: A disease caused by failure of the digits to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This disease is characterised by multiple digits of below normal length. This condition may be associated with mutation in the GDF5 gene.
synonyms: Brachydactyly types B and E combined

LD26.41.title: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita
LD26.41.definition: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, comprises nonprogressive congenital conditions characterised by multiple joint contractures. The term is currently used in connection with a very heterogeneous group of disorders that all include multiple congenital joint contractures. The major cause of arthrogryposis is fetal akinesia due to fetal abnormalities (e.g. neurogenic, muscle, or connective tissue abnormalities; mechanical limitations to movement) or maternal disorders (e.g. infection, drugs, trauma, other maternal illnesses). Generalised fetal akinesia can also lead to polyhydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, micrognathia, ocular hypertelorism, and short umbilical cord. Lack of fetal movement causes extra connective tissue to develop around the joint, limiting movement and further aggravating the joint contracture.
synonyms: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with whistling face

LD26.5.title: Constriction rings
LD26.5.definition: A condition caused by entangling of fibrous bands of the amniotic sac around a developing fetus. This condition may present with circular indentation around a digit or limb, swelling, restriction of the lymphatic or venous flow, limb development defects, or in utero amputation.

LD27.00.title: Incontinentia pigmenti
LD27.00.definition: Incontinentia pigmenti is an X-linked dominant gene disorder due to abnormalities of the NF-kappa-B (NEMO) gene on chromosome Xq28. It is lethal in male fetuses but the presence of a normal second X chromosome in females results in a mosaicism which is compatible with life. Affected females present in infancy with skin blisters in linear arrays (Blaschko lines) typically on the scalp and limbs. Within the first few months of life these are succeeded by warty changes and hyperpigmentation. These tend to resolve over time, often leaving atrophic streaks. Associated features include abnormal dentition, ocular defects and a variety of neurological complications.

LD26.Z.title: Syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
synonyms: Syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature, unspecified
Syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature

LD26.60.title: Angio-osteohypertrophic syndrome
LD26.60.definition: Angio-osteohypertrophic (AOH) syndrome is a congenital vascular bone syndrome characterised by the presence of vascular malformations in a limb resulting in limb overgrowth. Depending on whether the malformations are slow flow venous or fast flow arteriovenous the syndrome may be divided into two subtypes, Klippel-Trénaunay and Parkes-Weber syndromes respectively. Some cases of the latter are associated with mutations in the RASA1 gene.

LD27.03.title: Hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Clouston type
LD27.03.definition: Clouston syndrome (or hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia) is an inherited disorder characterised by the clinical triad of nail dystrophy, alopecia, and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.

LD26.6Y.title: Other specified congenital vascular bone syndromes
synonyms: Other specified congenital vascular bone syndromes
Congenital vascular bone syndrome with limb overgrowth
Congenital vascular bone syndrome with limb shortening

LD26.Y.title: Other specified syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature
synonyms: Other specified syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature

LD27.02.title: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
LD27.02.definition: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia is a genetic disorder of ectoderm development characterised by malformation of ectodermal structures such as skin, hair, teeth and sweat glands. It comprises three clinically almost indistinguishable subtypes with impaired sweating as the key symptom: Christ-Siemens-Touraine syndrome (X-linked), autosomal recessive and autosomal dominant hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, as well as a fourth rare subtype with immunodeficiency as the key symptom.
synonyms: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia - hypothyroidism - ciliary dyskinesia

LD27.01.title: Cronkhite-Canada syndrome
LD27.01.definition: Cronkhite-Canada syndrome (CCS) is a sporadically occurring, noninherited disorder of generalised gastrointestinal polyps (hamartomas), cutaneous pigmentation, alopecia, and onychodystrophy. The possibility of progression to cancer is considered to be low. Chronic diarrhea and protein-losing enteropathy are often observed.

LD27.1.title: Xeroderma pigmentosum
LD27.1.definition: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is a rare genodermatosis characterised by extreme sensitivity to ultraviolet (UV)-induced changes in the skin and eyes, and multiple skin cancers. It is subdivided into 8 complementation groups, according to the affected gene: XPA to XPG, and XP variant (XPV). The severity of the clinical manifestations and the age of onset are extremely variable and are in part dependent on exposure to sunlight and the complementation group.

LD27.5.definition: A heterogeneous group of inherited diseases characterised by the presence of multiple hamartomata and associated with an increased risk of malignancy.

Follicular atrophoderma and basal cell carcinoma syndrome [Bazex]

LD27.3.definition: Genetic syndromes in which excessive non-androgen-dependent hair growth is associated with other abnormalities.
synonyms: Cervical hypertrichosis – peripheral sensory and motor neuropathy

LD27.2.definition: Hereditary disorders in which ichthyosis is associated with significant other abnormalities.

LD28.10.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, classical type
LD28.10.definition: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, classic type is a type of Ehlers-Danlos syndromes (EDS), a heterogeneous group of hereditary connective tissue diseases characterised by joint hyperlaxity, cutaneous hyperelasticity and tissue fragility, and is characterised by the following major clinical diagnostic criteria: hyperextensible skin, atrophic cutaneous scars due to tissue fragility and joint hyperlaxity.

LD27.6Z.title: Genetic lipodystrophy, unspecified
synonyms: Lipodystrophy due to peptidic growth factors deficiency
Combined insulin, insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) and epidermal growth factor (EGF) deficiency
Werner-like syndrome due to combined growth factor deficiency
Mandibuloacral dysplasia with type A lipodystrophy
Mandibuloacral dysplasia with type B lipodystrophy
Joint contractures - Muscular atrophy - microcytic anaemia - Panniculitis-induced lipodystrophy syndrome [JMP]

synonyms: Congenital onychodysplasia of the index fingers
COIF - [Congenital onychodysplasia of the index fingers] syndrome
Nail dystrophy resulting from epidermolysis bullosa classified elsewhere
Nail involvement in other specified genetic disease

LD28.00.title: Congenital contractural arachnodactyly
LD28.00.definition: Congenital contractural arachnodactyly (CCA, Beals syndrome) is a connective tissue disorder characterised by multiple flexion contractures, arachnodactyly, severe kyphoscoliosis, abnormal pinnae and muscular hypoplasia. Although the clinical features can be similar to Marfan syndrome (MFS), multiple joint contractures (especially of the elbow, knee, and finger joints), and crumpled ears in the absence of significant aortic root dilatation are characteristic of Beals syndrome and rarely found in MFS.

LD28.01.title: Marfan syndrome
LD28.01.definition: Marfan syndrome is a systemic disease of connective tissue characterised by a variable combination of cardiovascular, musculo-skeletal, ophthalmic and pulmonary manifestations. Cardiovascular involvement is characterised by 1) progressive dilation of the aorta accompanied by an increased risk of aortic dissection, which affects prognosis and 2) mitral insufficiency. Skeletal involvement is often the first sign of the disease and can include dolichostenomelia, large size, arachnodactyly, joint hypermobility, scoliotic deformations, acetabulum protrusion, thoracic deformity, dolichocephaly of the anteroposterior axis, micrognathism or malar hypoplasia. Ophthalmic involvement results in axile myopia, which can lead to retinal detachment and lens displacement.

LD2A.0.title: Ovotesticular disorder of sex development
LD2A.0.definition: Ovotesticular disorder of sex development, formerly called true hermaphroditism, is a rare cause of genital ambiguity characterised by the presence of ovarian and testicular tissue in an individual, leading to development of both male and female structures.

LD2A.Z.title: Malformative disorders of sex development, unspecified
synonyms: Malformative disorders of sex development, unspecified
Ambiguous genitalia due to developmental anomalies

LD2A.2.title: Testicular agenesis
LD2A.2.definition: A rare 46,XY disorder of gonadal development characterized by congenital complete absence of testicular tissue in an individual with an otherwise male phenotype and normal karyotype. In addition, a small penis is a frequent finding in anorchid patients. Typical hormonal characteristics are elevated basal levels of gonadotropins (especially FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone), low concentration of testosterone, and lack of increase of plasma testosterone in response to hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) administration. The GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) stimulation test induces a prolonged increase in FSH and LH (luteinizing hormone) levels.

LD2A.1.definition: This is any congenital developmental disorder of the reproductive system characterised by a progressive loss of primordial germ cells on the developing gonads of an embryo.
synonyms: 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis - motor and sensory neuropathy
