KA61.title: Other bacterial infections of the fetus or newborn

KA82.title: Intracranial nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn
KA82.definition: Intraventricular (nontraumatic) haemorrhage of the fetus and newborn is a condition characterised by bleeding within the skull of a newborn that is not due to injury causing physical damage.
exclusions: intracranial haemorrhage due to birth injury
Intracranial haemorrhage due to head trauma

KA85.title: Hydrops fetalis due to haemolytic disease
KA85.definition: A fetal condition characterised by an accumulation of fluid or oedema in at least two fetal compartments, including subcutaneous compartments, the pleura, the pericardium, or the abdomen, due to the antibody-mediated break-down of fetal red blood cells.
exclusions: Hydrops fetalis not due to haemolytic disease

KA84.title: Haemolytic disease of fetus or newborn
KA84.definition: A paediatric alloimmune condition characterised by the break-down of red blood cells by IgG antibodies which are transmitted from mother to child via the placenta.

KA63.title: Fungal infection of fetus or newborn
KA63.definition: Any condition affecting fetuses or newborns, caused by an infection with a fungal agent.

KA83.title: Certain specified neonatal haemorrhages
KA83.definition: Any other condition characterised by bleeding in a newborn.
exclusions: Pulmonary haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period

KA87.title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia
KA87.definition: A condition characterised as an increased level of bilirubin above 85 µmol/l (5 mg/dL) which manifests as yellowing of the eyes, skin, and other tissues of a newborn due to excessive break-down of red blood cells for any other reason not classified elsewhere.

KA80.title: Fetal blood loss
KA80.definition: Fetal blood loss is a loss of blood from the fetal circulation during pregnancy, labour, or delivery. Due to the small volume of fetal blood that is present, even a small loss can lead to anaemia or fetal death.

KA64.title: Parasitic diseases in the fetus or newborn
KA64.definition: Any condition affecting fetuses or newborns, caused by an infection with a parasite.

KA8F.title: Neonatal vitamin K deficiency
KA8F.definition: There are 3 forms of vitamin K–deficiency bleeding (VKDB) of the newborn. Early VKDB (haemorrhagic disease of the newborn) that occurs at 1-14 days of age. The most common sites of bleeding are the gastrointestinal tract, mucosal and cutaneous tissue, the umbilical stump, and the post-circumcision site. Late VKDB most commonly occurs at 2-12 weeks of age, although cases can occur up to 6 months. The most common site of bleeding is intracranial, although cutaneous and gastrointestinal bleeding may be initial manifestation. The third form of VKDB occurs at birth or shortly thereafter. It is secondary to maternal intake of medications (warfarin, phenobarbital, phenytoin) that cross the placenta.

KA83.0.title: Neonatal bleeding originating in the mouth, nose or pharynx
synonyms: Neonatal bleeding originating in the mouth, nose or pharynx
exclusions: Neonatal haematemesis or melaena due to swallowed maternal blood

KA89.title: Transient neonatal thrombocytopaenia
KA89.definition: A rare paediatric condition characterised by a temporary relative decrease in the number of platelets in the blood associated with either increased destruction or decreased production of platelets in a newborn.

KA8A.title: Polycythaemia neonatorum
KA8A.definition: Polycythaemia of the neonate represents an excessive quality of circulating red blood cells due to excessive marrow production and haematocrits that exceed ~60%.

KB20.title: Intrauterine hypoxia
KB20.definition: Intrauterine hypoxia occurs when the fetus is deprived of an adequate supply of oxygen. This may occur with prolapse or occlusion of the umbilical cord, placental infarction and maternal smoking. This can lead to damage of the central nervous system and neonatal encephalopathy, which increases the risk of mortality.
exclusions: Intracranial nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus or newborn

KB00.title: Neonatal cerebral ischaemia
KB00.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by insufficient blood flow to the brain of a newborn to meet metabolic demand.

KB23.title: Respiratory distress of newborn
KB23.definition: A condition characterised by developmental insufficiency of surfactant associated proteins or surfactant production and structural immaturity in the lungs.

KB08.title: Disorders of muscle tone of newborn
KB08.definition: A group of paediatric conditions characterised by abnormal muscle tone in a newborn.

KB28.title: Pulmonary haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period
KB28.definition: A condition characterised by bleeding from the lung which begins during the period of time around childbirth, especially the five months before and one month after birth.
exclusions: Acute idiopathic pulmonary haemorrhage in infants over 28 days of age

KB27.title: Pulmonary air leak or related conditions originating in the perinatal period
KB27.definition: Clinical syndrome due to free air from rupture of overdistended alveoli tracking into pulmonary interstitium, mediastinum, pleural cavity or subcutaneous tissues.

KB2J.title: Airway obstruction in the neonate due to airway abnormality

KB26.title: Neonatal aspiration syndromes
KB26.definition: Aspiration of meconium, blood, amniotic fluids and gastric contents in a neonate resulting in clinical symptoms from airway obstruction (atelectasis, air trapping and air leaks), parenchymal injury (pneumonitis), right-to-left shunting, and ventilation-perfusion mismatch.

KB29.title: Chronic respiratory disease originating in the perinatal period
KB29.definition: A group of conditions associated with the respiratory system which begin during the period of time around childbirth, especially the five months before and one month after birth, and which lasts for at least 3 months.

KB2A.title: Apnoea of newborn
KB2A.definition: Any condition characterised by suspension of external breathing in a newborn (premature or term) which is not classified elsewhere

KB23.0.title: Respiratory distress syndrome of newborn
KB23.0.definition: Respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) is an acute illness, usually of preterm infants, due to pulmonary surfactant deficiency, developing within 4-6 hours of birth, and is characterised by respiratory distress (tachypnoea, intercostal and sternal retractions, expiratory grunt, and cyanosis) with abnormal chest radiograph showing diffuse reticulogranular densities and air bronchograms, evidence of reduced lung compliance and functional residual capacity, evidence of abnormal gas exchange (hypoxaemia, hypercapnia, cyanosis) of sufficient severity to require oxygen and/or continuous or intermittent positive pressure ventilatory support for more than 24 hours.

KB40.title: Neonatal cardiac failure
KB40.definition: Cardiac failure originating in the neonatal period

KB61.title: Transitory neonatal disorders of calcium or magnesium metabolism
KB61.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn associated with abnormal chemical reactions in the body disrupting the normal processes of enzyme catalyzed reactions to utilize calcium and magnesium for other body functions.

KB60.2.title: Neonatal diabetes mellitus
KB60.2.definition: Neonatal diabetes mellitus (NDM) is a monogenic form of diabetes that occurs in the first 6 months of life. It is a rare condition occurring in only one in 100,000 to 500,000 live births. Infants with NDM do not produce enough insulin, leading to an increase in blood glucose. NDM can be mistaken for the much more common type 1 diabetes, but type 1 diabetes usually occurs later than the first 6 months of life. In about half of those with NDM, the condition is lifelong and is called permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus (PNDM). In the rest of those with NDM, the condition is transient and disappears during infancy but can reappear later in life; this type of NDM is called transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (TNDM).

KB60.title: Transitory disorders of carbohydrate metabolism specific to fetus or newborn
KB60.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn or infant associated with abnormal chemical reactions in the body disrupting the process of getting or making energy from consumed carbohydrates.

KB63.title: Certain specified transitory neonatal electrolyte or metabolic disturbances
KB63.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary abnormality in the normal processes of enzyme catalyzed reactions within tissue cells (metabolism) or with the levels of minerals in the blood or other body fluids.
synonyms: Certain specified transitory neonatal electrolyte or metabolic disturbances

KB86.title: Postnatal intestinal perforation
KB86.definition: Postnatal intestinal perforation is a complete penetration of wall of the large or small intestine, often resulting in the leakage of luminal contents into the abdominal cavity.

KB81.title: Oesophagitis in newborn
KB81.definition: Oesophagitis is inflammation of the oesophagus. If left untreated, this condition can cause ulcers or scarring of the oesophagus.

KB63.3.title: Disturbances of potassium balance of newborn
KB63.3.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally high or low levels of potassium in the blood in a newborn, when the normal range is defined as 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L.

KB85.title: Prenatal intrauterine intestinal perforation
KB85.definition: In-utero or prenatal bowel perforation results in a chemical peritonitis (meconium peritonitis) from peritoneal leakage of sterile meconium. Meconium peritonitis results from prenatal intestinal perforation nearly always involving the small bowel.

KB62.title: Transitory neonatal disorders of thyroid function
KB62.definition: A group of paediatric conditions in which there is a temporary disorder in a newborn or infant associated with the thyroid.

KB88.title: Necrotising enterocolitis of newborn
KB88.definition: This is a fulminating disease of neonates in which there is extensive mucosal ulceration, pseudomembrane formation, submucosal haemorrhage, and necrosis usually of the right colon, caecum, terminal ileum, and appendix (ENTEROCOLITIS), possibly due to perinatal intestinal ischemia and bacterial invasion. The entire colon, small intestine, stomach, and oesophagus may also be affected. Most infants are premature or suffer from respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, or hypoxia. Symptoms (apparent during the first few weeks of life) include abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and melaena; there may be apnoea, lethargy, temperature instability, tachycardia, tachypnoea, and a fall in blood pressure. The disorder may progress to perforation and peritonitis.

KC41.title: Miscellaneous specified conditions of integument specific to fetus or newborn
synonyms: Miscellaneous specified conditions of integument specific to fetus or newborn

KC40.title: Miscellaneous skin disorders in the neonate
synonyms: Miscellaneous skin disorders in the neonate

KC21.title: Inflammatory dermatoses of the newborn
KC21.definition: A range of inflammatory skin disorders presenting in the neonatal period.

KB63.2.title: Disturbances of sodium balance of newborn
KB63.2.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by abnormally high or low levels of sodium in the blood in a newborn, when the normal range is defined as 135 to 150 mEq/L.

KB87.title: Intestinal obstruction of newborn
KB87.definition: Any other impairment, arrest, or reversal of the normal flow of intestinal toward the anal canal in a newborn

KD12.title: Hypothermia of newborn
KD12.definition: Core body temperature of a newborn below -1SD (36.0 degrees C) compared with mean temperature (36.5 degrees of C).

KD30.title: Birth depression
KD30.definition: A condition characterised by cardiorespiratory and neurological depression in a newborn.

KD3C.title: Vomiting in newborn
KD3C.definition: A paediatric condition characterised by the forceful expulsion of the contents of the stomach through the mouth and sometimes the nose of a newborn.

LA00.title: Anencephaly or similar anomalies
LA00.definition: A malformation of the nervous system caused by the failure of neuropore closure. Infants are born with intact spinal cord, cerebellum, and brainstem, but lack formation of neural structures above this level. The skull is only partially formed but the eyes are usually normal.

KD32.title: Feeding problems of newborn
KD32.definition: A lack of interest in feeding or a problem receiving the proper amount of nutrition in a newborn.

KD39.title: Complications of intrauterine procedures, not elsewhere classified
KD39.definition: A group of conditions characterised as an unfavourable evolution of a condition (complication) due to a health intervention applied inside of the uterus.
exclusions: fetus and newborn affected by placental separation and haemorrhage due to intrauterine procedures

LA00.0.title: Anencephaly
LA00.0.definition: Anencephaly is a neural tube defect, characterised by the total or partial absence of the cranial vault and the covering skin, the brain being missing or reduced to a small mass. Most cases are stillborn, although some infants have been reported to survive for a few hours. In most cases autopsy findings reveal absence of adrenal glands. Anencephaly is likely to be multifactorial, the result of gene-environment interactions. Familial cases with a seemingly autosomal recessive mode of inheritance have been described but most cases are sporadic. Folic acid and zinc deficiencies, as well as maternal obesity, have been shown to be risk factors.

LA02.title: Spina bifida
LA02.definition: Spina bifida is the most common of a group of birth defects called neural tube defects. Spina bifida affects the backbone and, sometimes, the spinal cord. Aperta spina bifida defines the dorsal malclosure of vertebrae, associated with various degrees of spine defects. A pocket of skin may form, containing meninges (meningocele) or spinal cord and meninges (myelomeningocele). Different subtypes are distinguished according to the location of the defect. Consequences are paraplegia (paralysed lower limbs), hydrocephaly, Chiari malformation (result of the attached spine during life in utero), urinary and anorectal incontinence. The intensity of signs varies greatly with the level and extent of the lesion.

LA05.5.title: Abnormal neuronal migration
LA05.5.definition: Any condition caused by abnormal migration of neuronal cells during the antenatal period. These conditions may present with poor muscle tone and motor function, seizures, developmental delays, mental retardation, failure to grow and thrive, difficulties with feeding, swelling in the extremities or microcephaly.

LA05.title: Cerebral structural developmental anomalies
LA05.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the brain to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA02.0.title: Spina bifida cystica
LA02.0.definition: A condition caused by failure of the neural tube to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by nerve damage and the presence of meningoceles on the back. This condition may present with physical or mental impairment.

LA07.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord or vertebral column
LA07.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the neurenteric canal, spinal cord and vertebral column to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA04.title: Congenital hydrocephalus
LA04.definition: A disease caused by failure of the brain to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a rapid increase in head circumference or an unusually large head size due to excessive accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. This condition may also present with vomiting, sleepiness, irritability, downward deviation of the eyes, or seizures. Confirmation is through observation of cerebrospinal fluid within cerebral ventricles by imaging.

LA11.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the anterior segment of eye
LA11.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the anterior segment of the eye to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA13.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the posterior segment of eye
LA13.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the posterior segment of the eye to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by clinical, functional, or morphological changes to the posterior segment of the eye.

LA06.title: Cerebellar structural developmental anomalies
LA06.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the brain to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA10.title: Structural developmental anomalies of ocular globes
LA10.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the ocular globes to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA12.title: Structural developmental anomalies of lens or zonula
LA12.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the lens and zonula to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA21.title: Minor anomalies of pinnae
LA21.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the pinna to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by asymptomatic abnormalities of the visible part of the ear.

KD3B.title: Fetal death, cause not specified
KD3B.definition:
Fetal death is death of a fetus prior to its complete expulsion or extraction from a woman, irrespective of the duration of pregnancy. Fetal death may be diagnosed in utero by absence of fetal heart sounds, confirmed by imaging techniques where available, or after delivery by absence of signs of life after the complete expulsion or extraction from the woman.

Stillbirth is the complete expulsion or extraction from a woman of a fetus, following its death prior to the complete expulsion or extraction, at 22 or more completed weeks of gestation.

LA14.1.title: Structural developmental anomalies of lacrimal apparatus
LA14.1.definition: This refers to structural developmental anomalies of the physiologic system containing the orbital structures for tear production and drainage.

LA22.title: Structural developmental anomalies of ear causing hearing impairment
LA22.definition: Any condition caused by the failure of the ear to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by hearing impairment.

LA40.title: Cleft lip
LA40.definition: Isolated cleft lip is a fissure type embryopathy extending from the upper lip to the nasal base.

LA31.title: Structural developmental anomalies of mouth or tongue
LA31.definition: Embryo fetal anomalies affecting structure of maxillo-labial or mandibular tissues or the tongue.

LA14.title: Structural developmental anomalies of eyelid, lacrimal apparatus or orbit
LA14.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the eyelid lacrimal apparatus and orbit to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA71.title: Structural developmental anomalies of larynx
LA71.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the larynx to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA13.8.title: Certain congenital malformations of posterior segment of eye
synonyms: Certain congenital malformations of posterior segment of eye

LA70.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the nose or cavum
LA70.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the nose and cavum to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA41.title: Cleft lip and alveolus
LA41.definition: Cleft lip and alveolus is a fissure type embryopathy that involves the upper lip, nasal base and alveolar ridge in variable degrees.

LA74.title: Structural developmental anomalies of bronchi
LA74.definition: This refers to the structural developmental anomalies of the passage of airway in the respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.

LA30.title: Structural developmental anomalies of teeth and periodontal tissues

LA30.5.title: Anomalies in tooth resorption or loss

LA80.title: Anomalous position-orientation of heart
LA80.definition: A congenital cardiovascular finding or malformation in which there is an abnormality of the position or orientation of heart.

LA42.title: Cleft palate
LA42.definition: Cleft palate is a fissure type embryopathy that affects the soft and hard palate to varying degrees.

LA85.title: Congenital anomaly of an atrioventricular or ventriculo-arterial connection
LA85.definition:
A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which one or more of the following connections is abnormal 1) the morphologically right atrium to the morphologically right ventricle, 2) the morphologically left atrium to the morphologically left ventricle, 3) the morphologically right ventricle to the pulmonary trunk, 4) the morphologically left ventricle to the aorta.

This excludes codes for hearts with a univentricular atrioventricular connection (mitral atresia, tricuspid atresia and double inlet ventricle), as these are listed under Functionally Univentricular Heart.

LA75.title: Structural developmental anomalies of lungs
LA75.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the lungs to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA85.0.title: Discordant atrioventricular connections
LA85.0.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the morphologically right atrium connects to the morphologically left ventricle and the morphologically left atrium connects to the morphologically right ventricle.

LA87.title: Congenital anomaly of an atrioventricular valve or atrioventricular septum
LA87.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is an abnormality of the atrioventricular valve or atrioventricular septum.

LA85.2.title: Double outlet right ventricle
LA85.2.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which both great arteries arise entirely or predominantly from the morphologically right ventricle.

LA88.2.title: Tetralogy of Fallot
LA88.2.definition:
A group of congenital cardiovascular malformations with biventricular atrioventricular alignments or connections characterised by anterosuperior deviation of the conal or outlet septum or its fibrous remnant, narrowing or atresia of the pulmonary outflow, a ventricular septal defect of the malalignment type, and biventricular origin of the aorta.

Additional information: tetralogy of Fallot will always have a ventricular septal defect, narrowing or atresia of the pulmonary outflow, aortic override, and most often right ventricular hypertrophy.

LA87.0.title: Congenital anomaly of tricuspid valve
LA87.0.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is an abnormality of the tricuspid valve.
inclusions: congenital anomaly of tricuspid subvalvular apparatus

LA86.2.title: Anomalous pulmonary venous connection
LA86.2.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which one or more pulmonary vein does not connect normally to the morphologically left atrium.

LA85.4.title: Common arterial trunk
LA85.4.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which a single arterial trunk arises from the heart, giving origin sequentially to the coronary arteries, one or more pulmonary arteries, and the systemic arterial circulation.

LA86.title: Congenital anomaly of mediastinal vein
LA86.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is an abnormality of a mediastinal vein including but not limited to: pulmonary veins, caval veins, coronary sinus, hepatic veins connecting to the heart, brachiocephalic veins, azygos veins, and/or levo-atrial cardinal veins.

LA87.1.title: Congenital anomaly of mitral valve
LA87.1.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation in which there is an abnormality of the mitral valve.

LA88.4.title: Ventricular septal defect
LA88.4.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation in which there is a hole or pathway between the ventricular chambers.

LA8A.title: Congenital anomaly of a ventriculo-arterial valve or adjacent regions
LA8A.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of a ventriculo-arterial valve or its immediate subvalvar and supravalvar regions.

LA88.title: Congenital anomaly of a ventricle or the ventricular septum
LA88.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation in which there is an abnormality of a ventricle and/or the ventricular septum. The ventricles include the ventricular inlet, ventricular body and ventricular outflow tract.

LA89.title: Functionally univentricular heart
LA89.definition:
The term “functionally univentricular heart” describes a spectrum of congenital cardiovascular malformations in which the ventricular mass may not readily lend itself to partitioning that commits one ventricular pump to the systemic circulation, and another to the pulmonary circulation.

Additional information: a heart may be functionally univentricular because of its anatomy or because of the lack of feasibility or lack of advisability of surgically partitioning the ventricular mass. Common lesions in this category typically include double inlet right ventricle (DIRV), double inlet left ventricle (DILV), tricuspid atresia, mitral atresia, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Other lesions which sometimes may be considered to be a functionally univentricular heart include complex forms of atrioventricular septal defect, double outlet right ventricle, congenitally corrected transposition, pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum, and other cardiovascular malformations. Specific diagnostic codes should be used whenever possible, and not the term “functionally univentricular heart”.

LA8A.2.title: Congenital anomaly of aortic valve
LA8A.2.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation where the aortic valve is abnormal.

LA8B.2.title: Congenital anomaly of aorta or its branches
LA8B.2.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the aorta and/or its branches.

LA8B.title: Congenital anomaly of great arteries including arterial duct
LA8B.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation of the great arteries (aorta, pulmonary trunk [main pulmonary artery], branch pulmonary arteries) or the arterial duct (ductus arteriosus).

LA87.4.title: Common atrioventricular junction with atrioventricular septal defect

LA8A.1.title: Congenital pulmonary atresia
LA8A.1.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is no opening between any ventricle and the pulmonary arterial tree.
exclusions: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia

LA8E.title: Congenital anomaly of atrial septum
LA8E.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is an abnormality of the atrial septum.

LA8G.title: Congenital anomaly of left atrium
LA8G.definition: A congenital cardiovascular malformation in which there is an abnormality of the left atrium.

LA90.title: Structural developmental anomalies of the peripheral vascular system
exclusions: Congenital anomaly of pulmonary arterial tree

LA90.0.title: Capillary malformations
LA90.0.definition: This is a vascular anomaly consisting of superficial and deep dilated capillaries in the skin which produce a reddish to purplish discoloration of the skin.

LA90.4.title: Peripheral arterial malformations
LA90.4.definition: This is a peripheral lesion with a direct connection between an artery and a vein, without an intervening capillary bed, but with an interposed nidus of dysplastic vascular channels in between.

LA90.1.title: Lymphatic malformations
LA90.1.definition: Lymphatic malformations (LM), formerly referred to by the term lymphangioma, are malformations of the lymphatic system which result in obstructed lymphatic drainage. There are two types of LM: macrocystic LM (including cystic hygroma/lymphangioma) and tissue-infiltrating microcystic LM (lymphangioma circumscriptum). The macro and microcystic forms of LM may occur in association.

LB03.title: Structural developmental anomalies of umbilical cord
LB03.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the umbilical cord to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LA90.3.title: Peripheral arteriovenous malformations
LA90.3.definition: This is a peripheral, abnormal connection between arteries and veins, bypassing the capillary system. This vascular anomaly is widely known because of its occurrence in the central nervous system, but can appear in any location.

LA8A.0.title: Congenital anomaly of pulmonary valve
LA8A.0.definition: A congenital malformation of the heart where the pulmonary valve is abnormal.

LB15.title: Structural developmental anomalies of small intestine
LB15.definition: Congenital gross anatomical structural defect of small intestine that results from interference with the normal growth and differentiation of the fetus, which may be inherited genetically, acquired during gestation, or inflicted during parturition.

LB12.title: Structural developmental anomalies of oesophagus
LB12.definition: Any congenital defect of oesophagus that results from interference with the normal growth and differentiation of the fetus. Such defects can arise at any stage of embryonic development, vary greatly in type and severity, and are caused by a wide variety of determining factors, including genetic mutations, chromosomal aberrations, teratogenic agents, and environmental factors. Most developmental defects are apparent at birth, especially any structural malformation, but some become evident later.

LB13.title: Structural developmental anomalies of stomach
LB13.definition: Any congenital defect of stomach that results from interference with the normal growth and differentiation of the fetus. Such defects can arise at any stage of embryonic development, vary greatly in type and severity, and are caused by a wide variety of determining factors, including genetic mutations, chromosomal aberrations, teratogenic agents, and environmental factors. Most developmental defects are apparent at birth, especially any structural malformation, but some become evident later.

LB12.1.title: Atresia of oesophagus
LB12.1.definition: Oesophageal atresia encompasses a group of congenital anomalies with an interruption in the continuity of the oesophagus, with or without persistent communication with the trachea. In 86% of cases there is a distal tracheoesophageal fistula, in 7% of cases there is no fistulous connection, while in 4% of cases there is a tracheoesophageal fistula without atresia. The remaining cases are made up of patients with OA with proximal, or both proximal and distal, tracheoesophageal fistula.

LA8C.title: Congenital anomaly of coronary artery
LA8C.definition:
A congenital cardiovascular malformation of a coronary artery. This includes absence of a coronary, anomalous origin or course, dilation or stenosis, and fistulas.

Additional information: congenital anomalies of the coronary venous system should not be included here but rather under 'Congenital anomaly of mediastinal systemic vein'.

LB17.title: Structural developmental anomalies of anal canal

LB16.title: Structural developmental anomalies of large intestine
LB16.definition: Any congenital defect of large intestine that results from interference with the normal growth and differentiation of the fetus. Such defects can arise at any stage of embryonic development, vary greatly in type and severity, and are caused by a wide variety of determining factors, including genetic mutations, chromosomal aberrations, teratogenic agents, and environmental factors. Most developmental defects are apparent at birth, especially any structural malformation, but some become evident later.

LB20.title: Structural developmental anomalies of gallbladder, bile ducts or liver
LB20.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the gallbladder, bile ducts and liver to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB20.2.title: Structural developmental anomalies of bile ducts

LB22.title: Structural developmental anomalies of spleen
LB22.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the spleen to correctly develop during the antenatal period.
exclusions: isomerism of atrial appendages (with asplenia or polysplenia)

LB30.title: Structural developmental anomalies of kidneys
LB30.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the kidneys to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB30.0.title: Renal agenesis or other reduction defects of kidney
LB30.0.definition: A series of conditions resulting in reduced kidney function including a congenital absence of both kidneys

LB40.title: Structural developmental anomalies of vulva
LB40.definition: A deformation established before birth of an anatomical structure of the vulva.

LB30.6.title: Fusion anomaly of kidneys
LB30.6.definition: The embryological, incomplete fusion of renal lobules and/or kidneys

LB31.title: Structural developmental anomalies of urinary tract
LB31.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the urinary tract to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB42.title: Structural developmental anomalies of vagina
LB42.definition: A deformation established before birth of an anatomical structure of the vagina.

LB44.title: Structural developmental anomalies of uterus, except cervix

LB45.title: Structural developmental anomalies of ovaries, fallopian tubes or broad ligaments

LB41.title: Structural developmental anomalies of clitoris
LB41.definition: A deformation established before birth of an anatomical structure of the clitoris.

LB52.title: Cryptorchidism
LB52.definition: A disorder affecting males, caused by an abnormality occurring in sex development during the antenatal period. This disorder is characterised by the absence of one or both testes from the scrotum. This disorder may also present with reduced fertility, psychological implications, or increased risk of testicular germ cell tumours. Confirmation is by imaging, karyotyping, or identification of male sex hormones in a blood sample.

LB43.title: Structural developmental anomalies of cervix uteri

LB70.0.title: Craniosynostosis
LB70.0.definition: Craniosynostosis consists of premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, resulting in an abnormal head shape. It can be divided in several subgroups; the major different types are primary vs secondary craniosynostosis and isolated vs syndromic craniosynostosis.

LB53.title: Hypospadias
LB53.definition: Any condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by a malformation of the urethra and an abnormally placed urinary meatus.

LB70.title: Structural developmental anomalies of cranium
LB70.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the cranium to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB72.title: Structural developmental anomalies of shoulder girdle
LB72.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the shoulder girdle to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB53.0.title: Hypospadias, balanic
LB53.0.definition: A condition of the urethra affecting males, caused by determinants arising during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by a malformation of the urethra and an abnormally placed urinary meatus that opens at the site of the frenulum. This condition may also present with an incomplete foreskin that forms a hood.

LB71.title: Structural developmental anomalies of facial bones
LB71.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the facial bones to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB74.title: Structural developmental anomalies of pelvic girdle
LB74.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the pelvic girdle to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB73.2.title: Structural developmental anomalies of spine
LB73.2.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the spine to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB73.1.title: Structural developmental anomalies of chest wall
LB73.1.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the chest wall to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB78.title: Polydactyly
LB78.definition: Any condition caused by development of supernumerary fingers during the antenatal period.

LB73.title: Structural developmental anomalies of spine or bony thorax
LB73.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the spine or bony thorax to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB80.title: Congenital deformities of fingers
LB80.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the fingers to develop correctly during the antenatal period.

LB75.title: Brachydactyly
LB75.definition: Brachydactyly ('short digits') is a general term that refers to disproportionately short fingers and toes, and forms part of the group of limb malformations characterised by bone dysostosis. The various types of isolated brachydactyly are rare, except for types A3 and D.

LB90.title: Joint formation defects
LB90.definition: Any condition of the skeletal system, caused by failure of joints to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LB79.title: Syndactyly
LB79.definition: A condition caused by failure of the longitudinal interdigital necrosis that normally separates the digits during the antenatal period. This condition is characterised by the presence of two or more digits that are fused together.

LB98.2.title: Congenital valgus deformities of feet
LB98.2.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the bones of the foot to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by twisting of parts of the foot outward from the centre of the body.

LB93.title: Congenital knee dislocation
LB93.definition: A condition characterised by hyperextension of the knee joint.

LB97.title: Limb overgrowth
LB97.definition: Disproportionately long or asymmetric upper limbs

LC50.title: Developmental capillary vascular malformations of the skin
synonyms: Developmental capillary vascular malformations of the skin

LB98.0.title: Congenital varus deformities of feet
LB98.0.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the bones of the foot to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by twisting of parts of the foot inward from the centre of the body.

LB98.title: Congenital deformities of feet
LB98.definition: Any condition caused by malformation of the foot during the antenatal period.

LD20.title: Syndromes with central nervous system anomalies as a major feature

LB99.title: Reduction defects of upper limb
LB99.definition: Any condition caused by the failure of an upper limb to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by reduction in size or absence of the limb.

LB9A.title: Reduction defects of lower limb
LB9A.definition: Any condition caused by the failure of a lower limb to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These conditions are characterised by reduction in size or absence of the limb.

LC00.title: Keratinocytic epidermal hamartoma
LC00.definition: Keratinocytic epidermal hamartoma or epidermal naevus is a congenital hamartomatous epidermal malformation composed of keratinocytes. It is thought to arise as a result of somatic mutation: early embryonic mutations can give rise to extensive systematised naevi, though typically epidermal naevi are localised linear papillomatous or verrucous plaques. Histologically they exhibit acanthosis, papillomatosis and acanthosis.

LB96.title: Congenital bowing of long bones
LB96.definition: Congenital bowing of long bones is a congenital condition described by the presence of symmetric or asymmetric angular deformity and shortening of the long bones, particularly the femurs, tibiae and ulnae.

LD24.title: Syndromes with skeletal anomalies as a major feature

LD20.0.title: Syndromes with cerebellar anomalies as a major feature

LD24.1.title: Bone diseases with increased bone density

LD21.title: Syndromes with eye anomalies as a major feature
LD21.definition: Any syndrome caused by failure of one or both eyes to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LD24.G.title: Syndromic craniosynostoses
LD24.G.definition: Any syndrome caused by premature fusing of sections of the infant skull. These syndromes are characterised by disfiguring compensatory growth of the skull. These syndromes may also present with frequent worsening morning headache, recurrent vomiting, cephalocranial disproportion, raised intracranial pressure, optic atrophy, blindness, or developmental delay.

LD24.0.title: Syndromes with micromelia
LD24.0.definition: Syndromes in which abnormally short limbs are a major feature

LD24.2.title: Bone diseases with disorganised development of skeletal components

LD24.J.title: Patellar dysostoses
LD24.J.definition: Any syndrome characterised by malformation of the patella during the antenatal period.

LD25.title: Syndromes with face or limb anomalies as a major feature

LD25.0.title: Oromandibular-limb anomaly syndrome
LD25.0.definition: A syndrome caused by failure of the face and limbs to correctly develop during the antenatal period. This syndrome is characterised by malformations of the tongue, mandible, and limbs.
exclusions: Ectrodactyly - ectodermal dysplasia - cleft lip or palate

LD24.K.title: Genetic bone diseases with decreased bone density

LD26.4.title: Arthrogryposis syndromes
LD26.4.definition: Any syndrome caused by failure of elastic tissue to correctly develop during the antenatal period. These syndromes are characterised by the presence of multiple joint contractures, where elastic tissues are replaced by inelastic tissues, which results in fixation of the joint.

LD26.title: Syndromes with limb anomalies as a major feature

LD27.title: Syndromes with skin or mucosal anomalies as a major feature

LD28.title: Syndromes with connective tissue involvement as a major feature

LD27.6.title: Genetic lipodystrophy
LD27.6.definition: Genetic lipodystrophies represent a heterogeneous group of rare diseases characterised by a generalised or localised loss of body fat (lipoatrophy).

LD27.0.title: Ectodermal dysplasia syndromes
LD27.0.definition: Ectodermal dysplasias (EDs) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterised by developmental dystrophies of ectodermal structures, such as hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis, onychodysplasia and hypodontia or anodontia. More than 160 clinically and genetically distinct hereditary ectodermal dysplasias have been catalogued.

LD2A.title: Malformative disorders of sex development
LD2A.definition: Any condition caused by failure of the genitals to correctly develop during the antenatal period.

LD28.1.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
LD28.1.definition: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) is a heterogeneous group of inherited disorders of connective tissue, principally collagen, that range in severity from mild joint hypermobility to life-threatening fragility of soft tissue and vasculature.

LD2F.1.title: Syndromes with multiple structural anomalies, not of environmental origin

LD2D.1.title: Neurofibromatoses
LD2D.1.definition: The neurofibromatoses (NF) are related genetic disorders which affect bone, soft tissue, skin and nervous system. In NF type 1 neurofibromas develop in the skin and elsewhere: these can cause problems as a result of their visibility in the skin, compression of vital internal structures or from malignant degeneration. Neuromas of the acoustic nerve are the predominant problem in NF type 2.

LD40.title: Complete trisomies of the autosomes
LD40.definition: Any disease caused by the presence of one extra autosome, for a total of three. Confirmation is through observation of a supernumerary autosome by karyotyping.

LD2F.title: Syndromes with multiple structural anomalies, without predominant body system involvement

LD42.title: Polyploidies
LD42.definition: Any disease caused by one or more additional sets of chromosomes. Non-mosaic versions of these diseases are characterised by gross fetal malformation or death of the fetus. Confirmation is through observation of supernumerary sets of chromosomes by karyotyping.

LD45.title: Uniparental disomies
LD45.definition: Any disease caused by the inheritance of two homologous copies of a chromosome from one parent, and none from the other parent. Confirmation is by observation of identical chromosomes pairs by genetic testing.

LD50.0.title: Turner syndrome
LD50.0.definition: Karyotype missing one X chromosome (45,X0 or 45,X0/46,XX mosaicism); gonads: ovaries (streak); phenotype female with short stature, amenorrhea (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism), absence of sexual development, webbed neck, low set ears, posterior hairline, widely-spaced nipples, short fourth metacarpals, and increased carrying angle at the elbow (cubitus valgus). Often associated with renal, cardiac and ocular abnormalities.

LD47.title: Balanced rearrangements or structural rearrangements
LD47.definition: A condition caused by translocation or other structural rearrangement of genomic material between chromosomes demonstrating no net gain or loss of genomic material, in an individual displaying no phenotype. Confirmation is through observation of a balanced event by genetic testing.

LD50.3.title: Klinefelter syndrome
LD50.3.definition: Klinefelter syndrome defines a group of chromosomal disorders in which there is at least one extra X chromosome compared with the normal 46,XY male karyotype. The effects on physical features and on physical and cognitive development increase with the number of extra X's, and each extra X is associated with an intelligence quotient (IQ) decrease of approximately 15-16 points, with language most affected, particularly expressive language skills.

LD56.title: Chimaera 46, XX, 46, XY
LD56.definition: A disease caused by XX and XY embryonic fusion or two distinct loss events of a sex chromosome from an XXY embryo early in development. This results in a subset of cells in the body having an XX karyotype, while other cells demonstrate an XY karyotype. This disease may present with abnormal genital development.
